info.title: mailcow REST API v2
info.description:
mailcow REST API v2 runs next to the legacy mailcow UI and `/api/v1`, which keep working
unchanged. It is the only backend of the mailcowui-ng web app. This document is the source of
truth: the implementation mirrors it exactly, and undocumented behaviour is a bug.

## Conventions

- Names are camelCase. Booleans are `true`/`false`. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC.
- A single resource is returned as `{"data": {...}}`. A list is returned as
  `{"data": [...], "meta": {"total", "limit", "offset"}}` and accepts `limit` (default 25, at
  most 1,000), `offset`, `sort`, `order`, a substring search `q` and the documented filters.
- Create returns `201` with a `Location` header, read and update return `200`, delete returns
  `204`. Non-CRUD actions are sub-resources (for example `POST /api-keys/{apiKeyId}/revocation`)
  and return `200` with the affected resource or the ceremony data.
- `PATCH` takes JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396, `application/merge-patch+json`).
- Operations with JSON request bodies require a JSON `Content-Type` for every non-empty
  body. A non-JSON or missing content type answers `415` before field validation or resource
  changes. Raw uploads use the media types documented by their operation.
- Mutable resources carry a version tag: a strong ETag over their stored settings, never over
  usage data. A single read returns it in the `ETag` header, and every representation,
  including each list entry, carries the same value in `etag`. Writes accept `If-Match` and
  answer `412` when it does not match. The legacy UI edits the same rows, so clients should
  send it.

## Errors

Every error is an RFC 9457 problem (`application/problem+json`) with `type`, `title`,
`status`, `detail` and `requestId`. Problem types that clients act on are relative URI
references of the form `/api/v2/problems/{name}`, documented in `docs/problems.md` and served
as HTML by `GET /problems/{problemType}`. Compare `type` as an exact string. Other problems
use `about:blank` and are identified by their status (`400` malformed request, `404` unknown
resource or path, `405` method not allowed, `409` conflict described in `detail`, `412`
precondition failed, `415` unsupported request body media type, `500` unexpected failure).

Errors are never localised: the API ignores `Accept-Language`. `title` and `detail` are
English and meant for logs and scripts. A validation problem (`422`) carries an `errors` map
from each invalid field to a list of violations, each with a stable rule `code` and its
`params`, so that clients build translated messages themselves.

## Authentication

**Browser clients** use a same-origin session cookie (`sessionCookie`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`,
`SameSite=Strict`). Every state-changing request made with a session, including sign-in, must
carry the session's anti-forgery token in the `X-CSRF-Token` header (`csrfToken`), whatever
its content type. The flow is:

1. `GET /csrf-token` starts an anonymous session and returns its token. The token stays valid
   for the lifetime of the session, including across sign-in. A `403` with type
   `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch` means the session ended or its identity changed (the
   token is renewed when an impersonation starts or ends). Fetch a new token and re-read
   `GET /me`. Retry the write once only if the identity is unchanged; otherwise discard it, so
   that a write prepared under one identity is never sent under another.
2. Sign in with a passkey (`POST /session/passkey-challenge`, then
   `POST /session/passkey-assertion`) or with a password (`POST /session`).
3. If the password step answers with state `pendingSecondFactor`, complete one of the listed
   methods (`POST /session/pending-sign-in/second-factor`, after
   `POST /session/pending-sign-in/webauthn-challenge` for WebAuthn) or cancel it
   (`DELETE /session/pending-sign-in`).
4. Sign out with `DELETE /session`.

**Automation clients** send an API key in the `X-API-Key` header (`apiKeyAuth`). A request
with a key never creates a session and needs no anti-forgery token. When a request carries
both a key and a session cookie, the key decides and the cookie is ignored. Any request that
carries a non-empty `X-API-Key` header is authenticated by that key, and an invalid, expired
or revoked key, or a key used from a disallowed address, is reported to mailcow's fail2ban.
The System operations (health checks, the contract, the documentation and the problem pages)
ignore `X-API-Key`.

## Recommended presentation of sign-in methods

Clients should offer **passkey sign-in first** whenever the device supports WebAuthn
(`PublicKeyCredential` is available), and username and password second. Passkeys registered
in the legacy UI under the names "FIDO2" or "Touch ID" are ordinary passkeys and need no
special handling. In the second-factor step, `PendingSignIn.methods` is already in the
recommended order: WebAuthn security keys and passkeys first, TOTP second, Yubico OTP last.
Methods with `tier: primary` are offered directly; methods with `tier: advanced` belong behind
an "other methods" option.

## Restricted sessions

When mailcow forces an account to change its password or to set up a second factor, the
session is restricted (`state: restricted`, non-empty `pendingActions`). It can read
`GET /me` and `GET /capabilities/self-service` and sign out. While `passwordChange` is
pending it can read `GET /me/password-policy` and change the password (`PUT /me/password`);
while `secondFactorSetup` is pending it can list and enrol second factors
(`/me/second-factors`) and, when that is the only pending action, register a passkey.
Operations that need no signed-in account stay available: `GET /csrf-token`, `GET /session`,
sign-in and its steps, the public configuration, the documentation and the health checks.
Every other operation answers `403` with type `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required`.
API keys are never restricted: `Identity.pendingActions` is empty for them. Pending actions are re-evaluated from mailcow's
data on every request, so a restriction lifts as soon as it is resolved in either UI.

Aliases and catch-all aliases, copies over alias domains, bulk actions, and the capabilities
of aliases, alias domains, resources and sender settings.

tags.name: Resources

tags.name: Mailbox templates
tags.description: Templates whose values pre-fill new mailboxes, and their bulk deletion.

tags.name: Password policy
tags.description: The password rules applied whenever a password is set.

tags.name: DKIM
tags.description: DKIM signing keys of domains and alias domains, their DNS records, private key export and the FeldHost ISPConfig DNS publication.

tags.name: MTA-STS
tags.description: MTA-STS policies of domains, published for the domain and its alias domains.

tags.name: DNS diagnostics
tags.description: DNS checks of a domain or alias domain against the server's configuration, with a zone file.

tags.name: Identity provider
tags.description:
The server's external identity provider: Keycloak, a generic OpenID Connect provider or an
LDAP directory, with attribute mapping, mailbox creation on first sign-in, synchronisation
settings and connection tests. Single sign-on and provider password sign-in are part of
Authentication.

tags.name: OAuth2 clients
Administrators
tags.description:
Administrator accounts (feature 007) and the account capabilities. Administrator accounts
are written only in a signed-in administrator session; keys owned by administrators may
list and inspect them. The server always keeps at least one active administrator.

tags.name: Domain administrators
tags.description:
Domain administrator accounts with their domains and the 19 permission flags (feature 007).
Managed by administrators, also with a read-write administrator key.

tags.name: Single sign-on tokens
tags.description:
Short-lived, single-use tokens with which a domain administrator signs in without a password
(feature 007), shared with the legacy domain administrator login.

tags.name: Impersonation
tags.description:
Login-as (legacy "dual login"): administrators, and domain administrators with the `loginAs`
flag, act as another account and return to their own; webmail sign-in on a user's behalf
(feature 007). Every audit record written during an impersonation names both accounts.

tags.name: Host and installation
tags.description:
System overview, mail storage usage, public addresses, installed version, update status and
monitoring capabilities (feature 011). Administrators only. Live data carries its collection
time; poll every 5 seconds while visible, there is no push channel.

tags.name: Containers
tags.description:
mailcow's service containers: states, resource usage, start, stop and restart (feature 011).
Stop and restart are destructive: clients confirm and name the container.

tags.name: Logs
tags.description:
Every log mailcow keeps, with server-side paging, filters and search; secrets in legacy logs
are masked (feature 011). Administrators only.

tags.name: Rspamd
tags.description: Rspamd's scan history and statistics (feature 011). Administrators only.

tags.name: Mail queue
tags.description:
The Postfix mail queue: listing, message content (audited), deliver now, hold, release,
delete, flush and delete all (feature 011). Deletions are destructive and irreversible.

tags.name: Fail2ban
tags.description:
mailcow's ban service (legacy "Fail2ban"): settings, allowlist and denylist, rules, active and
permanent bans, and the public ban list ID (feature 011).

tags.name: Relayhosts
tags.description:
Relayhosts (legacy "sender-dependent transports"): SMTP servers through which mailcow sends the
outbound mail of selected domains and mailboxes, with write-only credentials, usage, choices
for selectors and a connection test (feature 009).

tags.name: Relayhost assignments
tags.description:
The relayhost a domain or a mailbox sends through, read and replaced on its own, with the
effective relayhost of a mailbox (feature 009).

tags.name: Transports
tags.description:
Transport maps: mail for selected recipients routed to a next hop, with credentials shared per
next hop and a connection test (feature 009).

tags.name: BCC maps
tags.description:
Silent copies of mail sent by or to a domain, alias domain, mailbox or alias, and the local
destination choices (feature 009).

tags.name: Recipient maps
tags.description: Envelope recipient rewriting before delivery (feature 009).

tags.name: TLS policy maps
tags.description: Outbound TLS policy overrides per destination (feature 009).

tags.name: Forwarding hosts
tags.description:
Servers that forward mail to mailcow and are accepted without blocklist checks, greylisting or
spam rejection, stored in mailcow's Redis (feature 009).

tags.name: Routing capabilities
tags.description: Server settings and limits for routing clients (feature 009).

tags.name: Quarantine
tags.description:
Quarantine items and their release, learning, deletion and downloads, bulk actions, the
quarantine settings with template preview, the quarantine capabilities and the quarantine
notification settings of mailboxes (feature 006).

tags.name: Spam policy
tags.description:
Allow and block lists of domains, alias domains and mailboxes, mailbox spam scores and the
spam filter's action statistics (feature 006).

tags.name: Rate limits
tags.description: Sending rate limits of domains, alias domains and mailboxes, and bucket resets (feature 006).

tags.name: Branding settings
tags.description: Logos, UI texts, login page options, app links, brand colours and the IP check opt-in (feature 013).

tags.name: Password settings
tags.description: The password reset notification (feature 013). The password policy change is under "Password policy".

tags.name: Quota notification settings
tags.description: The quota notification e-mail and each domain's copy recipients (feature 013).

tags.name: Rspamd settings
tags.description:
Rspamd settings rules, the global regex maps, the effective settings map and the Rspamd web
interface password (feature 013).

tags.name: Global filters
tags.description: The global Sieve pre-filter and post-filter that Dovecot applies to every mailbox (feature 013).

tags.name: Presets
tags.description: The Rspamd and Sieve examples mailcow ships (feature 013).

tags.name: Server settings
tags.description: The settings capabilities and the CORS settings of the legacy API (feature 013).

tags.name: Mass mail
tags.description: Recipient previews and background mass mail jobs delivered into the mailboxes (feature 013).

tags.name: License
tags.description: The server's GUID and its verification against mailcow's license service (feature 013).

tags.name: Self-service
tags.description: Server settings and limits for the self-service operations, partly readable before sign-in (feature 005).

tags.name: Own account
tags.description:
The signed-in account's own password (including a forced change), second factors (including
a forced setup) and, for mailbox users, recovery address, mailbox overview, webmail hand-off,
Apple connection profile and client configuration (feature 005). Sessions only.

tags.name: Password reset
tags.description: Forgotten-password reset through the mailbox's recovery address, shared with the legacy reset page (feature 005).

tags.name: Mailbox self-service
tags.description:
App passwords, temporary aliases, push notifications, mail settings, recent logins and
groupware resets of the mailboxes in the caller's scope (feature 005).

tags.name: Sieve filters
tags.description: Administrator-managed prefilters and postfilters of mailboxes, and the user's active Sieve script (feature 005).

get.description:
Returns the anti-forgery token of the caller's session and starts an anonymous session (sets
the session cookie) when there is none. Call it once when the web app starts and after a
`csrf-token-mismatch` problem. The token stays valid until the session ends, including
across sign-in.

Returns the state of the caller's browser session: `anonymous`, `pendingSecondFactor` (with
the methods to offer), `restricted` (with the pending actions) or `active`. Never fails for a
missing or ended session; it reports `anonymous` instead. Requests with an API key are refused
with `session-required`.

post.summary: Sign in with username and password
post.description:
Verifies an existing mailcow username and password, for every role, with every password hash
format mailcow accepts. Signing in never modifies the stored hash.

- Without an active second factor the session becomes `active`, or `restricted` when mailcow
  forces a password change or second-factor setup. All of the account's second-factor entries
  are re-activated (legacy "disable second factor for the next login").
- With active second factors the session becomes `pendingSecondFactor` and lists the methods
  in the recommended order. Complete one within 5 minutes.
- A mailbox user's password verification records a recent-login entry (mailcow `sasl_log`),
  as legacy does.

Failures return one generic `sign-in-failed` error, are audited and are published to mailcow's
fail2ban channel as `mailcow UI: Invalid password for <username> by <client address>` (not for
mailboxes that authenticate against an external identity provider). Each failure for the same
username and client address is answered 0.5 s later than the previous one; after 10 failures
within 15 minutes attempts are refused with `429` without checking the password. A correct
password resets the count. Failed second factors have their own count per username and client
address, which a correct password does not reset: after 10 of them within 15 minutes the
password step is refused with `429` as well, until a sign-in completes or the window ends.

The session identifier is renewed when the step succeeds. A previous sign-in of the same
session is replaced.

**Identity provider mailboxes** (feature 012): a mailbox with the LDAP source is verified by a
bind to the directory, and a mailbox with the Keycloak source, when the mailpassword flow is
on, against the hash in the user's `mailcow_password` attribute. When no account matches and
LDAP, or Keycloak with the mailpassword flow, is configured, the username and password are
verified at the provider and a mailbox is created from the mapped or default template. Second
factors, forced second-factor setup, throttling and fail2ban reporting then work as for a
mailcow password; `authMethod` is `directoryPassword*` or `providerPassword*`. A provider that
cannot be reached, times out or refuses the service account answers `503
identity-provider-unavailable`, which is neither reported to fail2ban nor counted towards
throttling. A verified password for which no mailbox can be created, a Keycloak user without a
`mailcow_password` value, and a mailbox of a generic OIDC provider get `sign-in-failed`
without a fail2ban report.

delete.description:
Ends the session immediately in any state, including a pending sign-in, and audits the
sign-out of a signed-in account. Any further request with the old cookie is anonymous; fetch a
new anti-forgery token before signing in again. Without a live session the request succeeds
and changes nothing, and no anti-forgery token is needed.

Cancels a sign-in that awaits a second factor. The session returns to `anonymous` and keeps
its anti-forgery token. Succeeds and changes nothing when no sign-in is pending.

post.summary: Get a WebAuthn challenge for the pending sign-in
post.description:
Issues a single-use WebAuthn challenge, bound to the pending sign-in, that allows the
account's active WebAuthn second factors. It expires after 5 minutes or at the first
verification attempt. A new request replaces the previous challenge. User verification
follows mailcow's `WEBAUTHN_UV_FLAG_LOGIN`, and `extensions.appid` is set as in legacy.

post.summary: Complete the pending sign-in with a second factor
post.description:
Verifies one of the pending sign-in's methods: a TOTP code, a WebAuthn assertion or a Yubico
OTP. Second factors enrolled in the legacy UI verify without re-enrolment.

On success the session identifier is renewed, the session becomes `active` (or `restricted`)
and the sign-in is audited with `authMethod: passwordAndSecondFactor`.

One failed attempt cancels the pending sign-in (`second-factor-failed`), counts towards the
second-factor throttling of the username and client address, and is audited. That count is
not reset by a correct password, only by a completed sign-in: after 10 failures within 15
minutes, password steps and second-factor steps of the pair answer `429` without checking
credentials, and each failure is answered 0.5 s later than the previous one. A method that was
deactivated or deleted since the password step also cancels it. A TOTP code is accepted only
once within its validity window. When the Yubico service is unreachable the answer is `503`,
the pending sign-in stays open and nothing is counted. A malformed request (`422`) changes
nothing.

Issues a single-use challenge for usernameless passkey sign-in, bound to the session, with
an empty `allowCredentials` list so that the device offers its discoverable credentials for
this host. It expires after 5 minutes or at the first sign-in attempt. A new request replaces
the previous challenge. User verification follows mailcow's `FIDO2_UV_FLAG_LOGIN` (default
`preferred`).

Verifies an assertion for the session's passkey challenge and signs in the account that owns
the credential, with no password and no further second factor. Passkeys registered in the
legacy UI ("FIDO2", "Touch ID") work unchanged.

The credential must be active and its account must be able to sign in (active account, active
mailbox and domain, not a resource mailbox). Without `role`, the account type is resolved in
mailcow's order (administrator or domain administrator, then mailbox user); with `role`, an
account of another type fails. Forced password change and second-factor setup restrict the
session as after a password sign-in. A mailbox user's sign-in records a recent-login entry.

Failures return the generic `sign-in-failed` error, are audited and count towards throttling
per client address. They are not reported to fail2ban. The session identifier is renewed on
success.

get.description:
Returns the authenticated caller: username, role, how it authenticated, scope, effective
permission flags, pending actions and, for sessions, the preferences. For an API key it
returns the owner's role, scope and flags together with the key's identifier, name and access
level. Available in restricted sessions.
Returns the signed-in user's language and theme. Not available to API keys.

patch.description:
Changes the signed-in user's language (one of the enabled languages) and/or theme. The change
persists across sessions and devices and is audited. Not available to API keys.

get.description:
Lists the signed-in user's passkeys, including those registered in the legacy UI as "FIDO2"
or "Touch ID" credentials. `q` searches the name and the authenticator description. Not
available to API keys or in restricted sessions.

post.description:
Verifies the authenticator's response to the session's registration options and saves the
passkey where legacy mailcow stores FIDO2 credentials, bound to this host name, so that it
works for usernameless sign-in in both UIs. User verification and accepted attestation formats
follow mailcow's `FIDO2_UV_FLAG_REGISTER` and `FIDO2_FORMATS`. The registration is audited.

Needs a full session, or a session restricted only by `secondFactorSetup`, which the
registration lifts immediately. Not available to API keys or during a pending sign-in.

Issues single-use registration options bound to the session: a discoverable credential
(`residentKey: required`) for this host name, with the account's existing passkeys excluded.
They expire after 5 minutes or at the first registration attempt. A new request replaces the
previous options. Same access rules as `registerPasskey`.

patch.description: Changes the display name. Audited.

delete.description:
Removes the passkey from mailcow, so it no longer signs in through either UI. Removing the
last passkey is allowed, as in legacy. Audited.

get.description:
Lists API keys, including revoked and expired ones. Administrators only: a signed-in
administrator or a key owned by an administrator. Secrets are never included. `q` searches
the name, the prefix and the owner's username.

parameters.name: ownerUsername
parameters.description: Only keys owned by this account (exact match).

post.description:
Creates a key owned by an existing administrator or domain administrator, with an access
level, an optional expiry in the future and optional allowed source networks. The response
contains the secret exactly once; only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Audited without the
secret.

Only a signed-in administrator may create keys. Requests authenticated by a key are refused
with `session-required`, so that a leaked key cannot mint replacements for itself.

get.description:
Lists the active administrators and active domain administrators that can own an API key
(mailcow's `admin` table with `active = 1`), for the owner field of the key form. Mailbox users
are never listed. Administrators only: a signed-in administrator or a key owned by an
administrator, read-only keys included.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: Only this role.

get.description:
Returns one key with its owner, access level, networks, expiry, creation, last use (accurate
to the minute), status and revocation. Administrators only, as for `listApiKeys`.

post.description:
Revokes the key. It is refused from the very next request, stays listed with its revocation
time and the revoking administrator, and cannot be restored. Audited. Revoking an already
revoked key succeeds and changes nothing; this check comes before `If-Match`, so a retried
revocation never answers `412`.

Only a signed-in administrator may revoke keys; requests authenticated by a key are refused
with `session-required`.

get.description:
Returns the branding, login page options and languages configured in mailcow's legacy UI.
No authentication is needed. Values are read from mailcow on every request, so a change saved
in the legacy UI is visible immediately; clients revalidate with `If-None-Match`.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: `ETag` of a cached representation.

get.description:
Returns the logo uploaded in the legacy UI. `404` when none is uploaded for this variant; the
public configuration then points to the default logo instead.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: Version from `Logo.url`. With a matching version the response is cacheable for a year.

get.description:
Lists audit records, newest first by default. Administrators only: a signed-in administrator
or a key owned by an administrator. Records cannot be changed or deleted through the API and
are removed after the configured retention period (365 days by default). `q` searches the
actor username, the target name and the user agent.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only records at or after this time.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only records before this time.

parameters.name: eventType
parameters.description:
Only these event types. Repeat the parameter for several. A type this server does not
record (for example one of a feature it does not implement yet) matches no records.

parameters.name: authMethod
parameters.description:
Only records of these authentication methods. Repeat the parameter for several. Records
without a method (`authMethod: null`) never match. A method this server does not record
matches no records.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description:
Only records written while handling the request with this identifier (the `requestId` of
its problem details and log lines, its W3C trace ID), so that the records of one request,
for example one bulk action, can be linked.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: Only records whose actor username (including attempted usernames) or API key ID equals this value.

parameters.name: clientAddress
parameters.description: Only records from this IPv4 or IPv6 address, or from within this prefix.

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: Only records whose target is of this type.

parameters.name: targetId
parameters.description:
Only records whose target identifier equals this value. Domain names (targets `domain`,
`domainFooter` and `mtaStsPolicy`) may be given in ASCII or Unicode form and any letter case.
DKIM keys (`dkimKey`) match in that normalised form and, for an unused key that legacy stored
under another spelling, also by that exact spelling. Without `targetType`, a domain name
matches the records of the domain and of its footer.

parameters.name: impersonatedAccount
parameters.description:
Feature 007: only records written while this account (a mailbox address or a domain
administrator's username, exact match after lower-casing) was impersonated, including the
starts and ends of its impersonations.

get.summary: Redirect the base path to the API documentation
get.description:
Redirects `/api/v2/` to `GET /docs`, the interactive documentation, so that a browser opening
the base path lands on a page. The `Location` is relative, keeping the scheme and host the
client used. Ignores `X-API-Key`.

302.description: Found. The documentation page is at the `Location` address.

Location.description: Always `/api/v2/docs`.

get.description: Answers `200` while the PHP runtime serves requests. Checks no dependency and ignores `X-API-Key`.

Checks the MariaDB connection, the mailcow schema version (`versions.db_schema` must be one
this release supports), the Redis connection and that this API's own migrations are applied.
Ignores `X-API-Key`.
Returns the bundled OpenAPI document of the running release. Ignores `X-API-Key`.
HTML page that renders `GET /openapi.yaml`. All assets are served by the API itself. Ignores `X-API-Key`.

Human-readable documentation of a problem type, so that every documented `type` URI
dereferences on each installation. Rendered from `docs/problems.md`. Ignores `X-API-Key`.

200.description: The documentation of this problem type.

get.description:
Lists the sync jobs in the caller's scope, by default sorted by `id`. An administrator sees
every job whose target mailbox exists, a domain administrator the jobs of mailboxes in the
domains they manage, and a mailbox user the jobs that sync into their own mailbox. Each entry
carries its version tag and run status, but not the log (`GET /sync-jobs/{syncJobId}/log`).
The remote password is never included.

`q` searches the target mailbox, the remote user and the remote host. Filters narrow the
result within the caller's scope; a filter value outside the scope simply matches nothing.

Requires the sync-jobs permission (`permissions.syncjobs` of `GET /me`): administrators always
hold it, domain administrators and mailbox users only when their `syncjobs` flag is set.
Callers without it get `403` with type `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required` and
`requiredFlags: [syncjobs]`.

parameters.name: mailbox
parameters.description: Only jobs that sync into this mailbox (exact address, case-insensitive).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only jobs whose target mailbox belongs to this domain (exact name, case-insensitive).

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) jobs.

parameters.name: running
parameters.description: Only jobs with (`true`) or without (`false`) a run in progress.

parameters.name: lastResult
parameters.description: Only jobs whose last result is this value.

post.description:
Creates a sync job that pulls mail from a remote IMAP account into a local mailbox.
Administrators and domain administrators name the target `mailbox`; a mailbox user's job always
syncs into their own mailbox. Omitted options take the legacy form's defaults (see
`SyncJobCreateRequest` and `GET /capabilities/sync-jobs`). The remote password is stored for
the runner and never returned. Audited without the password.

This API never starts a run. An active job runs on the imapsync runner's own schedule: every
minute on the master node, mailcow's dovecot container runs each active job that is not
running and whose interval has elapsed since its last run (or that never ran).

Refusals:
- `403 permission-flag-required` (`requiredFlags: [syncjobs]`): the caller lacks the sync-jobs permission; `403 insufficient-key-scope`: a
  read-only key.
- `404`: the target mailbox does not exist or lies outside the caller's scope (also when a
  mailbox user names another mailbox).
- `409 sync-job-exists`: a job for the same mailbox, remote user and remote host exists.
- `422 validation-failed`: invalid members, all named at once; nothing is stored.

administrator.summary: An administrator choosing the target and options

get.description:
Returns what a client needs before it submits a sync job, as configured on this server for the
caller: whether custom imapsync parameters are allowed for the caller and the allow-list in
effect (never containing `showpasswords`), the bulk limit, the page sizes, every field's limits,
the allowed encryption values and the creation defaults. Changes nothing; read-only keys may use
it. Requires the sync-jobs permission (`403 permission-flag-required`,
`requiredFlags: [syncjobs]`, otherwise).

post.summary: Apply an action to several sync jobs
post.description:
Activates, deactivates, reschedules or deletes up to the bulk limit (default 100) of sync jobs
in one request, as the legacy mass actions do. Creation and other edits are single-job
requests.

The whole request is refused only when the caller may never perform the action: `403
permission-flag-required` (`requiredFlags: [syncjobs]`) without the sync-jobs permission, `403 insufficient-key-scope` for a read-only key,
and `422` for a malformed body or more targets than the bulk limit. Otherwise each job is checked,
processed and audited on its own, as a single request for it would be, and gets one result in
request order:

- `done`: the action was applied. `version` carries the job's new version tag exactly as its
  `ETag` header and `etag` member show it (quoted), except after `delete`; a target's `version`
  accepts it with or without the quotes. Activating an active job or deactivating an inactive
  one is `done` and changes nothing.
- `notFound`: the job does not exist or its mailbox lies outside the caller's scope.
- `outdated`: the target's `version` no longer matches; the job is unchanged. Not checked for
  `reschedule`, and not checked for targets without `version`.
- `refused` or `failed`: the result's `problem` explains why.

A failure on one job never stops or undoes the others. A job named twice is processed and
reported once. Every audit record of the request carries `bulkRequestId`.

get.description:
Returns the job's full configuration, its version tag and its run status. The remote password
is never included; `remotePasswordSet` says whether one is stored. Requires the sync-jobs
permission (`403 permission-flag-required`, `requiredFlags: [syncjobs]`, otherwise). A job outside the caller's scope answers `404`.

patch.summary: Change, activate or deactivate a sync job
patch.description:
Changes the sent members only (JSON Merge Patch); every other member, including the stored
remote password, keeps its value. Activating and deactivating are changes of `active`. A change
takes effect from the runner's next cycle and never interrupts a run in progress. The target
`mailbox` cannot change (`immutable`). Audited with each changed attribute's old and new value;
the password is recorded only as changed.

Interactive clients should always send the version tag they read in `If-Match`: the legacy UI
and `/api/v1` edit the same rows, and an outdated tag answers `412` without changing anything.

Refusals: `403` (no sync-jobs permission, or a read-only key), `404` (unknown or out of scope),
`412` (outdated `If-Match`), `422` (invalid members, all named at once), `409 sync-job-exists`
(the new remote user and host duplicate another job of the same mailbox).

delete.description:
Deletes the job at once, so the runner no longer selects it. A run in progress is not
interrupted, and its final status write for the deleted job has no effect. Audited.

Interactive clients should send the version tag they read in `If-Match`; an outdated tag
answers `412` and deletes nothing. Refusals: `403` (no sync-jobs permission, or a read-only
key), `404` (unknown or out of scope), `412`.

get.summary: Get the run log of a sync job
get.description:
Returns the output of the job's last imapsync run, as the runner stored it, together with the
current run status. The log is produced by the remote server and by imapsync; the runner masks
passwords in it, and because this API refuses the `showpasswords` option the remote password
does not appear. Render it as plain text. It may be empty, and it can be several megabytes
long. Anyone who may read the job may read its log; reads are not audited.

post.description:
Clears the job's last run time and last result (legacy "Schedule next"), so the imapsync runner
selects it on its next cycle if it is active and not running. This API never starts a run
itself. A run in progress is not interrupted: it finishes, writes its own status, and the next
cycle runs the job again.

Rescheduling changes only the run status, so it neither requires nor checks `If-Match` and does
not change the version tag. Audited. Refusals: `403` (no sync-jobs permission, or a read-only
key), `404` (unknown or out of scope), and `422` (unsafe stored custom parameters).

get.description:
Lists the domains in the caller's scope, as the legacy "Mail setup › Domains" screen shows
them: each entry is the full domain with its usage figures and its version tag, so the list
needs no request per row. Administrators see every domain; domain administrators see the
domains assigned to them through an active assignment, whether or not the domain is active,
and never `domainAdmins`. Mailbox users are refused with `403 forbidden`.

`q` searches, case-insensitively and as a substring, the ASCII name, the readable (Unicode)
name, the description and the tags.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) domains.

parameters.name: backupMx
parameters.description: Only domains with (`true`) or without (`false`) "relay this domain".

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description:
Only domains that carry any of these tags, matched as whole tags without regard to letter
case. Repeat the parameter for several tags. Use `q` for substring matching.

post.description:
Creates a domain, pre-filled from a domain template (the Default template unless `templateId`
names another). Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key.

The domain row, its tags and its entry in mailcow's domain map (Redis `DOMAIN_MAP`) are stored
together or not at all; external sender addresses in the new domain that were granted to
mailboxes are removed, because the domain is now local. Then the follow-up steps run, each
reported in `data.creationReport` and in the audit record, none undoing the creation:
1. the initial rate limit, when the request or the template sets one;
2. a DKIM key with the selector and key size of the request, the template or the built-in
   defaults, unless a key already exists for the name or the selector is explicitly empty;
   when the DKIM DNS publication is enabled (FeldHost setting), the public key is published to
   the ISPConfig DNS server;
3. the groupware restart, when `restartGroupware` is `true`.

Like legacy, a creation does not rebuild the groupware directory or flush its cache: the new
domain has no mailboxes yet.

When mailcow's shared store is unavailable, the creation is refused with `503
temporary-failure` and nothing is stored. Concurrent creations of the same name: exactly one
succeeds.

post.summary: Apply an action to several domains
post.description:
Activates, deactivates or deletes up to 100 domains in one request, as the legacy mass actions
do. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write
key; any other caller is refused as a whole (`403`). More than 100 targets are refused as a
whole (`422`, `tooMany` on `targets`, with `max: 100`).

Otherwise each distinct domain is processed on its own, with the checks, side effects and
audit record of the single operation, and gets one result in request order:
- `done`: applied, with the new version tag for activations and deactivations;
- `notFound`: the domain does not exist (or the name is not a valid domain name);
- `refused`: for example `domain-not-empty` for a deletion;
- `outdated`: the target's `version` no longer matches (`412` problem); the domain is unchanged;
- `failed`: an unexpected or downstream failure, for example `temporary-failure`.

Targets without `version` are not version-checked. Activating an active domain is `done`
without a change (still audited). The groupware directory is updated once for the whole
request. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description:
Returns one domain in the caller's scope with its usage figures, including the value a mailbox
form needs (`usage.maxNewMailboxQuota`) and the numbers a deletion would remove. Domain
administrators never receive `domainAdmins`.

patch.description:
Changes a domain with a JSON Merge Patch. See `DomainPatch` for who may change what and for
the rules. Administrators may change every editable attribute of any domain; domain
administrators may change the Global Address List flag and the tags of their domains, and the
description with the `domainDesc` permission flag. A read-only key is refused.

Send the version tag in `If-Match` (recommended for interactive clients): a stale tag answers
`412` and changes nothing, also when the change was made in the legacy UI or `/api/v1`. The
tag does not change with the usage figures. After a successful change the groupware directory
is updated and its cache flushed, unless the groupware is disabled. A change of
`globalAddressList` takes effect at the groupware's next restart; an edit never restarts it.
A patch that changes nothing returns the domain unchanged; it is audited with no changes and
triggers no groupware update.

delete.description:
Deletes a domain that has no mailboxes and no resources. Administrators only, with a session
or a read-write key. A domain with mailboxes or resources is refused with `409
domain-not-empty`, which reports how many remain. Use `previewDomainDeletion` first to show
what the deletion affects.

A deletion removes, as legacy mailcow does: the domain, its tags, its domain administrator
assignments and aliases; the sender permissions, quota records, notification settings and
temporary aliases of addresses in the domain; its spam allow and block lists and its MTA-STS
policy; its entries in the domain map and the rate limits; and domain administrator accounts
left without any domain, whose API keys then stop working. Unlike legacy, it also removes the
domain's BCC maps (stored as `@<domain>` or as the bare name), its footer, and every alias
domain that points to it exactly as a deletion of that alias domain would. The DKIM key is
kept, so that the name reuses it when it is added again. The stored mail is moved to
mailcow's garbage area; a failure there does not stop the deletion and is recorded in the
audit record. Then the groupware directory is updated and its cache flushed, unless the
groupware is disabled.

When mailcow's shared store is unavailable, the deletion is refused with `503
temporary-failure` and nothing is removed.

get.description:
Shows what deleting the domain would currently be blocked by (mailboxes and resources), what it
would remove (alias domains, aliases including those of the alias domains, the footer), the
domain administrator accounts it would delete, and whether a DKIM key exists, which it would
keep. Computed by the same rules as `deleteDomain`. Changes nothing and writes no audit
record. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

Returns the footer of a domain in the caller's scope. Administrators and the domain's domain
administrators, no permission flag needed. A domain without a footer returns empty texts,
`skipReplies: false` and no exclusions. An alias domain name answers `404`.

put.description:
Replaces the footer as a whole, where legacy mailcow stores it, so that the mail filter applies
it to mail from the domain and its alias domains. Administrators and the domain's domain
administrators, no permission flag needed; a read-only key is refused. Send the version tag in
`If-Match`: a stale tag answers `412`. Audited, with the texts recorded only as changed and
their old and new sizes.

get.description:
Returns the server settings and limits that the domain forms need before they submit (the
`domains` area of the API-wide capabilities reads, `/capabilities/{area}`): whether
the groupware is enabled, the tagging limit and the other limits, and, for administrators
only, the DKIM defaults and whether the DKIM DNS publication is enabled. Reflects the current
configuration on every request and contains no secret. Administrators and domain
administrators, read-only keys included.

Lists each distinct tag of the domains in the caller's scope with the number of domains that
carry it, for filter and tag-editor suggestions. Tags that appear only on domains outside the
caller's scope are never revealed. `q` searches the tag. Administrators and domain
administrators, read-only keys included.

Lists the domain templates, each with its version tag. Administrators only, read-only keys
included; domain administrators and mailbox users are refused with `403 forbidden`. `q`
searches the name.

post.description:
Creates a domain template. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key. Omitted
values get the legacy defaults; see `DomainTemplateCreateRequest`. A name already used by
another domain template, compared case-insensitively, is refused with `409
domain-template-name-exists`. Audited.

post.summary: Apply an action to several domain templates
post.description:
Deletes up to 100 domain templates in one request, as the legacy mass deletion does.
Administrators only, from a session or a read-write key; any other caller is refused as a whole
(`403`). More than 100 targets are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany` on `targets`, with
`max: 100`).

Otherwise each distinct template is processed like the single deletion, with its checks and
audit record (which carries the bulk request ID), and gets one result in request order:
- `done`: deleted;
- `notFound`: no domain template has this ID;
- `refused`: the Default template (`domain-template-protected`);
- `outdated`: the target's `version` no longer matches (`412` problem); the template is kept;
- `failed`: an unexpected failure.

Targets without `version` are not version-checked. Domains created from a deleted template keep
their values. Legacy's mass deletion of domain templates stops after the first selected
template; this operation deletes every target.

get.description: Returns one domain template. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Changes only the sent values of a domain template (JSON Merge Patch). Administrators only, with
a session or a read-write key. Renaming the Default template, or renaming a template to a name
another domain template has, is refused with `409` and changes nothing. Domains created from
the template keep their values. Send the version tag in `If-Match`: a stale tag answers `412`.
Audited.

delete.description:
Deletes a domain template. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key. The
Default template is refused with `409 domain-template-protected`. Domains created from the
template keep their values. Audited.

get.description:
Lists the aliases in the caller's scope, newest first by default. Administrators see every
alias, including orphaned aliases whose domain no longer exists (`orphaned: true`). Domain
administrators see the aliases of the domains assigned to them and of those domains' alias
domains. The rows through which mailboxes receive mail at their own address are never listed
or counted. Each entry carries the full representation and its version tag.

`q` matches, case-insensitively and as a substring, the address in ASCII and readable
(Unicode) form, the destinations and both comments.
Several values of the same filter match aliases that have any of them. A domain filter outside
a domain administrator's scope returns an empty list.

Data is read on every request, so changes made in the legacy UI or `/api/v1` appear at once.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description:
Only aliases with exactly this address (letter case ignored; the domain part may be given
in Unicode form). Use it to find an alias by address. Repeat for several.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only aliases whose own domain is one of these (an alias domain matches only its own aliases).

parameters.name: primaryDomain
parameters.description: Only aliases of these domains together with their alias domains.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only aliases of these kinds.

parameters.name: destinationType
parameters.description: Only aliases with one of these destination types.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description:
Only aliases that deliver to one of these addresses, among other destinations (letter case
ignored). For example the aliases that deliver to a mailbox.

post.description:
Creates one alias, regular or catch-all, delivering to destination addresses or performing one
special action. Mail to the address is accepted at once. When the alias allows sending, its
destination mailboxes may send as the address, explicit permissions that would duplicate that
right are removed, and the address appears as a sender identity in their webmail when the
alias is visible in the groupware and not a catch-all.

Checks, in this order: validation of every field and entry (`422`, naming every invalid entry,
including external destinations when the server disables them); the `aliasExternalGoto`
permission for added external destinations (`403 attribute-not-permitted`, naming every refused
destination); then `409 address-in-use` and `409 domain-alias-limit-reached`. Concurrent
requests never together exceed the alias limit or create the same address twice. A request
with any invalid or refused entry changes nothing. Audited, including refusals.

Administrators, domain administrators within their scope, and read-write keys of either.

get.summary: Get the capabilities of aliases, alias domains, resources and sender settings
get.description:
The server settings and limits a client needs before it submits: whether the groupware is
enabled, whether external alias destinations are disabled for every role, the bulk limit, page
sizes, field limits, rate limit time frames, DKIM key sizes and, for the alias domain creation
form, the DKIM defaults. Domain administrators get `dkimDefaults` only with the `aliasDomains`
permission and never `dkimDnsPublicationEnabled`. Changes nothing; read-only keys may use it.

post.summary: Apply an action to several aliases
post.description:
Activates, deactivates, shows or hides in the groupware, deletes, or copies over alias domains
up to 100 aliases, as the legacy mass actions do. Each alias is authorised, checked, changed and
audited on its own, exactly as the single operation would, and gets one result: `done`,
`notFound` (missing or outside the caller's scope), `refused` (with `problem`), `outdated` (its
`version` no longer matches) or `failed`. Every audit record carries `bulkRequestId`; a copy
has one record per created alias. One failure does not stop or undo the others, as in legacy.

The whole request is refused only when the caller's role or key scope never allows the action
(`403`). More than 100 targets are refused with `422` (`tooMany`, `max` 100).

get.description:
Returns one alias in the caller's scope with its version tag. An alias outside the caller's
scope, and the row through which a mailbox receives mail at its own address, answer `404`
exactly like an alias that does not exist.

patch.description:
Changes the attributes that are sent (JSON Merge Patch). Interactive clients should always send
`If-Match` with the version they read: the legacy UI edits the same rows and never sends a
version, so only the version check protects a change made there meanwhile.

After the change, explicit permissions that let a destination mailbox send as the address are
removed when the alias allows sending (they are kept when it does not, because they override
it), and the groupware identities of the former and new destination mailboxes are updated. A
failure of that groupware update does not undo the change and is recorded in the audit record.
Turning sending off takes the right away from the destination mailboxes that hold no explicit
permission.

The `If-Match` check comes first (`412`), then the order of checks of `createAlias`.

delete.description:
Deletes the alias and every explicit sender permission to send as its address. For a catch-all
alias that address is `@domain`, so the domain-wide explicit permissions for that domain go
with it, as in legacy. The groupware identities of the destination mailboxes are updated.
Other aliases that name the deleted address as a destination keep it, as in legacy. Orphaned
aliases can be deleted by administrators. Audited.

post.summary: Copy an alias over its domain's alias domains
post.description:
The legacy action "Expand alias over alias domains". For each alias domain of the alias's
domain, creates `<local part>@<alias domain>` (for a catch-all, `@<alias domain>`) with the same
destination or special action, active state, "allowed to send as", groupware visibility and
internal flag, and no comments, unless that address is in use. Each copy is created with the
checks and follow-up steps of a creation by the caller and has its own audit record carrying
the request ID. The response lists the outcome per alias domain.

An alias that lives in an alias domain is refused with `409 not-primary-domain-alias`. A domain
without alias domains succeeds and creates nothing. `If-Match` makes sure the copies are made
from the version the client read.

get.description:
Lists the alias domains in the caller's scope: all for administrators, those whose target is
one of their domains for domain administrators. `q` matches, case-insensitively and as a
substring, the name and the target in ASCII and readable (Unicode) form. Each entry carries its
version tag. The rate limits are read from mailcow's
shared store; when it is unavailable the request answers `503`.

parameters.name: targetDomain
parameters.description: Only alias domains of these target domains. Repeat for several.

post.description:
Creates one alias domain, so that every mailbox of the target domain also receives mail under
the new name. The alias domain and its entry in mailcow's domain map (Redis `DOMAIN_MAP`, which
the mail filter uses to recognise local domains) are stored together or not at all; when the
shared store is unavailable the request answers `503` and stores nothing. External sender
addresses of any mailbox that lie in the new alias domain are removed, because the domain is
now local.

Then the follow-up steps run, and a failing step never undoes the creation: the initial rate
limit, the DKIM key (with the fork-only DNS publication when enabled), and the groupware
directory update. `data.creationReport` gives each outcome. The rate limit is read-only
afterwards (feature 006) and DKIM keys are managed in feature 010.

Domain administrators need `aliasDomains`, and `ratelimit` for an initial rate limit; a missing
flag refuses the request before anything is stored. Audited with the creation report.

post.summary: Apply an action to several alias domains
post.description:
Activates, deactivates or deletes up to 100 alias domains, as the legacy mass actions do. Each
alias domain is authorised, checked, changed and audited on its own, exactly as the single
change or deletion would, and gets one result. A shared-store failure on one target gives that
target `failed` (with a `temporary-failure` problem) and changes nothing for it. Every audit
record carries `bulkRequestId`. More than 100 targets are refused with `422` (`tooMany`,
`max` 100).

get.description:
Returns one alias domain in the caller's scope with its version tag. When mailcow's shared
store is unavailable, so that the rate limit cannot be read, the request answers `503`.

patch.description:
Changes the target domain or the active state (JSON Merge Patch). No permission flag is needed,
as in legacy; a domain administrator can only move an alias domain between domains they manage.
A new target must be an existing domain (not an alias domain) in the caller's scope that is not
a relay (backup MX) domain, and the alias domain's aliases must fit within the new target's
alias limit. After the change the groupware directory is updated. Deactivating an alias domain
stops mail to its addresses. Interactive clients should always send `If-Match`. Audited.

get.description:
Lists the resources in the caller's scope: all for administrators, those of their domains for
domain administrators. `q` matches, case-insensitively and as a substring, the description and
the address in ASCII and readable (Unicode) form. Each entry carries its version tag.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only resources of these domains. Repeat for several.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only resources of these kinds.

post.description:
Creates a location, thing or group that is booked through the groupware. The address is
derived from the description and never changes. The resource is stored as legacy stores it
(without a password and with no quota), so it does not count towards the domain's mailbox limit
or quota, and the groupware directory is updated so that it can be booked at once. Audited.

post.summary: Apply an action to several resources
post.description:
Activates, deactivates or deletes up to 100 resources, as the legacy mass actions do. Each
resource is processed and audited on its own, exactly as the single change or deletion would,
and gets one result. Every audit record carries `bulkRequestId`. More than 100 targets are refused
with `422` (`tooMany`, `max` 100).

get.description: Returns one resource in the caller's scope with its version tag. A mailbox address answers `404`.

patch.description:
Changes the description, kind, booking rule or active state (JSON Merge Patch). The address and
the domain never change. The groupware directory is updated; an inactive resource disappears
from the groupware and can no longer be booked. Interactive clients should always send
`If-Match`. Audited.

delete.description:
Deletes the resource and its groupware data (profile, cached folders, sharing permissions,
calendars and their indexes), and updates the groupware directory. Audited.

get.summary: Get what a mailbox may send as
get.description:
Returns every address the mailbox may send as and why: its own address, its addresses in its
domain's alias domains, the aliases that deliver to it (with whether each allows sending and
whether it is a catch-all), its explicit permissions (each marked changeable or not for the
caller, and stale when its domain or address no longer exists), whether its sender check is
disabled, and its external sender addresses. The version tag covers the explicit permissions
and external sender addresses only.

Administrators for every mailbox, domain administrators for the mailboxes of their domains.

patch.summary: Change what a mailbox may send as
patch.description:
Replaces the explicit permissions, the external sender addresses, or both (each list that is
sent replaces the stored list as a whole). The mail server applies the change to the next
submission. After the external sender addresses change, the mailbox's groupware identities are
updated, so its external full addresses become selectable sender identities.

Hints repeated from the legacy UI:
- For an external domain, import a DKIM key for it and add this server to the domain's SPF
  record, or receivers may reject the mail.
- A permission for another mailbox's address applies to the mail server at once, but the
  groupware offers that address as a sender identity only after the other mailbox delegates
  access in the groupware.

"Any address" (`*`) is for administrators only. Domain administrators keep the entries outside
their scope and need `extendSenderAcl` to change external sender addresses. A request with any
invalid or refused entry is refused as a whole, naming every such entry. Interactive clients
should always send `If-Match`. Audited.

get.summary: List entries that could be granted to a mailbox
get.description:
Helper list for the sender settings form. Lists the entries the caller could add to the
explicit sender permissions of the mailbox named in `mailbox`, as the legacy selection list
does: the domains and alias domains in the caller's scope, "any address" (`*`) for
administrators, and the addresses of aliases and mailboxes in the caller's scope. The mailbox
itself, the aliases that deliver to it, its alias-domain addresses, catch-all aliases and the
entries already granted are left out. `q` matches the value case-insensitively as a substring.
A mailbox that does not exist, is outside the caller's scope or is a resource gives `422` with
`notFound` on `mailbox`.

parameters.name: mailbox
parameters.description:
Full address of the mailbox whose sender settings are edited, in any letter case and with
the domain in ASCII or Unicode form.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only candidates of these types.

get.description:
Lists the mailboxes in the caller's scope: every mailbox for an administrator, the mailboxes of
the domains assigned to a domain administrator (active assignments). Resources are never
listed. Each entry carries the full representation and its version tag; a page is built
without a lookup per mailbox. `q` matches the address, the display name and the tags as
case-insensitive substrings. Filters accept several values (repeat the parameter) and match any
of them; filters combine with each other and with `q`. A domain outside the caller's scope
matches nothing.

Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a key (read-only keys included).
Mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only mailboxes of these domains (ASCII or Unicode form, any letter case).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only mailboxes with one of these statuses.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only mailboxes carrying one of these tags (whole tag, case-insensitive).

parameters.name: authSource
parameters.description: Only mailboxes with one of these authentication sources.

post.description:
Creates a mailbox in a domain of the caller's scope, exactly as the legacy "Add mailbox" form
does: the mailbox row with its settings and password hash, its zeroed usage records (primary
and replica), its own alias with the mailbox's status, its user permissions and its tags are
stored together. The domain's mailbox limit, maximum mailbox quota and domain quota hold even
for concurrent requests. Then the follow-up steps run: the initial rate limit and the
tagged-mail handling in mailcow's shared store, and the groupware directory entry with a cache
flush (skipped when the groupware is disabled). A failed follow-up step never removes the
mailbox; `creationReport` reports each one. Audited, without the password.

Administrators and domain administrators (see `MailboxCreateRequest` for the permission
flags), from a session or a read-write key.

get.description:
Returns the server settings and limits a client needs before it submits a mailbox form: the
configured identity provider type and the authentication sources it allows, whether the
groupware is enabled and last logins are reported, the bulk, tag, custom-attribute and page
limits, and the garbage-area retention. Changes nothing. Administrators and domain
administrators, from a session or a key (read-only keys included).

get.summary: List the mailbox tags in use
get.description:
Lists the distinct tags of the mailboxes in the caller's scope with the number of mailboxes
that carry each, for tag filters and tag suggestions. Tags that differ only in letter case form
one entry. `q` is a case-insensitive substring search on the tag. Administrators and domain
administrators, from a session or a key (read-only keys included).

post.summary: Apply an action to several mailboxes
post.description:
Activates, disables login for, deactivates or deletes up to 100 mailboxes, or allows or
disallows one protocol for them, as the legacy mass actions do. Each mailbox is processed like
the single operation, with the same checks, side effects and audit record (which carries the
bulk request ID). A target outside the caller's scope gets `notFound`, an outdated `version`
gets `outdated`, and a failed mail-store cleanup or service outage gets `failed`; the other
targets proceed. The response has one result per distinct target, in request order.

Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a read-write key.

get.description:
Returns one mailbox of the caller's scope with its full representation, including the largest
quota it may be given, its user permissions and custom attributes, and its version tag.
Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a key (read-only keys included).

patch.description:
Changes the values sent (JSON Merge Patch): display name, status, quota, password, forced
password change and second-factor setup, webmail redirect, protocol access, authentication
source, recovery e-mail, tags, user permissions and custom attributes. A status change gives
the mailbox's own alias the same status. Afterwards the groupware directory entry is updated,
the groupware cache is flushed (unless the groupware is disabled) and the identity-provider
template marker (`attributes.attribute_hash`) is cleared, as legacy does on every edit. Send the
version tag in `If-Match`: an edit made meanwhile in the legacy UI then gives `412`. Audited
with every changed value, except the password, recorded only as set.

Administrators and domain administrators (see `MailboxPatch` for the permission flags), from a
session or a read-write key.

delete.description:
First asks the mail store to move the mailbox's mail to mailcow's garbage area (every mail node
in a replicated cluster), from which mailcow purges it after `MAILDIR_GC_TIME`. If the mail
store reports a failure or cannot be reached, the deletion is refused (`503`) and nothing is
removed; if it does not answer within `DOCKER_TIMEOUT`, the answer is `504` and no records are
removed (a retry is safe). Then, together, it removes everything legacy removes: the mailbox,
its usage records, user permissions, tags, sieve filters, app passwords, aliases whose only
recipient is the mailbox (its own alias included), the mailbox from other aliases' recipients,
sender permissions in both directions, temporary aliases, sync jobs delivering into it, spam
settings and allow and block lists, quarantine items, push notification settings, BCC maps with
it as local destination, webmail data, OAuth tokens and codes, second factors, passkeys and its
rate limit; and also its tagged-mail handling and recent-login records, which legacy leaves
behind. The groupware directory entry is removed and the cache flushed. Audited.

Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a read-write key.

get.description:
Reports what `deleteMailbox` would remove and move now, whether it could proceed (the only
blockers are an unreachable mail store or shared store), the garbage-area retention and the
current version tag. Changes nothing and writes no audit record. Administrators and domain
administrators, from a session or a key (read-only keys included).

post.description:
Changes the local part of an active or login-disabled mailbox. Every check runs before anything
changes: status, a different local part, a free new address, room for the optional alias, and
reachable mail store and webmail services. Then it does what legacy does (the shared-folder
permissions are removed and re-created for the new address in both directions, every row that
names the mailbox is updated, the maildir is moved and the SOGo data is renamed) and also
carries over what legacy leaves behind (second factors, passkeys, temporary aliases, spam
settings, quarantine items, the rate limit, tagged-mail handling and recent logins). OAuth
tokens and codes bound to the old address are revoked, and the groupware cache is flushed. The
permission flags of a domain-administrator account with the same name are not moved.

A failing step undoes the steps already done (`503`, extension `steps`). If undoing fails too,
the answer is `500` with type `mailbox-rename-incomplete`. A step without an answer within
`DOCKER_TIMEOUT` gives `504`. Audited with both addresses and every step's outcome.

Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a read-write key.

get.description:
Lists the mailbox templates, each with its values and version tag. `q` searches the name.
Administrators and domain administrators (who pick a template when creating a mailbox), from a
session or a key (read-only keys included).

post.description:
Creates a template. Values not given get the built-in defaults, with an unlimited quota as in
the legacy Default template. Audited. Administrators only, from a session or a read-write key.

post.summary: Apply an action to several mailbox templates

get.description: Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a key (read-only keys included).

patch.description:
Changes only the values sent. The Default template cannot be renamed
(`mailbox-template-protected`). Mailboxes created from the template do not change. Audited.
Administrators only, from a session or a read-write key.

delete.description:
Deletes the template. The Default template cannot be deleted (`mailbox-template-protected`).
Mailboxes created from the template do not change. Audited. Administrators only, from a session
or a read-write key.

get.description:
Returns the password policy that applies when a password is set, as structured rules, read from
where legacy keeps it (Redis `PASSWD_POLICY`) on every request, with the legacy defaults for
rules never saved. A password that meets these rules is accepted by `createMailbox` and
`updateMailbox`. The version tag is the one feature 013 uses to change the policy. Changes
nothing. When mailcow's shared store is unavailable the answer is `503`.

Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a key (read-only keys included).
Mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`).

patch.description:
Feature 013. Changes the sent rules of the password policy, stored where legacy keeps it, and
returns the whole policy with its new version tag, the same tag `getPasswordPolicy` returns. The
policy applies to the next password set through either UI or either API; existing passwords
keep working, and nothing is reloaded. A minimum length outside 3 to 64 is refused and changes
nothing. Audited with each changed rule. Administrators only, by session or by an
administrator's read-write key.

get.description:
Lists one entry per domain, per alias domain and, for administrators, per unused key (a key whose
name is neither a domain nor an alias domain), with its key state. Domain administrators see the
domains assigned to them and the alias domains that point to those domains, never unused keys.
No permission flag is needed. Entries never contain private keys.

`q` searches the ASCII and the readable name, case-insensitively and as a substring.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only entries in one of these states. Repeat the parameter for several.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Only entries whose key has exactly this selector.

parameters.name: complete
parameters.description:
`true`: only entries with a complete key. `false`: only entries with an incomplete key.
Entries without a key never match.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only this domain and the alias domains that point to it (ASCII or Unicode form).

post.description:
Creates a new RSA key pair for one domain or alias domain and stores its public key, selector and
private key where mailcow keeps DKIM keys (Redis `DKIM_PUB_KEYS`, `DKIM_SELECTORS` and
`DKIM_PRIV_KEYS`), all together or not at all. Rspamd signs the name's outgoing mail and seals
its forwarded mail (ARC) with it from the next message on. Domain and alias domain creation use
the same generation.

Administrators may generate for any domain or alias domain, domain administrators for those in
their scope; any other name answers `404`. A name that already has a key answers `409`
(`dkim-key-exists`) unless an administrator sends `overwrite: true`, which replaces the whole old
key atomically and answers `200`; `If-Match` then applies to the old key.

When the FeldHost DKIM DNS publication is enabled, the record is published to the name's
ISPConfig zone within 15 seconds, and `data.dnsPublication` reports the outcome; a failure never
undoes the key. Audited, without the private key.

post.summary: Apply an action to several DKIM keys
post.description:
Deletes up to 100 DKIM keys in one request, as the legacy mass remove does. Administrators
only, with a session or a read-write key; any other caller is refused as a whole (`403`). More
than 100 targets are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany` on `targets`, with `max: 100`).

Otherwise each distinct name is processed on its own, with the checks, side effects and audit
record of `deleteDkimKey`, and gets one result in request order:
- `done`: the key's public key, selector and private key were removed together; signing stops
  from the next message, and the entry of a domain or alias domain then shows `missing`;
- `notFound`: the name has no key (or is not a valid name);
- `outdated`: the target's `version` no longer matches (`412` problem); the key is unchanged;
- `failed`: an unexpected or downstream failure, for example `temporary-failure` when mailcow's
  shared store is unavailable; nothing of that key was removed.

Targets without `version` are not version-checked. When the FeldHost DKIM DNS publication is
enabled, each removed key's record is removed from its ISPConfig zone (at most 15 seconds per
key) and `meta.dnsPublication` reports the outcome per target; a failed removal never undoes the
deletion. Unless the publication is enabled, published records stay until the operator removes
them. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description:
Returns the entry of one name with its key state and, when it has a key, its selector, its exact
key length, its public key and the DNS TXT record to publish, as one text and split into pieces
of at most 255 characters. Administrators reach every domain, alias domain and unused key;
domain administrators reach the domains assigned to them and their alias domains. Any other name
answers `404`. Never contains the private key.

delete.description:
Removes the public key, the selector and the private key of the name together. Signing and
sealing with the key stop from the next message. The domain or alias domain itself is unchanged:
its entry then shows `missing`; the entry of an unused key disappears. A name without a key
answers `404`. Administrators only.

Unless the FeldHost DKIM DNS publication is enabled, the published DNS record stays until the
operator removes it. When the publication is enabled, the record is removed from the name's
ISPConfig zone within 15 seconds. The response has no body: the publication outcome is recorded
in the audit record of the deletion, which clients read from the audit history of the name
(`listAuditEvents` filtered by target).

post.description:
Stores an existing unencrypted RSA private key (PEM, PKCS #1 or PKCS #8, 1,024 to 8,192 bits) for
the name in the path, with the public key derived from it, all together or not at all. The name
must be a valid domain name but need not be a domain or alias domain, as in legacy: a key
imported for another name is listed as unused until that domain or alias domain is created,
which then reuses it. Administrators only.

A name that already has a key answers `409` (`dkim-key-exists`) unless `overwrite: true` is sent,
which replaces the whole old key, including the private key stored under the old selector,
atomically and answers `200`; `If-Match` then applies to the old key. The key text never appears
in any response, error, log or audit record. Publication and audit as for `generateDkimKey`.

post.summary: Copy a DKIM key to another name
post.description:
Copies the selector, public key and private key of the name in the path (the source, which must
have a key, valid or unused) to one target, which must be an existing domain or alias domain.
The source stays unchanged. A source without a key answers `404`. Administrators only.

A target that already has a key answers `409` (`dkim-key-exists`) unless `overwrite: true` is
sent, which replaces the target's whole old key, including the private key stored under its old
selector, atomically and answers `200`; `If-Match` then applies to the target's old key. The
response contains the target's entry and the DKIM DNS publication outcome for the target.
Audited on the target, with the source name.

get.description:
Returns the private key of the name exactly as stored. Administrators only, and only while the
operator setting mirroring legacy's `SHOW_DKIM_PRIV_KEYS` is enabled (off by default); otherwise
`403` with type `/api/v2/problems/dkim-private-key-export-disabled`. An export is a read, so an
administrator's API key may export with either access level. A name without a key answers
`404`. Every export and every refused attempt is audited, without the key. No other operation
ever returns a private key.

post.summary: Publish a DKIM record to ISPConfig again
post.description:
FeldHost DKIM DNS publication: publishes the record of the name's current key to the ISPConfig
zone whose origin is exactly the name, with the same steps and outcomes as after a key change,
for example after a failed publication. It changes the DNS zone, so read-only keys are refused.
Administrators only. A name without a key answers `404`. While the publication is disabled (the
default), `403` with type `/api/v2/problems/dkim-dns-publication-disabled`. The key itself is
unchanged. Audited with the outcome.

get.summary: Get the DKIM, MTA-STS and DNS diagnostics capabilities
get.description:
Returns the server values and limits that clients need before they submit: the server host name
(to pre-fill MTA-STS MX hosts), the DKIM defaults and limits, the MTA-STS defaults and limits,
and the DNS diagnostics limits. Administrators and domain administrators; read-only keys may use
it. `dkim.privateKeyExportEnabled` is `null` for domain administrators. Contains no secret and
no connection detail.

Lists the policies of the domains in the caller's scope: every domain for administrators, the
domains assigned to them for domain administrators. No permission flag is needed. Policies
belong to domains only; alias domains publish their target domain's policy. `q` searches the
ASCII and the readable domain name.

post.description:
Creates the policy of a domain in the caller's scope, with version `STSv1` unless sent, a new
policy identifier, and inactive unless `active: true` is sent, as in legacy. Any other name,
including an alias domain's, answers `404`. A domain that already has a policy answers `409`
(`mta-sts-policy-exists`).

While the policy is active, mailcow's publication endpoint serves it for the domain and its
alias domains from the next request on, and mailcow's certificate service requests
certificates for the `mta-sts.` names at its next run, which can take up to one day. Policies
cannot be deleted through this API: deactivate them instead; a policy is removed with its
domain. Audited.

get.description:
Returns the policy of a domain in the caller's scope with its identifier, the address at which it
is published, the policy text that is served while it is active, and the DNS records it needs.
A domain without a policy, a domain outside the caller's scope and an alias domain's name answer
`404`.

patch.description:
Changes the members sent; the others keep their values. A change of the version, the mode, the
MX hosts (including their order) or the maximum age assigns a new policy identifier, always
different from the previous one, so that senders fetch the new policy; a change of only the
active state, or a patch that changes nothing, keeps it. A domain without a policy answers
`404`. Audited with each changed member and the old and new identifier; a patch that changes
nothing is not audited.

get.summary: Run DNS diagnostics for a domain or alias domain
get.description:
Looks up every DNS record the name needs (MX, autodiscover and autoconfig, MTA-STS when the
policy that applies is active, SPF, DMARC, DKIM when the name has a key, and the service
records of non-standard ports), compares each with the value expected from the server's
configuration, and returns one structured check per record plus a zone file. Administrators
