first get the server-wide checks: the host name's IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, their reverse names
and the TLSA record for SMTP on port 25. Domain administrators reach the domains assigned to
them and their alias domains, without the server-wide checks. For an alias domain, the MTA-STS
checks expect its target domain's policy.

Lookups use the same recursive resolver as mailcow's mail services. Each lookup gives up after
5 seconds and the whole run returns within 30 seconds: checks still open then report
`lookupFailed` with reason `runTimeout`. DNS changes can take up to 24 hours to show. A run
changes nothing and is not audited.

Each caller (user or API key) may start 10 runs per minute; every response carries
`RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`. The server's public addresses
and certificate digest may be reused for up to 10 minutes.

Returns the server's external identity provider configuration with the defaults legacy shows
for missing values, whether each secret is set (never the secret), whether each mapped template
exists, whether the configuration is complete for sign-in, the new web app's return addresses
to register at the provider, the number of mailboxes per external authentication source and,
for Keycloak and LDAP, the synchronisation status. Values are read from mailcow on every
request, so changes made in the legacy UI or `/api/v1` are visible at once.

Administrators only: a signed-in administrator or a key owned by an administrator, read-only
keys included. Reads are not audited.

put.summary: Save the whole identity provider configuration
put.description:
Creates the configuration (`201`) or replaces the stored one (`200`) with a whole configuration
of the given type. Settings not sent take their defaults. The configuration is stored with
legacy's setting names and encodings, so the legacy UI, the mail clients' sign-in check and the
next synchronisation run use it at once, without a restart. After the save, only the settings
of the saved type are stored: settings of a previous type are removed. The cached Keycloak
service token is cleared. No mailbox changes.

- **Secrets** are write-only. The client secret or bind password must be sent when no
  configuration of the type is stored. Otherwise an omitted secret keeps the stored one, unless
  the address that receives it changes (Keycloak `serverUrl`, generic OIDC `tokenEndpoint`,
  LDAP `hosts`): then it must be sent again (rule code `secretRequired`) and nothing changes.
- **Type change**: refused with `identity-provider-in-use` while any mailbox authenticates
  against an external source other than the new type.
- **Mapping**: every mapped template and the default template must exist (rule code
  `notFound`); attribute values must be unique (rule code `duplicate`).
- Send the version tag you read in `If-Match`; the legacy UI edits the same settings. For a
  first setup, send `If-None-Match: *` so that the save only creates.

Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key. Audited, with every changed setting
and secrets only as "changed".

patch.summary: Change settings of the identity provider configuration
patch.description:
Changes only the settings sent (JSON Merge Patch) and keeps the others; the rules of a whole
save apply to the result. The type cannot change here: use `PUT`. A changed Keycloak
`serverUrl`, generic OIDC `tokenEndpoint` or LDAP `hosts` requires the secret in the same
request. A successful change clears the cached Keycloak service token, as every save does.

Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key. Audited.

delete.description:
Removes every stored setting, including the secrets and the cached Keycloak service token.
Single sign-on becomes unavailable, password sign-in through the provider stops, and the
synchronisation jobs stop at their next run. Refused with `identity-provider-in-use` while any
mailbox authenticates against an external source.

Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key. Audited.

post.summary: Test the connection with candidate settings
post.description:
Tests unsaved candidate settings and stores nothing. The settings must meet the rules of a
whole save, except that mapped templates need not exist. An omitted secret is replaced by the
stored one only when the stored type is the same and the address that receives the secret is
unchanged; otherwise the request is refused (rule code `secretRequired`). Each call to the
provider times out after 7 seconds, and the TLS certificate is verified unless
`ignoreTlsErrors` is `true`. Internal addresses are allowed.

The test sends credentials to a host, so it is an action: administrators only, with a session
or a read-write key, and audited with the provider type, the tested address and the outcome.

Starts a mailbox-user sign-in through the configured Keycloak or generic OIDC provider and
returns the provider's authorization address. Offer it to mailbox users when
`GET /public-config` reports `externalIdentityProvider.singleSignOnAvailable`. When the login
page option `forceSingleSignOn` is also set, offer single sign-on instead of the password form
on the mailbox-user sign-in screen and keep passkey sign-in; the API refuses no sign-in method
because of that option.

The pending single sign-on is bound to this browser session, carries a single-use random
`state` and a PKCE proof key (S256), and expires after 10 minutes. A new start replaces it. The
return address is the new web app's sign-in return address
(`https://<host>/ng/sso/return`) on the host name of this request when it is one of the server's
host names, and otherwise on `MAILCOW_HOSTNAME`. Keycloak is asked for `profile` and `email`,
plus `openid` from version 20.0.0; a generic OIDC provider for its configured scopes.

The provider returns the browser to the return address with `code` and `state`: submit them to
`POST /session/single-sign-on/completion`. With `error` and `state` instead: submit them to
`POST /session/single-sign-on/provider-error`. Not audited (ceremony); the completion is.

delete.description:
Discards the session's pending single sign-on, so its state can no longer be used. Succeeds
and changes nothing when none is pending. Not audited (ceremony).

post.description:
Completes the pending single sign-on with the `code` and `state` the provider returned. The
state is consumed by the first attempt; an unknown, expired, used or foreign state is refused
with `sign-in-state-invalid` without contacting the provider. The completion uses the current
configuration.

The code is exchanged, with the client credentials and the PKCE proof key, for the provider's
tokens, and the user details are read from the user info endpoint. The e-mail address (trimmed,
lower-cased) must belong to a mailbox, not a resource, whose authentication source is the
configured type, and the mailbox and its domain must be active. When no mailbox exists and
automatic creation is on, a mailbox is created from the template that the user's
`mailcow_template` value maps to, or from the default template. An existing mailbox whose value
maps to a changed template is updated from it first.

The session becomes `active` for the mailbox user, with `authMethod: singleSignOn`: no mailcow
second factor is asked for, and forced password change and second-factor setup do not restrict
it. A recent-login entry is recorded. The provider's tokens stay on the server. When the
provider issued a renewal token, the session is re-validated with the provider on the first
request more than 5 minutes after the last renewal; when that fails, the session ends with
`identity-provider-session-ended`. Signing out ends the session here only, not at the provider.

Failures are audited; they are neither reported to fail2ban nor counted towards sign-in
throttling. The session identifier is renewed on success.

post.summary: Report an error returned by the provider
post.description:
Reports that the provider returned the browser with `error` and `state` instead of a code, for
example because the user cancelled (`access_denied`). The state is validated and consumed as for
a completion, the pending single sign-on is cancelled, and a failed sign-in is audited with the
provider's error code. The provider's free-text description is never accepted or stored.

get.description:
Lists the OAuth2 clients, by default ordered by identifier, without secrets. `q` searches the
client ID and the redirect URIs, case-insensitively. Administrators only: a signed-in
administrator or a key owned by an administrator, read-only keys included.

parameters.name: hasActiveTokens
parameters.description: Only clients with (`true`) or without (`false`) an unexpired access or refresh token.

post.description:
Registers an application. The server generates, from a cryptographically secure source, a
client ID of 12 lowercase hexadecimal characters that no other client has and a secret of 24
lowercase hexadecimal characters, and sets the scope `profile`. The response contains the
secret exactly once. The legacy UI lists the client at once.

Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key. Audited without the secret.

post.summary: Delete, revoke the tokens of or renew the secrets of several OAuth2 clients
post.description:
Applies `delete`, `revokeTokens` or `renewSecret` to up to 100 clients, as the legacy mass
actions of the "OAuth2 Apps" table do. The whole request is refused only when the caller may never use the
action (role or key scope). Otherwise each distinct client is processed, checked and audited on
its own, as the single request for it would be, and gets one result: `done`, `notFound`,
`refused`, `outdated` (its `version` no longer matches) or `failed`. One failure does not stop
the others. A client named twice is processed once. Every audit record carries the bulk
request's identifier. `renewSecret` returns each new secret once, in the item's result
(`clientSecret`); it is never shown again, so copy it from this response (API gap G42).

Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key.

get.description: Returns one client without its secret. Administrators only, as for `listOauth2Clients`.

patch.summary: Replace an OAuth2 client's redirect URIs
patch.description:
Replaces the redirect URIs under the rules of the creation. The client ID and the scope cannot
change. Issued tokens are kept. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key.
Audited.

delete.description:
Removes the client together with its access tokens, refresh tokens and authorization codes, so
the profile endpoint refuses its access tokens at once. Administrators only, with a session or a
read-write key. Audited with the number of tokens and codes removed.

post.description:
Replaces the secret with a new one of 24 lowercase hexadecimal characters, returned only in this
response. Existing access tokens, refresh tokens and authorization codes are kept, but renewing
a token or exchanging a code with the old secret fails, as legacy documents. Administrators
only, with a session or a read-write key. Audited without the secret. The bulk action
`renewSecret` regenerates the secrets of several clients (API gap G42).

post.summary: Revoke all tokens of an OAuth2 client
post.description:
Removes the client's access tokens, refresh tokens and authorization codes, so every application
session ends at once and users must authorise again. A client without tokens is answered the
same way and nothing changes. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key. Audited
with the number of tokens and codes removed.

get.description:
Lists the administrator accounts, each with its full representation and version tag.
Administrators only: a signed-in administrator or a key owned by an administrator, read-only
keys included. `q` searches the username (case-insensitive substring).

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) accounts.

post.description:
Creates an active administrator (unless `active: false` is sent) without forced actions
(unless sent). Only a signed-in administrator may create administrators: requests
authenticated by a key are refused with `session-required`, so that a leaked key cannot create
lasting administrator credentials. Audited without the password.

post.summary: Apply an action to several administrators
post.description:
Activates, deactivates, suspends the second factors of, or deletes up to the bulk limit of
administrators (100) in one request, as the legacy mass actions do. Only a signed-in
administrator may do this: requests with a key, and callers of other roles, are refused as a
whole (`403`). More targets than the limit are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany` on
`targets`, with the limit as `max`).

Otherwise each distinct account is processed in the order given, with the checks, side effects
and audit record of the single operation, and gets one result:
- `done`: applied, with the new version tag unless deleted;
- `notFound`: no administrator has this username (also a domain administrator's username);
- `refused`: `last-active-admin` (the item that would leave no active administrator) or
  `cannot-delete-own-account`;
- `outdated`: the target's `version` no longer matches (`412` problem); the account is
  unchanged;
- `failed`: an unexpected failure.

Targets without `version` are not version-checked. Every audit record carries the
`bulkRequestId`. The path accepts only `POST`, and account paths never accept `POST`, so an
administrator named `bulk-actions` stays readable at `GET /admins/bulk-actions`.

get.description:
Returns one administrator account with its version tag. Administrators only, with a session or
a key (read-only keys included).

patch.description:
Changes the username, password, status or forced flags of an administrator with a JSON Merge
Patch (see `AdminPatch` for the rules). Only a signed-in administrator may do this; keys are
refused with `session-required`.

A deactivation or a deletion never leaves the server without an active administrator: the
check and the change are atomic, so concurrent requests cannot together remove the last one
(`409 last-active-admin`). An administrator may deactivate their own account while another
active administrator remains; their session then ends at its next request.

Send the version tag in `If-Match` (recommended for interactive clients): a stale tag answers
`412` and changes nothing, also when the change was made in the legacy UI or `/api/v1`. A
patch that changes nothing returns the account unchanged and is not audited. Every change is
audited with its old and new values; a password only as changed.

delete.description:
Deletes an administrator account. Only a signed-in administrator may do this; keys are refused
with `session-required`. Administrators cannot delete their own account
(`409 cannot-delete-own-account`), and the last active administrator cannot be deleted
(`409 last-active-admin`).

The deletion removes, as legacy mailcow does, the account and any domain assignments,
permission record, second factors and passkeys with its username. It also revokes the
account's API keys permanently (revocation reason `ownerDeleted`, revoked by the caller), ends
its sessions and every impersonation of it, and removes its preferences. Audit records are
kept. A later account with the same username inherits nothing.

post.description:
Deactivates every TOTP, WebAuthn and Yubico OTP entry of the account until its next successful
password sign-in, which re-activates them (legacy "disable TFA until next successful login").
Passkeys are not affected. Suspending an account without active entries succeeds and changes
nothing. Only a signed-in administrator may do this; keys are refused with `session-required`.
Audited with the number of suspended entries.

get.description:
Returns the server values a client needs before it creates or changes administrator and
domain administrator accounts: the default permission flags of a new domain administrator as
this server's mailcow schema stores them, the defaults of a new account, the bulk limit, the
page sizes, the username length limit and the single sign-on token lifetime. Changes nothing.
Administrators only, with a session or a key (read-only keys included).

Lists every domain administrator account, including accounts without any assignment, each
with its domains, permission flags and version tag. Administrators only: a signed-in
administrator or a key owned by an administrator, read-only keys included. `q` searches the
username and the assigned domain names in ASCII and readable form (case-insensitive
substring).

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) accounts.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description:
Only accounts with an assignment to any of these domains (ASCII or Unicode form, any letter
case). Repeat the parameter for several.

parameters.name: permission
parameters.description: Only accounts whose flag of this name has the value `permissionValue`. A missing permission record counts as every flag `false`.

parameters.name: permissionValue
parameters.description: Value the flag named by `permission` must have. Only valid together with `permission`.

post.description:
Creates a domain administrator with a username, a password and at least one domain, and
optionally its status, forced flags and permission flags (see `DomainAdminCreateRequest`).
Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key owned by an administrator, so that
billing systems can provision resellers. Audited without the password.

post.summary: Apply an action to several domain administrators
post.description:
Activates, deactivates, suspends the second factors of, or deletes up to the bulk limit of
domain administrators (100) in one request, as the legacy mass actions do. Administrators
only, with a session or a read-write key owned by an administrator; any other caller is refused
as a whole (`403`). More targets than the limit are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany` on
`targets`, with the limit as `max`).

Otherwise each distinct account is processed in the order given, with the checks, side effects
and audit record of the single operation, and gets one result:
- `done`: applied, with the new version tag unless deleted;
- `notFound`: no domain administrator has this username (also an administrator's username);
- `outdated`: the target's `version` no longer matches (`412` problem); the account is
  unchanged;
- `failed`: an unexpected failure.

Activating an active account is `done` without a change. Targets without `version` are not
version-checked. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`. The path accepts only `POST`,
and account paths never accept `POST`, so a domain administrator named `bulk-actions` stays
readable at `GET /domain-admins/bulk-actions`.

get.description:
Returns one domain administrator account with its domains, its 19 permission flags and its
version tag. Administrators only, with a session or a key (read-only keys included). A domain
administrator reads its own flags through `GET /me`.

patch.description:
Changes the username, password, status, forced flags, domains or permission flags of a domain
administrator with a JSON Merge Patch (see `DomainAdminPatch` for the rules). Administrators
only, with a session or a read-write key owned by an administrator. No domain administrator can
change any permission flag, its own or another's.

Changes apply to the account's next request, of its sessions, its API keys and its
impersonations. Send the version tag in `If-Match` (recommended for interactive clients): a
stale tag answers `412` and changes nothing, also when the change was made in the legacy UI or
`/api/v1`. A patch that changes nothing returns the account unchanged and is not audited. Every
change is audited with its old and new values, the domains added and removed and the flags
changed; a password only as changed.

delete.description:
Deletes a domain administrator account, with or without assignments. Administrators only, with
a session or a read-write key owned by an administrator.

The deletion removes, as legacy mailcow does, the account, its assignments, its permission
record, its second factors and its passkeys. It also removes its unused single sign-on tokens,
revokes its API keys permanently (revocation reason `ownerDeleted`, revoked by the caller),
ends its sessions and every impersonation of it, and removes its preferences. Audit records are
kept. A later account with the same username inherits nothing.

post.summary: Suspend a domain administrator's second factors
post.description:
Deactivates every TOTP, WebAuthn and Yubico OTP entry of the account until its next successful
password sign-in, which re-activates them, for example when a reseller lost their
authenticator. Passkeys are not affected. Suspending an account without active entries
succeeds and changes nothing. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key owned by
an administrator. Audited with the number of suspended entries.

post.summary: Issue a single sign-on token for a domain administrator
post.description:
Issues a token with which the domain administrator signs in once, within 30 seconds, without a
password and without a second factor, as reseller and billing panels do today through
`/api/v1` (`add/sso/domain-admin`). The panel redirects the user's browser to the legacy
domain administrator login (`/domainadmin?sso_token=<token>`) or to the new web app, which
submits it to `POST /session/sso-token`. The token is stored in mailcow's own token store, so
it works in both and only once. Issuing removes expired tokens.

Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key owned by an administrator. An inactive
account is refused with `409 account-inactive`, and no token is issued. Audited with the target
and the expiry, never the token.

post.summary: Sign in with a single sign-on token
post.description:
Signs in the domain administrator a token was issued for, without a password and without a
second factor, and consumes the token for this API and the legacy login alike. Tokens issued
through `/api/v1` work too. The token is valid only if it exists, is less than 30 seconds old,
and belongs to an active domain administrator account that existed when it was issued.

The session gets the domain administrator role and the sign-in method `ssoToken`. As after any
sign-in, the session identifier is renewed and forced password change or second-factor setup
restrict the session. A session the client already holds, including an impersonating one, is
replaced.

Failures return the generic `sign-in-failed` error, are audited and count towards sign-in
throttling per client address (`429` after 10 failures within 15 minutes). They are not
reported to fail2ban.

get.description:
Returns the impersonation of the caller's session: the impersonator, the impersonated account
and the start time. Without an active impersonation the answer is `404`. Available in
restricted sessions. Requests with an API key are refused with `session-required`.

post.description:
Makes the session act as another account (legacy "login as"), without signing in again.

- Administrators impersonate any mailbox user and any domain administrator.
- Domain administrators with the `loginAs` flag impersonate the mailbox users of domains
  assigned to them through an active assignment.
- Nobody impersonates an administrator, and a domain administrator never impersonates another
  domain administrator (`403 forbidden`). A domain administrator without `loginAs` gets
  `403 permission-flag-required` with `requiredFlags: [loginAs]`, checked before the target is looked
  up.
- Inactive targets and mailboxes in inactive domains are allowed, as in legacy. Resources,
  unknown accounts and mailboxes outside a domain administrator's domains answer `404`.

Only a full browser session may start one: API keys are refused with `session-required`, a
restricted session with `pending-action-required`, and a session that is already
impersonating with `409 already-impersonating`.

While impersonating, the session acts with the target's role and scope. The permission flags
are those legacy grants: an administrator gets every flag; a domain administrator gets every
mailbox user flag, except `syncjobs`, `quarantine`, `appPasswds`, `pushover` and `spamPolicy`,
and every domain administrator flag, which take its own current values. The target's forced
actions do not restrict the session, the impersonator's preferences stay in effect, and
managing the target's sign-in credentials or opening any webmail is refused with
`not-allowed-while-impersonating`. Every audit record names the impersonator as the actor and
the target as the impersonated account.

The session identifier and the anti-forgery token are renewed; the response carries the new
token and the new identity. The start is audited.

delete.description:
Returns the session to the impersonator, with the impersonator's original sign-in method. The
session identifier and the anti-forgery token are renewed. Audited. Without an active
impersonation the request succeeds and changes nothing. Available in restricted sessions.

Signing out (`DELETE /session`) during an impersonation ends the whole session, not only the
impersonation. An impersonation also ends automatically when the target is deleted or renamed,
leaves the impersonator's scope, or an impersonating domain administrator loses `loginAs`: the
next request is then refused with `impersonation-ended` and not carried out. Ending the
impersonation and signing out are the exceptions: they always succeed, also when they are the
request that detects the invalid impersonation, which is then ended and audited with its
reason.

post.summary: Open a mailbox's webmail on the user's behalf
post.description:
Grants the requesting browser a single-use webmail sign-in for a mailbox, so that a support
administrator sees what the user sees (legacy "SOGo" button). It uses the webmail hand-off of
feature 005 and records the legacy recent-login entry for webmail single sign-on (service `SSO`)
for the mailbox. The caller's session in this API is not changed.

Requires the server setting `ALLOW_ADMIN_EMAIL_LOGIN` (default off; otherwise
`webmail-on-behalf-disabled`). Administrators may open any mailbox; domain administrators with
the `loginAs` flag the mailboxes of their domains (without it: `permission-flag-required` with
`requiredFlags: [loginAs]`). Mailbox users are refused with `forbidden`. Only a full
browser session may do this: API keys are refused with `session-required`, and a session that
is impersonating another account with `not-allowed-while-impersonating`, whatever the target.
On a server without the groupware (`SKIP_SOGO=y`) the request is refused with feature 005's
`groupware-disabled`. A mailbox that cannot use webmail (inactive, login disabled, or in an
inactive domain) is refused with `notEligible` on `mailbox`. Audited, also when refused.

get.description:
Host name, time zone, architecture, installed version, current time, uptime, processor,
memory and swap of the mailcow host. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

**Freshness**: the host figures are at most 10 seconds old (`collectedAt`). Collection is shared
between clients, so more administrators polling do not measure the host more often. Poll every
5 seconds while the view is visible; there is no push channel.

Device, total, used and available space and used percentage of the disk holding the mail
storage, measured with `df -H` in the Dovecot container through mailcow's container service.
Values converted from rounded figures are marked `approximate`. When the measurement fails,
`measured` is `false` instead of zeros. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

**Freshness**: at most 60 seconds old (`collectedAt`), collected once for all clients.

get.summary: Look up the server's public addresses
get.description:
Asks mailcow's external check service for the server's public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, as
seen from outside. Only when the IP check of the legacy customisation settings is enabled
(`MonitoringCapabilities.ipCheckEnabled`); otherwise the request is refused with
`ip-check-disabled` and no outbound request is made. An address is `null` when the service does
not answer with a valid address of that family (10 seconds to connect, 15 seconds in total).
Not cached. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

Version tag, branch, and commit identifier and date when known, as the legacy UI shows them
(legacy `get/status/version`). Needs no container service. Administrators only, read-only keys
included.

Whether a newer mailcow release exists, with its tag, release page, publication time and release
notes, and the release notes of the installed version. The check is a server setting (on by
default, off in the FeldHost deployment) with a configurable release source and stable branch;
a disabled check, or an installation on another branch, reports `disabled` without any outbound
request. Successful checks are cached for 1 hour and failed checks for 5 minutes, per installed
version. Release notes are externally authored Markdown that clients must render safely.
Administrators only, read-only keys included.

Server settings and limits a client needs before it polls, pages or acts: whether the IP check
is enabled, the recommended polling interval and the maximum age of each kind of live data, the
retention of each log, the caller's own client address as this API sees it, and the bulk, rule
and list limits. Reflects the current configuration, contains no secret, changes nothing and
needs no container service. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

Lists the containers of this mailcow installation, including stopped ones, with their image,
state, health, start time, protected flag, role and available actions. Containers of other
projects on the same host are never listed. The antivirus scanner and the OLE scanner are hidden
when the configuration disables them, as in legacy. `q` searches the service name and the image.
Administrators only, read-only keys included.

**Freshness**: states are at most 5 seconds old (`collectedAt`), collected once for all clients.

parameters.name: running
parameters.description: Only running (`true`) or only not running (`false`) containers.

get.description:
One container by its service name. A container of another project, a hidden optional container
or an unknown name answers `404`. States are at most 5 seconds old. Administrators only,
read-only keys included.

Processor, memory, cumulative disk and network counters of a running container, and the disk
and network rates in bytes per second between the two newest samples. A container that is not
running is refused at once with `container-not-running`. Administrators only, read-only keys
included.

**Freshness**: poll every 5 seconds while the view is visible; the newest sample is then at most
15 seconds old. The first request after a pause answers within 5 seconds with one sample and
`null` rates; rates appear on the next request. Collection is shared between clients.

post.description:
Starts a container that is not running, retrying up to 4 attempts 1.5 seconds apart until it
runs, as legacy does. A running container is reported with `outcome: alreadyInState` and nothing
changes. Protected containers may be started. Needs an administrator session or a read-write
key owned by an administrator.

The response comes when the outcome is known, or after the container-service timeout (60
seconds by default): a timeout answers `outcome-unknown`, and the client reads the
container again. Exactly one audit record names the actor, the container, the action, the
outcome and the state before and after. When the audit log cannot be written before the action,
the request is refused with `temporary-failure` and nothing is done.

**Destructive**: the container's service is interrupted until it is started again. Clients
must ask for confirmation and name the container; the API needs no confirmation token.

Stops a running container, retrying up to 4 attempts 1.5 seconds apart, as legacy does. A
container that is not running is reported with `outcome: alreadyInState` and nothing changes.
Protected containers (by default the container service, the database, the key-value store, the
reverse proxy and this API's own container) are refused with `container-protected`. Needs an
administrator session or a read-write key owned by an administrator.

The response comes when the outcome is known, or after the container-service timeout (60
seconds by default): a timeout answers `outcome-unknown`. Exactly one audit record is
written, also for refusals. When the audit log cannot be written before the action, the request
is refused with `temporary-failure` and nothing is done.

**Destructive**: the container's service is interrupted while it restarts, and a graceful
restart can take a while. Clients must ask for confirmation and name the container; the API
needs no confirmation token.

Restarts the container whatever its state, which also starts a stopped container. Protected
containers may be restarted, except this API's own container (`container-protected`). Needs an
administrator session or a read-write key owned by an administrator.

The response comes after the restart completed, with the container's new start time, or after
the container-service timeout (60 seconds by default) with `outcome-unknown`.
Restarting the reverse proxy can drop the connection before the response arrives; read the
container again. Restarting the database or the key-value store delays the audit record until
it is reachable again; if it still cannot be written within the timeout, the response carries
`Audit-Recorded: false`. Exactly one audit record is written, also for refusals.

get.description:
The mail server log (Redis `POSTFIX_MAILLOG`): priority, severity class, program and message.
`q` searches the priority, program and message.

Administrators only, read-only keys included. Reads are not audited. Entries are returned as
mailcow retains them (see `MonitoringCapabilities.logRetention`); entries that cannot be parsed
are left out of the list and the total. Sorted by time, newest first by default; entries with
the same time keep the order in which mailcow stored them. `from` and `to` are inclusive. Text
filters match case-insensitively as substrings, and several values of one filter match entries
with any of them. To load older entries while new ones arrive, pass the `id` of the oldest entry
held as `before`.

get.summary: List the legacy API request log
get.description:
Requests to the legacy `/api/v1` (Redis `API_LOG`): URI, method, client address and the recorded
request data. **Secrets are masked**: the value of every field whose name contains `pass`,
`secret`, `private` or `token` (case-insensitive), or whose name is `key`, is replaced with `*`

parameters with the patterns of the legacy API request log (`pass`, `secret`, `private`, `token`,

Recent mailbox logins per service and client address (table `sasl_log`, cleaned daily by
mailcow): username, service, client address and whether an app password was used. Times are
converted from the server's time zone to UTC. Legacy web UI logins are reported with the service
label configured in feature 001, and filters match the reported label. `q` searches the username,
service and client address. The table records no storage order, so entries with the same time are
ordered by service, client address and username.

get.description:
The scan history Rspamd keeps (1,000 entries by default), read from the Rspamd controller at
request time: time, client address, senders, recipients, subject, action, score and required
score, symbols with their scores and options (largest positive scores first, then negative from
most negative, then zero), size, real and virtual scan time, message ID and authenticated user.
`q` searches the envelope and header senders and recipients, the subject, the client address,
the authenticated user and the message ID. `from`, `to`, `minScore` and `maxScore` are
inclusive. An unreachable controller answers `temporary-failure`. Administrators only,
read-only keys included.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only entries with one of these actions (exact Rspamd action names, case-insensitive).

parameters.name: minScore
parameters.description: Only entries with at least this score.

parameters.name: maxScore
parameters.description: Only entries with at most this score.

get.description:
Scanned and learned messages, spam and ham counts, the count per action as Rspamd names the
actions, connections, control connections, the Bayes statistics files and the fuzzy hashes per
storage, read from the Rspamd controller at request time. Fields Rspamd reports beyond these are
not passed through. The merged action chart of the legacy dashboard is feature 006's. An
unreachable controller answers `temporary-failure`. Administrators only, read-only keys
included.

The messages in Postfix's queues, read at request time (`postqueue -j` through mailcow's
container service): queue ID, queue, arrival time, size, sender, recipients with their deferral
reasons, and the forced-expiry mark when Postfix reports it. The listing covers at most the first
10,000 messages Postfix reports, as legacy does; `meta.truncated` says when it reported more, and
`meta.queueCounts` counts every message per queue, independent of filters and paging. `q`
searches the queue ID, sender, recipients and deferral reasons. `from` and `to` filter the
arrival time, inclusive. A stopped Postfix container answers `mail-service-not-running`.
Administrators only, read-only keys included.

parameters.name: queue
parameters.description: Only messages in these queues. Repeat the parameter for several.

parameters.name: sender
parameters.description: Only messages whose sender contains one of these values (case-insensitive).

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Only messages with a recipient address that contains one of these values (case-insensitive).

post.description:
Applies one action to 1 to 1,000 queued messages (`MailQueueBulkRequest`: `action` and
`targets`, the legacy Queue Manager's mass actions):

- `deliver`: asks Postfix to attempt immediate delivery (`postqueue -i`, legacy "Deliver"). The
  response comes once Postfix has accepted the request; delivery continues in the background and
  shows in later listings. Held messages stay on hold. The container service asks Postfix once
  per message, so a large selection can reach the container-service timeout; to retry everything
  that is not on hold, flush the queue instead.
- `hold`: moves the messages to the hold queue (`postsuper -h`). Holding a held message is `done`
  without change.
- `release`: returns held messages to the queue for delivery (`postsuper -H`, legacy "Unhold").
  Releasing a message that is not on hold is `done` without change.
- `delete`: **destructive and irreversible**: deletes the messages from every queue, including
  the hold queue (`postsuper -d`). Clients must ask for confirmation and name the number of
  messages; the API needs no confirmation token.

Hold, release and delete complete before the response. Each distinct queue ID gets one result,
in request order: `done`, or `notFound` when the message is not in the queue when the request
is processed; a missing ID never stops the others. Queued messages have no version tag, so
targets carry only `id`. More than 1,000 IDs or a non-hexadecimal ID refuses the whole request
(`422`) and nothing changes. A stopped Postfix container answers `mail-service-not-running`; a
Postfix failure answers `queue-action-failed` (nothing is reported per ID); a container-service
timeout answers `outcome-unknown` with `step` = the action. Needs an administrator session or a
read-write key owned by an administrator.

The request writes **one** audit record (event `mailQueueDelivery`, `mailQueueHold`,
`mailQueueRelease` or `mailQueueDeletion`) that lists every ID with its result; queued messages
are transient system objects, the documented exception to one record per object. Refusals are
audited too. When the audit log cannot be written before the action, the request is refused
with `temporary-failure` and nothing is done. When the record cannot be written after the
action, the response carries the header `Audit-Recorded: false` (declared on the shared
`BulkResultResponse`).

get.description:
The complete content of one queued message as Postfix shows it (`postcat -q`): envelope
records, headers and body. Queued mail contains personal data: **every view is audited** with
the queue ID, never the content, including views of a message that already left the queue
(`404`). Administrators only; a read-only key owned by an administrator may view content too.

post.description:
Asks Postfix to attempt delivery of every queued message that is not on hold (`postqueue -f`,
legacy "Flush queue"). The response comes once Postfix has accepted the request; delivery
continues in the background and shows in later listings. Held messages stay on hold. A stopped
Postfix container answers `mail-service-not-running`. Needs an administrator session or a
read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited; when the audit log cannot be written before
the action, it is refused with `temporary-failure`.

**Destructive and irreversible**: every queued message in every queue, including the hold queue,
is deleted and never delivered (`postsuper -d ALL`, legacy "Delete all"). Clients must ask for
confirmation and should name the number of queued messages (`meta.queueCounts.total` of the
listing); the API needs no confirmation token.

Completes before the response. A stopped Postfix container answers `mail-service-not-running`.
Needs an administrator session or a read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited; when the
audit log cannot be written before the action, it is refused with `temporary-failure`.

get.description:
Ban time and maximum ban time, growing ban time, maximum attempts and retry window, IPv4 and
IPv6 prefix lengths, external enforcement, the allowlist and denylist, the ban list ID and its
public address, and the version tag. When the ban service never stored settings, its defaults
are reported (`stored: false`). Administrators only, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
JSON Merge Patch: send only what changes. Omitted values keep their value, and a list that is
sent replaces the whole list. Out-of-range values and invalid list entries refuse the whole
request with `422`, naming each field or entry and its rule; nothing is corrected and nothing
changes. The parameters and both lists are stored together or not at all.

**When changes take effect**: the ban service applies the parameters at its next ban decision
and at least every 10 seconds, and the allowlist and denylist within 60 seconds, without a
restart; host names are resolved each time. A permanent ban is lifted by removing its entry from
the denylist. When the ban service is not running, the change is saved and takes effect once it
runs (`banServiceRunning: false`).

`If-Match` is optional; interactive clients should always send the version tag they read, which
ignores the ban service's own rewrites of unchanged values. Needs an administrator session or a
read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited with each changed parameter (old and new) and
the list entries added and removed.

post.description:
**Destructive**: external firewalls that use the old public ban list address stop receiving the
ban list immediately. Clients must ask for confirmation; the API needs no confirmation token.

Stores a new random ban list ID (UUID) and returns the settings with the new ID and address
(legacy `edit/fail2ban/banlist`). The public ban list endpoint itself stays in the legacy stack.
`If-Match` takes the settings' version tag and is optional. Interactive clients should always send the
version tag they read. Needs an administrator session or a
read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited without either ID.

get.description:
The ordered patterns that recognise failed logins in mailcow's logs, numbered from 1, and their
version tag. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

put.description:
Replaces the rules as a whole with 1 to 100 rules, numbered from 1 in the order given. Each rule
must compile in the ban service's regular-expression dialect (Python `re`) and contain a capture
group whose first group captures the client address. An invalid rule refuses the request with
`422`, naming it, and the stored rules stay unchanged. The ban service uses the new rules from
the next log line, without a restart. `If-Match` is optional. Interactive clients should always send the
version tag they read. Needs an administrator session or
a read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited with the old and new rules.

post.summary: Reset the ban rules to mailcow's defaults
post.description:
**Destructive**: the custom rules are discarded and the ban service is restarted, which briefly
interrupts banning. Clients must ask for confirmation; the API needs no confirmation token.

Removes the stored rules, restarts the ban service through mailcow's container service, and
waits up to 10 seconds after the restart for the ban service to store mailcow's default rules,
which it then returns. If they have not appeared in time, the request fails with
`ban-rules-not-restored`: the ban service stores them with the next log line it receives.
`If-Match` takes the rules' version tag and is optional. Interactive clients should always send the
version tag they read. Needs an administrator session or a
read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited with the old and new rules; when the audit log
cannot be written before the reset, it is refused with `temporary-failure` and nothing is done.

get.description:
The networks the ban service banned after failed logins, with the first address, the end of the
ban, the remaining seconds and whether the ban is queued for lifting. Read at request time. `q`
searches the network. Administrators only, read-only keys included.

parameters.name: queuedForLifting
parameters.description: Only bans that are (`true`) or are not (`false`) queued for lifting.

post.description:
Queues the ban for lifting (legacy "Unban"). The ban service lifts it within about 10 seconds
while it runs; until then it is listed with `queuedForLifting: true`. When the ban service is not
running, the lift stays queued.

Only for an active ban: a network that is not actively banned (including a ban that expired
meanwhile) answers `404`. No version tag is needed, because the action adds or removes single
entries. Needs an administrator session or a read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited
with the network and the list changes.

post.summary: Lift an active ban and allowlist its network
post.description:
Adds the network to the allowlist, removes it from the denylist and queues the ban for lifting
(legacy "Whitelist"), in one atomic change. The ban service lifts the ban within about 10 seconds
and applies the allowlist within 60 seconds. When the allowlist already holds 10,000 entries the
request is refused (`422`, `tooMany` on `network`).

Only for an active ban: a network that is not actively banned (including a ban that expired
meanwhile) answers `404`. No version tag is needed, because the action adds or removes single
entries. Needs an administrator session or a read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited
with the network and the list changes.

post.summary: Denylist the network of an active ban
post.description:
Adds the network to the denylist and removes it from the allowlist (legacy "Blacklist"), in one
atomic change, with the denylist rules of `PATCH /fail2ban/settings` (`reserved` on the key
`network`, or `tooMany` when the denylist already holds 10,000 entries). The ban service enforces the denylist entry as a permanent ban within 60 seconds,
without a restart. Clients should warn when the network covers the caller's own address.

Only for an active ban: a network that is not actively banned (including a ban that expired
meanwhile) answers `404`. No version tag is needed, because the action adds or removes single
entries. Needs an administrator session or a read-write key owned by an administrator. Audited
with the network and the list changes.

get.description:
The bans the ban service applies for denylist entries, with the first address and the time the
ban started. A permanent ban is lifted by removing its entry from the denylist
(`PATCH /fail2ban/settings`). `q` searches the network. Administrators only, read-only keys
included.

Lists relayhosts with their usage, as the legacy "System › Routing" screen does. Administrators
only, with a session or a key (read-only keys included); domain administrators use
`listRelayhostChoices`. Passwords are never included. `q` searches the host and the username.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) relayhosts.

parameters.name: inUse
parameters.description: Only relayhosts assigned (`true`) or not assigned (`false`) to any domain or mailbox.

post.description:
Creates a relayhost, active unless `active: false` is sent. Administrators only. The response
shows the username and whether a password is set, never the password. Audited without the
password.

get.description:
Lists every relayhost with only its identifier, host, username and active state, for the
relayhost selectors of the domain and mailbox screens, which legacy labels
`ID n: host (username)`. Administrators, and domain administrators who hold the
`domainRelayhost` or the `mailboxRelayhost` permission flag (otherwise
`403 permission-flag-required`). Passwords, password states and usage are never included.
Read-only keys may use it. `q` searches the host.

post.summary: Apply an action to several relayhosts
post.description:
Activates, deactivates or deletes up to 100 relayhosts in one request, as the legacy mass
actions do. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key; any other caller is
refused as a whole (`403`). More than 100 targets are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany` on
`targets`, with `max: 100`).

Otherwise each distinct relayhost is processed on its own, with the checks, side effects and
audit record of the single operation, and gets one result in request order: `done` (with the
new version tag unless deleted), `notFound`, `refused`, `outdated` (the target's `version` no
longer matches; unchanged) or `failed`. Targets without `version` are not version-checked. A
target named twice is processed once. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description: Returns one relayhost with its usage and version tag. Administrators only.

patch.description:
Changes the host, the username, the password or the active state. Administrators only.
Omitted members keep their values; an omitted password is kept and `""` removes it. Changes
apply to the next message, without any service reload. Audited; a password change is recorded
only as "set", "changed" or "removed".

delete.description:
Deletes the relayhost, whether or not it is in use. In the same step, every domain and mailbox
assigned to it loses its assignment (their mail is then delivered directly, or through the
domain's relayhost for a mailbox). Administrators only. The audit record lists the cleared
domains and mailboxes.

get.summary: List the domains and mailboxes using a relayhost
get.description:
Lists the domains and mailboxes assigned to the relayhost (legacy "in use by"). Administrators
only. `q` searches the name.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only domains or only mailboxes.

post.description:
Connects to the relayhost's host with its stored credentials and sends a short test message, as
the legacy "Test" dialog does (see `RoutingConnectionTestResult`). Inactive relayhosts can be
tested. The test sends a real message to the recipient, so it is a state-changing request: it
needs a session with the anti-forgery token or a read-write key, and it is audited (sender,
recipient, outcome and step, never the transcript). It answers within about 60 seconds.
Administrators only.

get.description:
Returns the relayhost assigned to the domain, with its host and state, or `null`.
Administrators for every domain; domain administrators for their own domains, without a
permission flag. An alias domain name answers `404`: alias domains follow their target domain.

put.description:
Assigns an existing relayhost to the domain, or none (`null`). Mail sent from the domain and its
alias domains then leaves through that relayhost while it is active; mailboxes with their own
active relayhost keep it. Only the assignment changes (and the domain's modification time), so
the domain's version tag in the domains API changes too. No service is reloaded.

Administrators for every domain. Domain administrators for their own domains, only with the
`domainRelayhost` permission flag (otherwise `403 permission-flag-required`, checked before the
domain is looked up). Audited, including refused attempts.

get.description:
Returns the mailbox's own relayhost, its domain's relayhost, the relayhost the mail server
connects to for mail from the mailbox, and the relayhost whose credentials it sends.
Administrators for every mailbox; domain administrators for the mailboxes of their own domains,
without a permission flag. Resources and alias-domain addresses answer `404`.

put.description:
Assigns an existing relayhost to the mailbox, or none (`null`). It applies to mail sent from the
mailbox's own address and from aliases whose only destination is the mailbox, not to its
addresses in alias domains, and it overrides the domain's relayhost for the host the mail server
connects to (see `MailboxRelayhostAssignment` for the credential lookup order). Only the
assignment changes (and the mailbox's modification time), so the mailbox's version tag in the
mailboxes API changes too.

Administrators for every mailbox. Domain administrators for the mailboxes of their own domains,
only with the `mailboxRelayhost` permission flag (otherwise `403 permission-flag-required`,
checked before the mailbox is looked up). Audited, including refused attempts.

get.description:
Lists transport map entries. Administrators only, with a session or a key (read-only keys
included). Passwords are never included. `q` searches the destination, the next hop and the
username.

parameters.name: nextHop
parameters.description:
Only transports with exactly this next hop, compared without regard to letter case: the
transports that share one set of credentials. The value is normalised like a stored next
hop (a bare IP address is put in brackets, a Unicode host name converted to ASCII).

post.description:
Creates a transport with one destination, inactive unless `active: true` is sent.
Administrators only. See `TransportCreateRequest` for how credentials are shared with existing
transports of the same next hop. Duplicate destinations, a different username for an existing
next hop and interfering next hops are refused with `409`. Audited without the password.

post.summary: Apply an action to several transports
post.description:
Activates, deactivates or deletes up to 100 transports in one request, as the legacy mass
actions do. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key; any other caller is
refused as a whole (`403`). More than 100 targets are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany`).

Each distinct transport is otherwise processed on its own, with the checks and audit record of
the single operation: `done`, `notFound`, `refused`, `outdated` or `failed`. Targets without
`version` are not version-checked. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description: Returns one transport with its version tag. Administrators only.

patch.description:
Changes the destination, next hop, MX-based flag, credentials or active state, validated as at
creation (see `TransportPatch` for the shared credentials). Administrators only. All changes of
the request, including credential changes on other transports, are stored together. Audited,
naming the other transports whose credentials changed.

delete.description:
Deletes only this transport; other transports of its next hop keep their credentials.
Administrators only. Audited.

post.description:
Connects to the transport's next hop with its stored credentials and sends a short test message,
as the legacy transport check does (see `RoutingConnectionTestResult`). Inactive transports can
be tested. A state-changing, audited request (session with anti-forgery token or read-write
key). It answers within about 60 seconds. Administrators only.

get.description:
Lists the BCC maps in the caller's scope. Administrators see all maps, including orphaned ones
whose domain no longer exists. Domain administrators see the maps of their domains and of those
domains' alias domains, without a permission flag, and never orphaned maps. Read-only keys may
list. `q` searches the local and the BCC destination.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only maps of these domains or alias domains (ASCII or Unicode). Repeat for several; any matches.

parameters.name: orphaned
parameters.description: Only orphaned (`true`) or not orphaned (`false`) maps. Domain administrators never see orphaned maps.

post.description:
Creates a BCC map, active unless `active: false` is sent. Administrators, and domain
administrators with the `bccMaps` permission flag for local destinations in their scope
(otherwise `403 permission-flag-required`). A local destination that does not exist and one
outside the caller's scope get the same validation error. A second map of the same type for the
same local destination is refused (`409 routing-entry-exists`). Audited.

get.description:
Lists the local destinations that `createBccMap` accepts from the caller: domains, alias
domains, mailboxes, aliases (not catch-alls, not mailboxes' own aliases) and mailbox addresses
in alias domains, each within the caller's scope. Administrators and domain administrators,
without a permission flag; read-only keys may use it. `q` searches the value.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only these kinds. Repeat for several.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only values of these domains or alias domains. Repeat for several.

post.summary: Apply an action to several BCC maps
post.description:
Activates, deactivates, switches the type of, or deletes up to 100 BCC maps in one request, as
the legacy mass actions do. Administrators, and domain administrators with the `bccMaps`
permission flag; any other caller is refused as a whole (`403`). More than 100 targets are
refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany`).

Each distinct map is otherwise processed on its own, with the checks and audit record of the
single operation: `done`, `notFound` (also for maps outside the caller's scope), `refused` (for
example `routing-entry-exists` when a type switch would duplicate another map), `outdated` or
`failed`. Targets without `version` are not version-checked. Every audit record carries the
`bulkRequestId`.

get.description:
Returns one BCC map in the caller's scope with its version tag. A map outside the caller's scope
answers `404`, exactly like one that does not exist.

patch.description:
Changes the type, the BCC destination or the active state. The local destination and the domain
are read-only. Administrators, and domain administrators with the `bccMaps` permission flag
(otherwise `403 permission-flag-required`), for maps in their scope. Audited.

delete.description:
Deletes the map. Administrators (also orphaned maps), and domain administrators with the
`bccMaps` permission flag for maps in their scope. Audited.

get.description:
Lists recipient maps. Administrators only, with a session or a key (read-only keys included).
`q` searches the original and the new destination.

post.description:
Creates a recipient map, active unless `active: false` is sent. Administrators only. The mail
server rewrites matching envelope recipients before delivery, also when the original
destination is a mailbox. A second map for the same original destination is refused
(`409 routing-entry-exists`). Audited.

post.summary: Apply an action to several recipient maps
post.description:
Activates, deactivates or deletes up to 100 recipient maps in one request, as the legacy mass
actions do. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key; any other caller is
refused as a whole (`403`). More than 100 targets are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany`).

Each distinct entry is otherwise processed on its own, with the checks and audit record of the
single operation: `done`, `notFound`, `refused`, `outdated` or `failed`. Targets without
`version` are not version-checked. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description: Returns one recipient map with its version tag. Administrators only.

patch.description:
Changes the original destination, the new destination or the active state, normalised as at
creation. Administrators only. Audited.

delete.description: Deletes the recipient map. Administrators only. Audited.

get.description:
Lists TLS policy maps. Administrators only, with a session or a key (read-only keys included).
`q` searches the destination and the parameters.

parameters.name: policy
parameters.description: Only these policies. Repeat for several; any matches.

post.description:
Creates a TLS policy map, active unless `active: false` is sent. Administrators only. A second
entry for the same destination (compared without regard to letter case) is refused
(`409 routing-entry-exists`). Audited.

post.summary: Apply an action to several TLS policy maps
post.description:
Activates, deactivates or deletes up to 100 TLS policy maps in one request, as the legacy mass
actions do. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key; any other caller is
refused as a whole (`403`). More than 100 targets are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany`).

Each distinct entry is otherwise processed on its own, with the checks and audit record of the
single operation: `done`, `notFound`, `refused`, `outdated` or `failed`. Targets without
`version` are not version-checked. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description: Returns one TLS policy map with its version tag. Administrators only.

patch.description:
Changes the destination, the policy, the parameters or the active state, with the rules of
creation. Administrators only. Audited.

delete.description: Deletes the TLS policy map. Administrators only. Audited.

get.description:
Lists the forwarding hosts stored in mailcow's Redis. Administrators only, with a session or a
key (read-only keys included). `q` searches the address and the source.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Only entries with exactly this source, for example all addresses added for one host name.

post.description:
Adds an address or prefix, or resolves a host name and adds every resulting address (see
`ForwardingHostCreateRequest`), with the spam filter enabled unless `spamFilter: false` is sent.
All addresses are stored together or not at all. Addresses already listed are updated with the
new source and spam filter setting. Answers `201` when at least one address was added and `200`
when all were already listed. A name without addresses is refused (`422`, `notResolvable`); a
temporary DNS failure or an unavailable Redis answers `503` and changes nothing.
Administrators only. Audited with every address and its outcome.

post.summary: Apply an action to several forwarding hosts
post.description:
Enables or disables the spam filter of, or deletes, up to 100 forwarding hosts in one request,
as the legacy mass actions do. Administrators only, with a session or a read-write key; any
other caller is refused as a whole (`403`). More than 100 targets are refused as a whole
(`422`, `tooMany`). An unavailable Redis gives each item `failed` with `temporary-failure`.

Each distinct entry is otherwise processed on its own, with the checks and audit record of the
single operation: `done`, `notFound`, `outdated` or `failed`. Targets without `version` are not
version-checked. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description: Returns one forwarding host by its stored address, with its version tag. Administrators only.

patch.summary: Change a forwarding host's spam filter
patch.description:
Enables or disables the spam filter of the entry. With it disabled, spam from the host is
accepted and delivered like other mail. The address and the source are read-only.
Administrators only. Audited.

delete.description: Removes the address and its spam filter setting together. Administrators only. Audited.

get.description:
Returns the server settings and limits clients need before they submit routing changes, for
example the default test addresses that the web app shows as placeholders. Administrators get
every value; domain administrators get the bulk limit, the page sizes and the BCC field limits
(`administration: null`). Read on every request from the current configuration. Read-only keys
may use it.

Lists the quarantine items in the caller's scope, newest first by default. Every role may list
whatever its permission flags (the `quarantine` flag gates only the actions):
- administrators: every item;
- domain administrators: items whose recipient mailbox belongs to a domain they manage
  (recipient domain), including items of mailboxes that no longer exist;
- mailbox users: items addressed to their own mailbox.

`q` searches, case-insensitively and as a substring, the subject, the envelope sender, the
recipient and the queue identifier. Neither the stored message nor the quick-action hash is
ever returned.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Only items for this recipient mailbox (case-insensitive exact match).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only items whose recipient is in this domain (ASCII or Unicode form).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only items with one of these actions. Repeat the parameter for several.

parameters.name: virus
parameters.description: Only items with (`true`) or without (`false`) the virus flag.

parameters.name: notified
parameters.description: Only items that a notification already included (`true`) or not (`false`).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only items that arrived at or after this time.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only items that arrived before this time.

parameters.name: minScore
parameters.description: Only items with a score of at least this value (items without a score are left out).

parameters.name: maxScore
parameters.description: Only items with a score of at most this value (items without a score are left out).

post.summary: Apply an action to several quarantine items
post.description:
Releases (with or without learning), learns as spam or deletes up to the bulk limit of items
(100) in one request, as the legacy quarantine page's mass actions do. The whole
request is refused (`403`) only when the caller's role, flags or key scope never allow the
action: domain administrators and mailbox users need `quarantine`, and read-only keys are
refused. More targets than the limit are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany` on `targets`,
with the limit as `max`).

Otherwise each distinct item is processed on its own, in request order, with the checks, side
effects and audit record of the single operation, and gets one result:
- `done`: carried out; `report` gives each step of a release or learning as spam;
- `notFound`: the item does not exist or is outside the caller's scope;
- `refused`: `quarantine-item-busy` or `quarantine-delivery-refused` (the item is kept);
- `outdated`: the target's `version` no longer matches (`412` problem); the item is unchanged;
- `failed`: an unexpected or downstream failure, for example `temporary-failure` (the item is
  kept).

Targets without `version` are not version-checked. A failure on one item does not stop or undo
the others. Every audit record carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.description:
Administrators receive every setting (`visibility: full`), with the effective defaults of
unset values: retention 0, maximum size 0 (inactive), no notification score limit, maximum
age 365 days, release format `original`, sender `quarantine@localhost`, subject "Spam
Quarantine Notification", no copy or redirect recipient, and the default template.

Domain administrators and mailbox users receive only whether the quarantine is active, the
retention per mailbox and the maximum message size (`visibility: public`), as the legacy
quarantine page shows them. Read-only keys may read. Values saved through the legacy UI are
returned by the next request.

patch.description:
Changes the settings sent and keeps the others (JSON Merge Patch). Administrators only
(`forbidden` for other roles). The values are stored where the legacy quarantine ingestion,
notifier and cleanup read them, atomically: on any invalid value, an outdated `If-Match` or an
unavailable shared store, nothing changes. Invalid values are refused with field errors; unlike
legacy, nothing is silently corrected.

A non-empty `notificationTemplate` is checked the way the legacy notifier uses it (see
`QuarantineSettingsPatch`). With `validateOnly=true`, every rule is applied, including
`If-Match` and the template check, but nothing is stored and nothing is audited; success answers
`200` with `{"data": {"valid": true}}`.

Audited with each changed value (old and new); the template is recorded only as changed, with
its old and new sizes.

200.description:
The changed settings (`QuarantineSettings`, with the `ETag` header), or with
`validateOnly=true` the validation result.

ETag.description: Version tag of the changed settings, equal to `data.etag`. Absent with `validateOnly=true`.

post.description:
Renders the given template, or the stored one (or the default) when none is given, with the
documented sample data, exactly as the legacy notifier would, and returns the rendered HTML as
text, the plain-text version the notifier derives from it, and the subject. Administrators
only. A template the notifier cannot use is refused with the same validation error as on save
(`invalidTemplate` on `template`).

**Clients must show `html` only as source text, never as live HTML.** The preview changes
nothing and is not audited. It is a `POST` because it carries a template, so read-only keys are
refused like for any `POST`.

get.description:
Returns one item in the caller's scope (see `listQuarantineItems`) with the spam filter's
symbols, fuzzy hashes, the sending server's address, the stored size and the parsed content:
headers, recipients, the plain-text part and the HTML part converted to plain text. HTML is
never returned.

Attachment details are returned only to callers who may download attachments: administrators,
domain administrators, and mailbox users with `quarantineAttachments`; for others
`content.attachments` is `null`. `authenticatedSender` is returned to administrators only.

A stored message larger than the content size limit (10 MiB by default) is not parsed:
`contentStatus` is `tooLarge` and `content` is `null`. Reading an item changes nothing and is
not audited.

delete.description:
Removes the item permanently without calling the spam filter (legacy "Remove"). Needs the
`quarantine` flag for domain administrators and mailbox users (`permission-flag-required`
otherwise). An item is released, learned or deleted by at most one request of this API: while
another request processes it, the answer is `409 quarantine-item-busy`, and afterwards `404`.
The item's notification state is never changed; quick links already sent for it stop working.
Audited (queue identifier, recipient and envelope sender; never the subject or content).

post.summary: Release a quarantine item to its mailbox
post.description:
Delivers the stored message to the item's recipient mailbox through mailcow's internal mail
submission that bypasses the spam filter (Postfix port 590), in the configured release format
(`QuarantineReleaseFormat`; `original` when none is stored). The envelope sender is the stored
sender, or `sender-unknown@rspamd` when none is stored. Needs the `quarantine` flag for domain
administrators and mailbox users.

Steps, reported in the response:
1. **Delivery.** When the mail server accepts the message, the item is removed. When it refuses
   it permanently, the item is kept, nothing is learned and the answer is
   `409 quarantine-delivery-refused` with the server's answer. When it cannot be reached, times
   out or answers temporarily, the same applies with `503 temporary-failure`
   (`dependency: mailServer`, `step: delivery`).
2. **Learning** (unless `learnAsHam` is `false`, the legacy quick release): the spam filter
   learns the message as ham, then stores its fuzzy hashes as wanted (flag 13). "Already
   learned" counts as success, and "no content to generate fuzzy hashes" is reported as
   skipped. A learning failure is reported in the response and never undoes the release.

An item is released, learned or deleted by at most one request of this API: while another
request processes it, the answer is `409 quarantine-item-busy`, and afterwards `404`. The
legacy UI does not take part in this protection. Audited, with the outcome of each step.

post.summary: Learn a quarantine item as spam and remove it
post.description:
Asks the spam filter to learn the message as spam, then to store its fuzzy hashes as unwanted
(flag 11), then removes the item (legacy "Learn as spam and delete"). Needs the `quarantine`
flag for domain administrators and mailbox users.

The item is removed only after the spam learning succeeded or was answered "already learned".
When the spam filter cannot be reached, times out (30 s) or refuses to learn, the item is kept
and the answer is `503 temporary-failure` (`dependency: spamFilter`, `step: learning`). A
failure of the fuzzy step is reported in the response and does not keep the item.

An item is released, learned or deleted by at most one request of this API (`409
quarantine-item-busy` while another one runs, `404` afterwards). Audited, with the outcome of
each step.

get.description:
Returns the stored message as an e-mail file to save. Administrators may always download it;
domain administrators need `quarantine`; mailbox users need `quarantine` and
`quarantineAttachments`, because the file contains the attachments
(`permission-flag-required` names a missing flag in `requiredFlags`, `quarantine` first). A message larger than the content size
limit is refused with `409 quarantine-message-too-large`. Read-only keys may download. Not
audited.

get.summary: Download one attachment of a quarantined message
get.description:
Returns the decoded attachment at `position` as a file to save, never to display. Allowed for
administrators, domain administrators, and mailbox users with `quarantineAttachments`
(`permission-flag-required` with `requiredFlags: [quarantineAttachments]` otherwise). An unknown position answers `404`. A message larger
than the content size limit is refused with `409 quarantine-message-too-large`. Read-only keys
may download. Not audited.

Returns the limits and server settings that clients need before they submit quarantine, spam
policy and rate limit requests: the bulk limit, the page sizes, the content size limit, the
spam score range, the allow and block list pattern rules, the rate limit range, the limits of
the quarantine settings and whether virus scanning is enabled. Every role may read it,
read-only keys included. It changes nothing.

post.summary: Set the quarantine notifications of several mailboxes
post.description:
Sets the frequency, the category, or both, for up to the bulk limit of mailboxes (100),
as the legacy mailbox list's mass actions do. Administrators and domain
administrators only (`forbidden` for mailbox users); read-only keys are refused. More targets
than the limit are refused as a whole (`422`, `tooMany` on `targets`).

Otherwise each distinct mailbox is processed on its own and gets one result: `done` (with the
new version tag in `version`), `notFound` (not a mailbox, a resource, or outside the caller's
scope), `outdated` (the target's `version` no longer matches) or `failed`. Every audit record
carries the `bulkRequestId`.

get.summary: Read a mailbox's quarantine notification settings
get.description:
Returns how often and for which items the mailbox user is notified about new quarantine items.
Administrators: every mailbox; domain administrators: mailboxes of their domains; mailbox
users: their own mailbox. Other mailboxes, and resources, answer `404`.

patch.summary: Change a mailbox's quarantine notification settings
patch.description:
Changes the frequency, the category, or both, in the mailbox's attributes, where the legacy
notifier reads them. A mailbox user needs `quarantineNotification` to change the frequency and
`quarantineCategory` to change the category: a member that would change without its flag is
refused with `attribute-not-permitted` (`attributes`, `requiredFlags`), while a member sent with
its current value is accepted. Administrators and domain administrators always may. The notifier applies the change
at its next run; the time of the last notification and the items' notification state are not
reset. Audited with the old and new values.

get.summary: List the allow and block lists of a domain
get.description:
Returns the domain's own entries (`own: true`, owner kind `domain`) and, read-only, the
entries of the mailboxes of the domain (`own: false`, owner kind `mailbox`), as the legacy
domain page shows them. `q` searches the pattern.

Administrators: every domain; domain administrators: the domains they manage. Mailbox users are
refused (`forbidden`).

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Only entries of this list.

parameters.name: ownership
parameters.description: Only the owner's own entries (`own`) or only the related, read-only ones (`inherited`).

post.summary: Add an entry to the allow or block list of a domain
post.description:
Adds a pattern to the allow or block list (`SpamPolicyEntryCreateRequest`). The pattern is
trimmed and lower-cased before it is checked and stored. The same pattern on either list of
the same owner is refused with `409 spam-policy-entry-exists`, which names the list and the
existing entry. The spam filter applies the entry within one refresh of its settings map (at
most 1 minute). Administrators may always add; domain administrators need `spamPolicy`; mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`). Audited on the owner (audit target `domain`), with the entry's `entryId`, `list` and `pattern` in the details.

get.summary: Read one allow or block list entry of a domain
get.description:
Returns one entry that belongs to a domain. An entry of another owner answers `404`, even when it is
shown read-only in this owner's list.

delete.summary: Remove an allow or block list entry of a domain
delete.description:
Removes the entry through its owner. An entry of another owner, such as a domain entry
addressed through one of its mailboxes, answers `404`. Administrators may always remove; domain administrators need `spamPolicy`; mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`). The spam filter stops applying it
within one refresh of its settings map (at most 1 minute). Audited on the owner (audit
target `domain`), with the entry's `entryId`, `list` and `pattern` in the details.
