get.summary: List the allow and block lists of an alias domain
get.description:
Returns the alias domain's own entries (owner kind `aliasDomain`). They apply to mail for
the alias domain only. `q` searches the pattern.

Administrators: every alias domain; domain administrators: the alias domains of the domains
they manage. Mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`).

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Only entries of this list.

parameters.name: ownership
parameters.description: Only the owner's own entries (`own`) or only the related, read-only ones (`inherited`).

post.summary: Add an entry to the allow or block list of an alias domain
post.description:
Adds a pattern to the allow or block list (`SpamPolicyEntryCreateRequest`). The pattern is
trimmed and lower-cased before it is checked and stored. The same pattern on either list of
the same owner is refused with `409 spam-policy-entry-exists`, which names the list and the
existing entry. The spam filter applies the entry within one refresh of its settings map (at
most 1 minute). Administrators may always add; domain administrators need `spamPolicy`; mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`). Audited on the owner (audit target `aliasDomain`), with the entry's `entryId`, `list` and `pattern` in the details.

get.summary: Read one allow or block list entry of an alias domain
get.description:
Returns one entry that belongs to an alias domain. An entry of another owner answers `404`, even when it is
shown read-only in this owner's list.

delete.summary: Remove an allow or block list entry of an alias domain
delete.description:
Removes the entry through its owner. An entry of another owner, such as a domain entry
addressed through one of its mailboxes, answers `404`. Administrators may always remove; domain administrators need `spamPolicy`; mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`). The spam filter stops applying it
within one refresh of its settings map (at most 1 minute). Audited on the owner (audit
target `aliasDomain`), with the entry's `entryId`, `list` and `pattern` in the details.

get.summary: List the allow and block lists of a mailbox
get.description:
Returns the mailbox's own entries (`own: true`) and, read-only, the entries of the mailbox's
domain (`own: false`, owner kind `domain`, "inherited"), as the legacy user page shows them.
`q` searches the pattern.

Administrators: every mailbox; domain administrators: mailboxes of their domains; mailbox
users: their own mailbox. Resources answer `404`.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Only entries of this list.

parameters.name: ownership
parameters.description: Only the owner's own entries (`own`) or only the related, read-only ones (`inherited`).

post.summary: Add an entry to the allow or block list of a mailbox
post.description:
Adds a pattern to the allow or block list (`SpamPolicyEntryCreateRequest`). The pattern is
trimmed and lower-cased before it is checked and stored. The same pattern on either list of
the same owner is refused with `409 spam-policy-entry-exists`, which names the list and the
existing entry. The spam filter applies the entry within one refresh of its settings map (at
most 1 minute). Administrators may always add; domain administrators and mailbox users need `spamPolicy`. Audited on the owner (audit target `mailbox`), with the entry's `entryId`, `list` and `pattern` in the details.

get.summary: Read one allow or block list entry of a mailbox
get.description:
Returns one entry that belongs to a mailbox. An entry of another owner answers `404`, even when it is
shown read-only in this owner's list.

delete.summary: Remove an allow or block list entry of a mailbox
delete.description:
Removes the entry through its owner. An entry of another owner, such as a domain entry
addressed through one of its mailboxes, answers `404`. Administrators may always remove; domain administrators and mailbox users need `spamPolicy`. The spam filter stops applying it
within one refresh of its settings map (at most 1 minute). Audited on the owner (audit
target `mailbox`), with the entry's `entryId`, `list` and `pattern` in the details.

get.description:
Returns the junk and reject scores in effect, whether they are custom, and the server defaults
(the spam filter's "add header" and "reject" thresholds, or 5 and 15 marked `fallback` when the
filter cannot be asked or a threshold is not configured). Administrators: every mailbox;
domain administrators: mailboxes of their domains; mailbox users: their own mailbox. Resources
and other mailboxes answer `404`.

put.summary: Set a mailbox's custom spam score
put.description:
Replaces the mailbox's custom scores (`SpamScoreUpdate`). Administrators and domain
administrators always may; mailbox users need `spamScore` for their own mailbox. When both
scores are equal, the reject score is raised by 0.1, as in legacy. The spam filter applies the
scores within one refresh of its settings map (at most 1 minute). Audited with the old and new
values.

delete.summary: Reset a mailbox's spam score to the server defaults
delete.description:
Removes the mailbox's custom scores, so that the server defaults apply again (legacy
`default`). Same permissions as `setMailboxSpamScore`. Resetting a mailbox without custom
scores succeeds and changes nothing. Audited with the old values.

get.summary: Read the spam filter's action statistics
get.description:
Returns how many messages the spam filter (Rspamd) rejected, soft-rejected (including
greylisted), marked by rewriting the subject, moved to the junk folder or let through, since
its statistics were last reset, as the legacy dashboard chart shows them. `countedSince` gives
the start of the counting period when the filter reports it (`null`: unknown);
`spamFilterRunningSince` gives since when the filter has been running. Administrators only
(`forbidden` for other roles). When the filter cannot be reached within 30 seconds, the answer
is `503 temporary-failure` (`dependency: spamFilter`).

get.summary: List the rate limits set in my scope
get.description:
Lists the rate limits that are set on existing domains, alias domains and mailboxes in the
caller's scope: every object for administrators; for domain administrators, the domains they
manage, the alias domains of those domains and their mailboxes. Mailbox users are refused
(`forbidden`). Objects without a limit are not listed. A stored value that does not match the
legacy format is listed with `limit: null` and `invalidStoredValue`. `q` searches the object
name.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only limits of this kind of object.

get.summary: Read the rate limit of a domain
get.description:
Returns the limit set on a domain, or `limit: null` when none is set. Administrators: every domain; domain administrators: the domains they manage. Mailbox users are
refused (`forbidden`). Domain administrators may read without the `ratelimit` flag.

put.summary: Set the rate limit of a domain
put.description:
Sets the limit, replacing any previous one, in mailcow's shared store where the spam filter
reads it (field = the normalised object name, value `<value> / 1<s|m|h|d>`). The spam filter
applies it from the next message on. Administrators always may; domain administrators need
`ratelimit`; mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`). Audited with the old and new values.

delete.summary: Remove the rate limit of a domain
delete.description:
Removes the limit. Removing a limit that is not set succeeds and changes nothing (and is not
audited). Same permissions as `setDomainRateLimit`. Audited with the old value.

get.summary: Read the rate limit of an alias domain
get.description:
Returns the limit set on an alias domain, or `limit: null` when none is set. Administrators: every alias domain; domain administrators: the alias domains of their domains. Mailbox users are
refused (`forbidden`). Domain administrators may read without the `ratelimit` flag.

put.summary: Set the rate limit of an alias domain
put.description:
Sets the limit, replacing any previous one, in mailcow's shared store where the spam filter
reads it (field = the normalised object name, value `<value> / 1<s|m|h|d>`). The spam filter
applies it from the next message on. Administrators always may; domain administrators need
`ratelimit`; mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`). Audited with the old and new values.

delete.summary: Remove the rate limit of an alias domain
delete.description:
Removes the limit. Removing a limit that is not set succeeds and changes nothing (and is not
audited). Same permissions as `setAliasDomainRateLimit`. Audited with the old value.

get.summary: Read the rate limit of a mailbox
get.description:
Returns the limit set on a mailbox, or `limit: null` when none is set. It also gives the effective limit and whether it comes from the mailbox or from its domain, as the legacy mailbox page shows it. Administrators: every mailbox; domain administrators: mailboxes of their domains; resources answer `404`. Mailbox users are
refused (`forbidden`). Domain administrators may read without the `ratelimit` flag.

put.summary: Set the rate limit of a mailbox
put.description:
Sets the limit, replacing any previous one, in mailcow's shared store where the spam filter
reads it (field = the normalised object name, value `<value> / 1<s|m|h|d>`). The spam filter
applies it from the next message on. Administrators always may; domain administrators need
`ratelimit`; mailbox users are refused (`forbidden`). Audited with the old and new values.

delete.summary: Remove the rate limit of a mailbox
delete.description:
Removes the limit. Removing a limit that is not set succeeds and changes nothing (and is not
audited). Same permissions as `setMailboxRateLimit`. Audited with the old value.

Deletes the spam filter's counters of the bucket and removes the rate-limited log entries whose
bucket identifier equals `bucketId`, so the sender can send again at once (legacy "Remove
hash"). When neither counters nor log entries exist, the answer is `404`. A bucket that already
expired while its log entries remain is reset by removing the entries. Administrators only
(`forbidden` for other roles). Audited with the identifier, whether counters existed and the
number of log entries removed.

get.description:
Returns the server settings and limits that the system settings forms need before they submit:
the logo limits and accepted types, whether license verification is enabled, whether demo mode
is on, the configured host name and the mass mail sender legacy suggests, the address of the
Rspamd web interface, the colour reference surfaces and minimum contrast, the field limits and
the mass mail delivery policy. The values reflect the current configuration and contain no
secret. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

get.summary: Get the CORS settings of the legacy API
get.description:
Returns the origins and methods that the legacy `/api/v1` allows for cross-origin browser
requests. These settings govern only the legacy API: this API does not answer cross-origin
requests. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.summary: Change the CORS settings of the legacy API
patch.description:
Replaces the sent lists. Origins are `*` or `scheme://host[:port]` (at most 100, stored in lower
case and once each); `*` together with specific origins allows every origin, as in legacy. An
empty origin list means the server's own origin. Methods are a non-empty set of GET, POST, PUT
and DELETE. The legacy API applies the change to its next request. Audited.

get.description:
Returns the uploaded logo of the light or dark theme with its type, size, pixel dimensions and
version tag, or `isSet: false`. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key,
read-only keys included.

put.description:
Replaces the logo of this theme with the image sent as the request body (the raw file, not a
form). The type is detected from the content, never from `Content-Type`: PNG, JPEG, GIF
(animated too) and SVG are accepted, and the logo is stored with the detected type
(`unsupportedImageType` otherwise).

- The file must not exceed the operator's size limit (15 MiB by default; `tooLong`, params
  `max` and `unit: bytes`).
- A raster image must decode and must not exceed the maximum width and height (1,920 × 1,920
  pixels by default; `imageDimensionsExceeded`, params `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `width`,
  `height`). SVGs have no dimension limit.
- An SVG must be a well-formed document whose root element is `svg`. It is refused, never
  altered, when it contains script elements, event-handler attributes, URLs with a script or
  HTML scheme, embedded HTML or other foreign content (`foreignObject`, XHTML elements),
  references to external resources (only in-document references and embedded PNG, JPEG, GIF or
  WebP data are allowed), external style sheet imports, or a document type or entity
  declaration (`unsafeSvgContent`, params `construct` and `line`).

Validation errors are reported on the key `body`. The limits are readable beforehand from
`GET /capabilities/settings`. Refused in demo mode. Audited with the old and new type,
dimensions and size. Signed-out clients receive the new logo through the public configuration
on their next request.

delete.description:
Deletes the logo of this theme only. Clients then show the deployment's default logo. Deleting
a logo that is not set succeeds and changes nothing (not audited). Refused in demo mode.

get.description:
Returns the page title, product name, apps heading, login help text, footer and
announcement, as the legacy "Customize" screen edits them, with their version tag and the
deployment defaults of the title and product name. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Changes the sent UI texts; the others keep their values (legacy overwrites every field).
The page title, product name and apps heading are plain text of at most 255 characters without
line breaks, stored HTML-escaped as legacy stores them, so that both UIs show the same text. The
help text and footer are operator HTML, stored as given; clients sanitise them before rendering.
The announcement text is plain text, stored as given. When the footer key of older releases
(`UI_IMPRESS`) still holds the footer, the change moves it to `UI_FOOTER`. Help text, footer and
announcement text are at most 65,535 characters. Refused in demo mode. Audited with each changed attribute. The change is visible in the
public configuration on its next read, and in the legacy UI. Help text and footer are audited
only as changed, with their old and new sizes.

get.description: Returns which login links the login page hides and whether single sign-on is forced. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Changes the sent options. Forcing single sign-on is stored even while single sign-on is not
available, where it has no effect, as in legacy; it never makes the API refuse another sign-in
method. Refused in demo mode. Audited with each changed attribute. The change is visible in the
public configuration on its next read, and in the legacy UI.

get.description:
Returns the custom app links in their order and, read-only, the built-in links of the
operator's configuration. Clients that display app links read them from the public configuration.
Old-style entries stored by older releases (name and address only) are returned converted, as
legacy converts them. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Replaces the whole list of custom app links (at most 50), keeping the given order. Every
entry is validated: the name has 1 to 255 characters without line breaks, and each address is an
absolute `http` or `https` URL or a path starting with a single `/` (`invalidFormat`, `format:
appLinkUrl`). A request with any invalid entry changes nothing and names each entry (legacy saves
nothing but reports success). The built-in links are never changed. Refused in demo mode. Audited with each changed attribute. The change is visible in the
public configuration on its next read, and in the legacy UI.

get.description:
Returns the stored light and dark brand colours and the colours in effect, with their
foregrounds. The colours are stored by this API only; the legacy UI does not show them. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Sets or clears (`null`) the light and dark brand colours. A light colour needs a WCAG 2.2
contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against `#ffffff`, a dark colour against `#1d2939`; a colour that
fails is refused with `insufficientContrast` and its measured ratio. Colours are stored in lower
case. Clearing both returns the web app to its own palette. Refused in demo mode. Audited with the
old and new colours. The colours in effect appear in the public configuration on its next read.

get.description:
Returns whether administrators may look up the server's public addresses through third-party
services (feature 011). Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Turns the opt-in on or off, stored where legacy keeps it, so that the legacy dashboard follows
it too. Refused in demo mode. Audited.

get.description:
Returns the sender, subject and templates of the password reset e-mail, whether self-service
password reset is available (only while both a sender and a subject are set), and mailcow's
default templates, marked as defaults, while both stored templates are empty. Administrators
only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Changes the sent values. The sender is empty or a valid e-mail address without control
characters (an invalid sender is refused; legacy stores it empty). The subject has at most 255
characters without line breaks; each template at most 1 MiB. Clearing the sender or the subject
switches self-service password reset off (feature 005). Leaving both templates empty restores
mailcow's defaults. A template without `{{link}}` is accepted, as in legacy, but the e-mail is
then useless. Audited; templates only as changed, with their old and new sizes.

get.description:
Returns the sender, subject and HTML template in effect for the quota notifications that
Dovecot sends at 80% and 95% of a mailbox's quota, and which of them are Dovecot's defaults.
Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.

patch.description:
Changes the sent values; an empty value restores Dovecot's default. The sender is empty or a
valid e-mail address without control characters (legacy stores an invalid one empty); the
subject has at most 255 characters without line breaks; the template at most 1 MiB and is not
checked. The change applies to the next notification, without a reload. Audited; the template
only as changed, with its old and new sizes.

get.summary: Get a domain's quota notification copy recipients
get.description:
Returns the addresses that receive a copy of the quota notifications of this domain's mailboxes
and whether copies are sent. A domain without stored settings returns an empty, inactive list.
Administrators for every domain, domain administrators for the domains they manage (no
permission flag needed, as in legacy), by session or by key. An alias domain's name, an unknown
domain and a domain outside the caller's scope answer `404`, because notifications follow the
mailbox's own domain.

patch.summary: Change a domain's quota notification copy recipients
patch.description:
Replaces the recipient list (at most 100) and/or switches the copies on or off, with the scope
rules of the read. Any invalid address refuses the whole request and is named (legacy saves the
valid entries). Entries that differ only in letter case are stored once. An empty list is stored
as inactive, as in legacy. Dovecot sends the copies of the next notification accordingly. Audited.

get.description:
Lists the rules of mailcow's Rspamd settings map with their content, active state and times.
`q` searches the description and the content. Administrators only, by session or by an
administrator's key, read-only keys included.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) rules.

post.description:
Creates a rule, inactive unless `active` is `true`. The content is checked for balanced
structure so that one rule cannot break the settings map Rspamd loads for all rules. Rspamd
applies an active rule at its next refresh of mailcow's settings map, within about a minute,
without a restart. With `validateOnly=true` nothing is created and the answer is `200`. Audited,
the content only as changed, with its size.

get.description: Returns one rule. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key.

patch.description:
Changes the sent attributes with the rules of the creation; an empty description or content is
refused (legacy keeps the old value). The content is stored trimmed. With `validateOnly=true`
nothing is changed and the answer is `{"data": {"valid": true}}`. Audited.

200.description:
The changed rule (`RspamdSettingsRule`, with the `ETag` header), or with `validateOnly=true`
the validation result.

ETag.description: Version tag of the changed rule. Absent with `validateOnly=true`.

delete.description: Deletes the rule. Rspamd stops applying it at its next refresh of the settings map. Audited.

get.description:
Lists the global regex maps that the operator's configuration makes editable (13 by default,
from "Header-From: Denylist" to "Monitoring Hosts"), in the configured order unless `sort` is
given, each with its size and version tag but without its content, which the single read
returns. A map whose file is missing on this server is listed with `available: false`. `q`
searches the name.
Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys included.
Returns one map with its content and version tag. Administrators only.

put.description:
Replaces the map's content after checking every line on the server with the rule the legacy
page applies in the browser. The content is written, trimmed and ending with a line break, to
the map file Rspamd reads, in one write; the file's change time is then set again (after about
1.5 seconds, as legacy does), so that Rspamd reloads the complete map without a restart, even if
it read the file during the write. A map whose file does not exist on this server is refused
with `regex-map-unavailable` (legacy reports success and writes nothing). The legacy UI edits
the same file and never sends a version tag, so it can still overwrite a change made here. With
`validateOnly=true` nothing is written. Audited with the old and new size.

200.description:
The replaced map (`RspamdRegexMap`, with the `ETag` header), or with `validateOnly=true` the
validation result.

ETag.description: Version tag of the new content. Absent with `validateOnly=true`.

get.summary: Get the effective Rspamd settings map
get.description:
Returns the settings map exactly as mailcow generates it for Rspamd, including mailcow's own
generated settings and an `additional_settings_<id>` block for each active rule, as the legacy
screen shows it. Read-only. When mailcow's settings map endpoint cannot be reached, the answer
is `503`. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key.

put.summary: Set the Rspamd web interface password
put.description:
Hands the new password to mailcow's container service, which stores its hash for Rspamd and
restarts Rspamd, as legacy does. The answer is `204` only once the service confirms it. The
password is never stored, logged, audited or returned by this API; the audit record only says
that it was changed.

Only a signed-in administrator may set it. Requests authenticated by an API key are refused with
`session-required`, whatever the key's owner and access level, so that a leaked key cannot lock
administrators out of the Rspamd web interface.

get.description:
Returns the global pre-filter and post-filter, pre-filter first, each with its script and
version tag, read from the shared files Dovecot compiles at start. A missing file reads as an
empty script. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key, read-only keys
included.
Returns the script and its version tag. Administrators only.

put.description:
Checks the script with legacy's Sieve parser, writes it to the shared file that Dovecot and the
legacy UI read, and restarts Dovecot through mailcow's container service so that it compiles
the script, unless `deferRestart` is `true`. **A restart briefly interrupts IMAP, POP3 and
delivery.** `meta.dovecotRestart` reports the restart as `done`, `failed` or `deferred`; a failed
restart does not undo the write, and the script then takes effect at Dovecot's next start.

An invalid script, and a file that does not exist on this server
(`global-sieve-filter-unavailable`; legacy restarts anyway and reports success), never cause a
restart. With `validateOnly=true` the script is only checked: nothing is written, restarted or
audited. Audited with the old and new size and the restart outcome.

200.description:
The saved filter (`GlobalSieveFilter`, with the `ETag` header) and the restart outcome in
`meta.dovecotRestart`, or with `validateOnly=true` the validation result without `meta`.

ETag.description: Version tag of the saved script. Absent with `validateOnly=true`.

get.description:
Lists the presets mailcow ships of one kind, read-only, each with its identifier, translation
key, English headline and content. `rspamd` presets are for administrators only (legacy also
lets domain administrators read them); `sieve` presets for administrators and domain
administrators. By session or by key. `q` searches the headline and the content.

Lists mass mail jobs, newest first by default, with their counts per outcome but without their
bodies, which the single read returns. `q` searches the subject. Jobs are kept for the audit retention period. Administrators only, by session or by an
administrator's key, read-only keys included.

post.description:
Creates a job that delivers one message per recipient of the selection, in the background, at
most 10 messages per second by default. Preview the selection first
(`POST /mass-mail-jobs/recipient-preview`) and confirm its recipient count in
`expectedRecipients`: a different count at this moment refuses the job, so that a changed
selection never sends unexpectedly. The recipients are fixed when the job is created; a mailbox
deleted or deactivated afterwards is recorded as failed.

Messages are delivered directly into each mailbox through Dovecot's local delivery (LMTP), as
legacy does: they do not pass Postfix or Rspamd, so they are never spam-filtered, quarantined,
DKIM-signed or relayed. A temporary refusal by Dovecot (for example during a Dovecot restart) is
retried up to 3 times within 5 minutes. No recipient receives the message twice; if this API is
interrupted, the job continues afterwards with the pending recipients, and a recipient whose
delivery was in progress is recorded as failed (`interrupted`). Only one job runs at a time.

Only a signed-in administrator may send. Requests authenticated by an API key are refused with
`session-required`. Audited with the sender, subject, a summary of the selection and the number
of recipients; the completion is audited again with the counts.

Returns the recipients that the selection yields now, sorted by address and paged, with the
recipient count of the whole selection in `meta.recipientCount`. `q` filters the listed
addresses without changing `recipientCount`. The selection travels in the body because its
lists can be long; the request changes nothing and is not audited. An invalid selection is
refused with field errors exactly as when sending.

Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key; read-only keys may use it,
because it changes nothing.

get.description:
Returns the job with its sender, subject, bodies, selection, creator, times, status and the
number of recipients per outcome. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key.

Lists the job's recipients, sorted by address by default, each with its outcome and, for a
failure, a stable `failureCode` and Dovecot's reply. `q` searches the address. Administrators only, by session or by an
administrator's key.

post.description:
Cancels a running job. Once the answer is sent, no further message is started; a delivery that
was already under way finishes within 5 seconds. The pending recipients are recorded as skipped,
and the job is reported as cancelled. Any administrator may cancel any job. Cancelling a
cancelled job succeeds and changes nothing; cancelling a completed job is refused with `409`.

Only a signed-in administrator may cancel. Requests authenticated by an API key are refused with
`session-required`. Audited with the counts at the moment of the cancellation.

get.description:
Returns the server's GUID, or that mailcow marked it invalid, and the last verification result
as the legacy dashboard shows it (also when the verification was made in the legacy UI). Reading
never contacts the license service. Refused with `feature-disabled` when the operator disabled
license verification. Administrators only, by session or by an administrator's key.

post.description:
Sends only the GUID to mailcow's license verification service (`https://verify.mailcow.email`,
waiting at most 10 seconds for a connection), stores the result where the legacy dashboard reads
it, and returns the new status. An unreachable service or an unreadable answer gives the result
`unreachable`, which is stored and returned, not an error. The license service is contacted
only by this request. Refused with `feature-disabled` when the operator disabled license
verification. Audited with the result.

get.description:
Returns the server settings and limits that clients of the self-service operations need before
they submit, read from the server's current configuration. Signed-out callers get only
`passwordReset`, so the sign-in page offers "Forgot password" only when it works.
Authenticated callers (a session, also a restricted one, or any API key, read-only included)
get every member; sessions also get `account`, which says for example whether the account must
keep a second factor. Changes nothing.

put.description:
Changes the signed-in account's password, for every role. The current password is required,
also for administrators, except in a session restricted by a forced password change, where the
change resolves the pending action at once. A wrong current password is audited, delayed and
counted like a failed sign-in for the account and client address (`429` after 10 failures in
15 minutes); it is not reported to fail2ban.

The new password must meet the password policy (`validation-failed` names each unmet rule with
feature 003's codes: `tooShort` with the policy's `min`, and `missingCharacterClass` with the
missing `characterClass`) and must not start with a hash-scheme prefix (`preHashedPassword`).
It is stored in mailcow's configured hash scheme, so the mail server verifies it. For a mailbox
the forced-change flag is cleared, the password-changed time recorded and the groupware
directory refreshed. App passwords, API keys and legacy UI sessions are not affected. The mail
server may accept the old password from mail clients for up to `mailServerCacheSeconds`.

By default the account's other sessions of this API end, with their webmail hand-offs; send
`endOtherSessions: false` to keep them. The current session stays signed in with a renewed
session identifier. Mailboxes whose password lives in an external identity provider are refused
(`password-managed-externally`). Not available to API keys. Audited, without the password.

get.summary: Read the rules for my new password
get.description:
Returns the password policy that a new password of the signed-in account must meet, with the
same values and version tag as `getPasswordPolicy`. Available to every role, also in a session
restricted by a forced password change. Not available to API keys. Changes nothing.

Lists every second-factor entry of the signed-in account (TOTP, WebAuthn security keys, Yubico
OTP and deprecated U2F or HOTP entries), wherever it was enrolled, active or not, without any
secret material. The entry that completed the current sign-in is marked. Passkeys are listed by
`GET /me/passkeys`. `q` searches the name. Available in a session restricted by a forced
second-factor setup. Not available to API keys.

post.description:
Enrols a TOTP authenticator app (after `POST /me/second-factors/totp-enrolment`), a WebAuthn
security key (after `POST /me/second-factors/webauthn-registration-options`) or a YubiKey in
Yubico OTP mode, stored where legacy mailcow stores second factors and active at once, so it
completes the second-factor step of both UIs from the next sign-in. An account may have several
entries of each type.

The current password is required, except in a session restricted by a forced second-factor
setup, which this enrolment resolves at once. Administrators, domain administrators and
mailboxes with the mailcow source only (`password-managed-externally` otherwise). A Yubico OTP
is verified with the Yubico service using the given credentials (`503` when it cannot be
reached; nothing is stored). Not available to API keys. Audited, without secrets.

Starts a TOTP enrolment bound to this session and returns, exactly once, a new random 160-bit
secret, its `otpauth://` provisioning address with the account's username and the server's
issuer name, and a QR code of that address. Codes have 6 digits, 30-second steps and SHA-1. The
enrolment expires after 10 minutes or five wrong codes; a new start replaces it. Same access
rules as `enrolOwnSecondFactor`.

Issues single-use registration options bound to this session for a security key used as a
second factor: bound to this host name, excluding the account's existing WebAuthn second
factors, with user verification and attestation formats following mailcow's settings. They
expire after 5 minutes or at the first enrolment attempt; a new request replaces them. Same
access rules as `enrolOwnSecondFactor`.

Removes every second-factor entry of the signed-in account after checking the current password
(legacy "Disable two-factor authentication"). Passkeys are not affected. Refused with
`second-factor-required-by-policy` when the account must keep a second factor. A wrong current
password is throttled like a failed sign-in. Not available to API keys. Audited.

get.summary: Get one of my second factors

delete.summary: Remove one of my second factors
delete.description:
Removes one entry, without the password, as legacy does. Refused with
`second-factor-required-by-policy` when the account must keep a second factor, and with
`last-second-factor` when the entry is the account's only active entry. Not available to API
keys or restricted sessions. Audited.

get.description:
Returns the signed-in mailbox user's password recovery address, shared with the legacy UI.
Mailbox users with the mailcow source only; administrators and domain administrators get
`forbidden`, external-source mailboxes `password-managed-externally`. Not available to API
keys.

put.summary: Set, change or remove my recovery address
put.description:
Sets the recovery address (a valid e-mail address of at most 255 characters) or removes it
(`null` or `""`), stored where legacy stores it. Needs the current password, and the `pwReset`
permission unless the address stays the same. Same access rules as `getOwnRecoveryEmail`.
Audited.

get.description:
Returns the signed-in mailbox user's mailbox at a glance, as the legacy user page shows it:
storage and messages against the quota, protocol access, webmail settings, the password-changed
time, the recovery address, the addresses that deliver to the mailbox, the addresses it may send
as, the domains for temporary aliases and counts of active app passwords and temporary aliases.
Mailbox users only; administrators and domain administrators get `forbidden`. Not available to
API keys or restricted sessions.

get.summary: Read the client configuration of my mailbox
get.description:
Returns what the legacy client setup help shows for setting up a mail client by hand: host names,
TLS and STARTTLS ports for IMAP, POP3 and SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV and ActiveSync when the groupware
is enabled, the authentication method and the mailcow documentation link with legacy's
parameters. Values come from the server's autodiscover settings. Autodiscover and autoconfig
themselves stay with the legacy endpoints. Mailbox users only; not available to API keys or
restricted sessions.

Returns an unsigned Apple connection profile (`.mobileconfig`) for the signed-in mailbox, with
the payloads, keys and identifiers of legacy `mobileconfig.php`: the IMAP account with its SMTP
server and, for `emailAndDav`, a CalDAV and a CardDAV account. No password is embedded; the
device asks for it. Mailbox users only; not available to API keys or restricted sessions.
Changes nothing.

post.summary: Download an Apple connection profile with a new app password
post.description:
Creates a new app password for the signed-in mailbox (IMAP and SMTP, plus CalDAV/CardDAV for
`emailAndDav`; active; a generated password) and returns the profile with that password
embedded (legacy `?app_password`). The password appears only in the file. Needs the
`appPasswds` permission (`permission-flag-required`). Audited as an app password creation. Same
access rules as `getOwnAppleProfile`.

post.summary: Open my webmail without signing in again
post.description:
Signs the requesting browser in to webmail as the signed-in mailbox user, through mailcow's
existing webmail single sign-on, without changing any mailcow container. The response sets
mailcow's legacy session cookie for a session that grants webmail only: the legacy UI still
shows its sign-in page in this browser (an existing legacy UI sign-in of this browser is
replaced), and `/api/v1` accepts no change through it. Open `data.url` in the same browser.

The hand-off ends when this API's session ends: at sign-out, when a password change or reset
ends the session, within a minute after the session expires, and at the latest after mailcow's
idle lifetime. A new request replaces the session's previous hand-off. A recent-login entry
`SSO` is recorded and the hand-off is audited.

Mailbox users with a full session only (`forbidden` for other roles, `pending-action-required`
in a restricted session); `groupware-disabled` when the server runs without webmail. Not
available to API keys.

Asks for a reset link for a mailbox whose password was forgotten. Every well-formed request
gets the same acknowledgement in the same time, whether or not the address exists, has a
recovery address, is eligible, has reached the limit of three outstanding links, and whether or
not the message could be sent; nothing about the account is revealed. A message is sent to the
recovery address only for an active mailbox with the mailcow source and a valid recovery
address. It is built from the operator's reset template (configured in the legacy UI) and links
to the reset page on this host. Links are valid for 15 minutes and are shared with the legacy
reset page.

Refused with `password-reset-unavailable` when the reset message has no sender or subject.
Throttled per client address (10 requests in 15 minutes by default). For browser sessions,
signed in or not, with the anti-forgery token. Every request is audited with its outcome.

Checks the token from a reset link (sent in the body, never in the URL) and returns the account
address, the expiry, the password rules and the account's second factors. Tokens issued by the
legacy reset page work too. Changes nothing. Throttled per client address (10 checks in 15
minutes by default). For browser sessions with the anti-forgery token.

post.summary: Get a WebAuthn challenge for a reset
post.description:
For an account with WebAuthn second factors, issues a single-use challenge bound to the valid
token and to this browser session, to be answered in `POST /password-resets/completion`. It
expires after 5 minutes or at the first completion attempt; a new request replaces it.
Throttled with the token checks.

Sets the new password with a valid token. When the account has active second factors, the
request must also carry one of them; without it the answer is `second-factor-required` with the
usable methods, and the client resends the new password with the second factor. A wrong second
factor leaves the token valid and counts towards the sign-in throttling of the account. An
account whose only second factors are deprecated gets `second-factor-unavailable`.

On success the password is stored in mailcow's hash scheme, the password-changed time is
recorded, a forced password change is cleared, every reset token of the account stops working,
the groupware directory is refreshed, and every session of the account in this API ends with its
webmail hand-offs. The new password works in both UIs. Throttled per client address (10
completions in 15 minutes by default). Audited, without the password or the token.

post.summary: Apply a mail-settings action to several mailboxes
post.description:
Applies `setTlsEnforcement` (inbound and/or outbound TLS enforcement) to up to 100 mailboxes, as
the legacy mailbox list's TLS mass actions do. Each mailbox is processed like `updateMailboxMailSettings`, with
the same checks and one audit record carrying the bulk request ID. A mailbox outside the
caller's scope gets `notFound`, an outdated `version` (the mailbox's mail-settings version tag)
gets `outdated`, and an outage gets `failed`; the others proceed. One result per distinct
mailbox, in request order.

Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a read-write key; mailbox users get
`forbidden`.

get.summary: List the app passwords of a mailbox
get.description:
Lists the mailbox's app passwords, never with their password or hash. `q` searches the name.
Administrators (any mailbox), domain administrators (mailboxes of their domains) and mailbox
users (their own mailbox), from a session or a key; reading needs no permission flag.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Only active (`true`) or inactive (`false`) app passwords.

post.description:
Creates an app password for the mailbox, for the chosen protocols (all six by default), active
by default. Without `password`, the system generates 32 random characters that meet the
password policy and returns them once as `generatedPassword`. An app password authenticates
only to its own protocols, independently of the mailbox's own protocol access, never signs in
to the web UI or webmail, and takes effect at the mail server's next authentication.

Needs the `appPasswds` permission: the mailbox user's own flag, or the domain administrator's
own `appPasswds` flag (`permission-flag-required`). Session or read-write key. Audited, without
the password.

patch.description:
Changes only the members sent: name, password (given, or generated with
`generatePassword: true` and returned once), protocols and active state. The app password always
stays with its mailbox, also when an administrator changes it. Needs `appPasswds` like
creation. Audited.

delete.description: Removes the app password at once. Needs `appPasswds` like creation. Audited.

get.summary: List the temporary aliases of a mailbox
get.description:
Lists the mailbox's permanent and not yet expired temporary aliases. `q` searches the address
and the description. Same callers as `listAppPasswords`; reading needs no permission flag.

parameters.name: permanent
parameters.description: Only permanent (`true`) or expiring (`false`) aliases.

post.description:
Creates a temporary alias with a random, readable address in the mailbox's domain or one of
its alias domains, valid for `lifetimeHours` (one year by default) or permanently. Mail sent to
it is delivered to the mailbox. Needs `spamAlias` (domain administrators always hold it).
Session or read-write key. Audited.

patch.description:
Sets a new lifetime of 1 to 87,600 hours counted from now, or makes the alias permanent.
Nothing else can change. Needs `spamAlias`. Audited.

delete.description: Removes the alias at once; mail to it is refused from then on. Needs `spamAlias`. Audited.

get.summary: List the domains for a mailbox's temporary aliases
get.description:
Lists the domains in which temporary aliases of the mailbox may be created: the mailbox's
domain first, then its alias domains by name. The order is fixed. `q` searches the domain
names. Same callers as `listTemporaryAliases`.

get.summary: Read the push notification settings of a mailbox
get.description:
Returns the mailbox's Pushover settings. The application token and the user key are never
returned; `tokenSet` and `userKeySet` say whether they are stored. Without stored settings
`configured` is `false`. Same callers as `listAppPasswords`; reading needs no permission flag.

put.summary: Replace the push notification settings of a mailbox
put.description:
Replaces the settings as a whole, stored where legacy stores them, so mailcow's notification
pipeline uses them unchanged. Token and user key are 30 letters or digits each; both are
required while none are stored and keep their stored values when omitted. Needs `pushover`:
the mailbox user's own flag, or the domain administrator's own `pushover` flag. Session or
read-write key. Audited, with the credentials only as "set" or "changed".

delete.summary: Remove the push notification settings of a mailbox
delete.description: Removes the settings; no further notification is sent. Needs `pushover`. Audited.

post.description:
Asks Pushover's validation service whether the stored token and user key are valid, without
sending a notification, and returns its verdict. `push-notifications-not-configured` when no
credentials are stored; `503` when Pushover cannot be reached. It acts on an external service for
the mailbox, so it counts as a change: needs `pushover`, a session or a read-write key, and is
audited.

get.summary: Read the mail settings of a mailbox
get.description:
Returns the tagged-mail handling and the inbound and outbound TLS enforcement of the mailbox.
Same callers as `listAppPasswords`; reading needs no permission flag. `503` when mailcow's
shared store is unavailable.

patch.summary: Change the mail settings of a mailbox
patch.description:
Changes the values sent; the others keep their current value. Tagged-mail handling is stored in
mailcow's shared store and TLS enforcement in the mailbox, where legacy stores them, so the mail
filter and the mail server apply them to the next message. Changing the tagged-mail handling
needs `delimiterAction`, changing TLS enforcement needs `tlsPolicy` (domain administrators hold
both); values sent equal to their current value need no flag. Session or read-write key.
Audited. `503` leaves no partial change.

get.summary: List the recent logins of a mailbox
get.description:
Lists where the mailbox was used during the last `days` days (7 by default, at most 31), grouped
by client address, service and app password with the latest time of each group, as legacy groups
them. Private and internal addresses are marked and never have a country. Countries come from
mailcow's shared cache; uncached public addresses of the page are looked up with the external
service legacy uses (when enabled), within a bounded time, and reported without a country when
the lookup does not finish. `q` searches the client address. Same callers as `listAppPasswords`.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Only this service (any letter case), for example `IMAP` or `WEBUI`.

delete.summary: Clear the recent logins of a mailbox
delete.description:
Removes all recent-login records of the mailbox and, when the caller is an administrator or the
mailbox user, also the legacy UI's records of the mailbox's successful sign-ins, as legacy does.
Both UIs then show an empty list. Session or read-write key. Audited.

delete.summary: Reset the ActiveSync cache of a mailbox
delete.description:
Removes the groupware's cached ActiveSync device state of the mailbox, as legacy does; phones
download everything again at their next sync. Needs `easReset` (domain administrators hold it).
`groupware-disabled` when the server runs without the groupware. Session or read-write key.
Audited.

delete.summary: Reset the groupware profile of a mailbox
delete.description:
Removes, as legacy does and **irreversibly**, the mailbox's groupware settings, cached device
state, sharing permissions on and by the mailbox, and its folders with their contacts and
events. Webmail may ask for a new sign-in. Needs `sogoProfileReset` (off by default for mailbox
users; domain administrators hold it). `groupware-disabled` when the server runs without the
groupware. Session or read-write key. Audited.

get.summary: List the Sieve filters of a mailbox
get.description:
Lists the mailbox's prefilters and postfilters. `q` searches the description. Administrators,
domain administrators (mailboxes of their domains) and mailbox users (their own mailbox), from a
session or a key.

post.description:
Creates a prefilter or postfilter for the mailbox, active by default, stored where legacy
stores filters so the mail server applies it to the next delivered message. Activating it
deactivates the mailbox's other active filter of the same kind. The script must pass legacy's
Sieve validation (`sieveSyntax` with the parser's message) and fit 65,535 bytes. Administrators
and domain administrators with the `filters` flag (`permission-flag-required`); mailbox users get
`forbidden`. Session or read-write key. Audited, with the script only as its size.

patch.description:
Changes only the members sent, with the rules of `createSieveFilter`; the mailbox never changes.
Activating the filter, or changing the kind of an active filter, deactivates the mailbox's
other active filter of that kind in the same change. Same callers as `createSieveFilter`.
Audited.

delete.description: Removes the filter at once. Same callers as `createSieveFilter`. Audited.

get.summary: Read the active Sieve script of a mailbox
get.description:
Returns the Sieve script that the user manages in webmail and that the mail server runs for the
mailbox, as the mail server reports it through mailcow's container service. `name` and `script`
are `null` when no script is active. `503` when the mail server cannot be reached or does not
answer within the container-service timeout. A read: read-only keys may use it. Same callers as
`listMailboxSieveFilters`.

get.summary: List the Sieve filters of all mailboxes in scope
get.description:
Lists the Sieve filters of every mailbox in the caller's scope, with pagination instead of
legacy's per-domain loop. Sorted by mailbox and then description by default. `q` searches the
description and the mailbox; `id` selects one filter. Administrators and domain administrators, from a session or a key;
reading needs no permission flag. Mailbox users list their own filters with
`listMailboxSieveFilters`.

parameters.name: mailbox
parameters.description: Only filters of this mailbox (any letter case, domain in ASCII or Unicode form).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Only the filter with this ID (G23), for example to read a filter whose mailbox is not known.

post.description:
Checks a script with the same Sieve parser legacy mailcow uses, without saving anything, and
says whether it is valid, with the parser's message when it is not. It changes nothing, so it
counts as a read: read-only keys may use it. Administrators and domain administrators; mailbox
users get `forbidden`.

get.description:
Returns what a client needs before it shows or submits the identity provider forms: whether a
configuration is stored and its type, the new web app's return addresses to register at a
provider (also before the first save), the provider types and what each offers, the defaults,
the field limits, the provider time-out and the single sign-on lifetimes. Changes nothing and is
not audited. Administrators only: a signed-in administrator or a key owned by an administrator,
read-only keys included.

Returns the legacy OAuth2 endpoint paths, the scope, the accepted grant types, the token
lifetimes in effect on this server, the redirect URI length limit, the bulk limit and the page
sizes. Changes nothing and is not audited. Administrators only: a signed-in administrator or a
key owned by an administrator, read-only keys included.

sessionCookie.name: __Host-restv2_session
sessionCookie.description:
Same-origin browser session. The cookie is `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`,
`Path=/` and has no `Domain`. It expires after the server's idle session lifetime
(mailcow's `SESSION_LIFETIME`, 3 hours by default) and when the user agent changes.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfToken.description:
Anti-forgery token of the current session, obtained from `GET /csrf-token`. Required on
every state-changing request made with a session.

apiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyAuth.description:
Secret of an API key created by an administrator. The key acts with its owner's role,
scope and permission flags, limited by its access level.

KnownProblemType.description:
Problem types of this API that clients act on, documented in `docs/problems.md`. Responses use
plain `string` for `Problem.type`; this enumeration exists so that generated clients get
constants. Later features add values.

PermissionFlagRequiredProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required` (status `403`, G34): the caller's role
may use the operation, but only with a permission flag (`da_acl` or `user_acl`) that it lacks.
Nothing changed. Every feature's variant of this problem extends this schema and may narrow the
flag names.

requiredFlags.description:
Flag names as in `PermissionFlags` (camelCase, for example `quarantineAttachments`), never
legacy column names, so that clients can compare them with `GET /me`. With
`requiredFlagsMatch: all`, only the flags the caller lacks are listed.

requiredFlagsMatch.description:
How the listed flags combine: `all` (every listed flag is needed; the default when the
member is absent) or `any` (any one of them suffices).

OutcomeUnknownProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/outcome-unknown` (status `504`, G11): mailcow's container service
did not answer within its timeout (`DOCKER_TIMEOUT`, 60 seconds), so the outcome of one step is
unknown. Shared by every feature that calls the container service; each feature's variant extends
this schema and documents its step names.

step.description: The step or action whose outcome is unknown.

CsrfToken.description: Anti-forgery token of the current session.

token.description: Send this value in the `X-CSRF-Token` header of every state-changing request.

Problem.description:
RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`). `type` is the stable machine-readable
code: compare it as an exact string. `title` and `detail` are English and may be reworded.
Extension members may be added later without notice.

type.description:
Problem type. Either one of the documented types (see `KnownProblemType` and
`docs/problems.md`) or `about:blank`, in which case the status code identifies the problem.

title.description: Short English summary of the problem type.

status.description: HTTP status code of this occurrence.

detail.description: English explanation of this occurrence. Never contains secrets.

requestId.description:
Identifier of the request (the W3C trace ID), also written to the service log and to any
audit record of the request.

PendingAction.description:
Action an account must complete before the session is fully usable.

- `passwordChange`: mailcow forces a password change (`force_pw_update`). Changing the password
  with `PUT /me/password`, which needs no current password in this case, resolves it.
- `secondFactorSetup`: mailcow forces second-factor setup (`force_tfa`) and the account has no
  second factor and no active passkey. Enrolling a second factor (`POST /me/second-factors`,
  without the current password in this case) or registering a passkey (`POST /me/passkeys`)
  resolves it.

PendingActionProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required` (status `403`). The session is
restricted until the listed actions are completed.

SessionState.description:
- `anonymous`: no account is signed in. The session only carries the anti-forgery token and
  any passkey challenge.
- `pendingSecondFactor`: the password was verified and one of `pendingSignIn.methods` must be
  completed within 5 minutes.
- `restricted`: signed in, but `pendingActions` must be completed first.
- `active`: signed in with full access for the account's role.

Role.description:
Account role. `admin` and `domainAdmin` accounts live in mailcow's `admin` table (`superadmin`
1 or 0); `mailboxUser` accounts are rows of the `mailbox` table.

SecondFactorType.description:
Second-factor type. `webauthn` covers security keys and passkeys enrolled as a second factor
(mailcow `tfa.authmech = webauthn`), `totp` authenticator apps, `yubiOtp` Yubico OTP keys
verified against the Yubico service. Deprecated U2F and HOTP entries are never offered.

SecondFactorMethod.description: One enrolled second factor. Never contains secret material.

name.description: Display name given at enrolment (mailcow `tfa.key_id`).

tier.description:
`primary` for `webauthn` and `totp`, offered directly. `advanced` for `yubiOtp`, offered
behind an "other methods" option.

PendingSignIn.description:
A sign-in whose password was verified and which needs one second factor. `methods` lists the
account's active, usable second factors in the recommended presentation order: WebAuthn
security keys and passkeys first, TOTP second, Yubico OTP last. One failed attempt cancels the
pending sign-in.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after the password step.

AuthMethod.description:
How the caller authenticated: `password` (no second factor active), `passwordAndSecondFactor`,
`passkey` (usernameless passkey sign-in) or `apiKey`. Feature 007 adds `ssoToken` (a domain
administrator's single sign-on token). Feature 012 adds `singleSignOn` (a mailbox user signed
in through a Keycloak or generic OIDC provider), `directoryPassword` and
`directoryPasswordAndSecondFactor` (password verified by the LDAP directory), and
`providerPassword` and `providerPasswordAndSecondFactor` (password verified against Keycloak
through the mailpassword flow). Clients must tolerate values added later.

Impersonation.description:
The impersonation of the caller's session (legacy "login as" or "dual login"): the signed-in
account (`impersonator`) acts as `target`, with the target's role and scope and the permission
flags legacy grants to impersonators. It ends when the impersonator ends it, signs out, or when
the target is deleted or renamed, leaves the impersonator's scope, or an impersonating domain
administrator loses the `loginAs` flag.

id.description: ULID of the impersonation, also the audit target of its start and end.

impersonator.description: The signed-in account and how it signed in.

Session.description:
The browser session of the caller. `username` and `role` are present in every state except
`anonymous`. `authMethod` and `signedInAt` are present in `restricted` and `active`.
`pendingSignIn` is present only in `pendingSecondFactor`.

username.description: Normalised (trimmed, lower-cased) username of the account.

authMethod.description:
How this session was signed in. `ssoToken` is a domain administrator's single sign-on token
(feature 007). `singleSignOn`, `directoryPassword*` (LDAP) and `providerPassword*` (Keycloak
mailpassword flow) are sign-ins through the identity provider (feature 012); see `AuthMethod`.

idleTimeout.description:
Seconds of inactivity after which the session ends (mailcow's `SESSION_LIFETIME`, 10800 by
default). Every request resets the timer.

impersonation.description:
Present while the session impersonates another account (feature 007). `username` and `role`
are then those of the impersonated account; `authMethod`, `signedInAt` and `pendingActions`
are those of the impersonator's own sign-in.

PasswordSignInRequest.description:
Username and password of an existing mailcow account. The username is trimmed and lower-cased
before lookup. Without `role`, account types are tried in mailcow's order: administrator,
domain administrator, mailbox user. With `role`, only that type is tried.

ValidationRuleCode.description:
Stable code of a validation rule. Clients must treat unknown codes as a generic invalid value,
because later features may add codes.

- `required`: the field is missing, `null` or empty.
- `invalidType`: wrong JSON type. Params: `expected` (`string`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`,
  `object`).
- `tooShort` / `tooLong`: string length out of bounds. Params: `min` / `max`.
- `tooMany`: too many list items. Params: `max`.
- `outOfRange`: number out of bounds. Params: `min`, `max`.
- `notInList`: value not among the allowed values. Params: `allowed`.
- `invalidFormat`: value does not match a format. Params: `format`, one of `dateTime`
  (RFC 3339), `ipNetwork` (IPv4 or IPv6 address or prefix), `ipAddress`, `totpCode` (six
  digits), `yubicoOtp` (44 letters or digits), `base64url`, `webauthnCredential`, `requestId`
  (32 lower-case hexadecimal digits).
- `mustBeInFuture`: a time that must lie in the future does not.
- `notFound`: the referenced object does not exist.
- `notEligible`: the referenced object exists but cannot be used here. Params: `allowedRoles`.
- Sync jobs (feature 008): `invalidFormat` also uses `format: hostName` (host name or IPv4
  address); `notEligible` uses `kind` (`resource`, `alias`, `aliasDomainAddress`) for a sync-job
  target that is not a mailbox; `optionNotAllowed` (an imapsync option not on the allow-list,
  param `option`); `optionContainsSpace` (an option token containing a space, param `token`);
  `customParamsNotPermitted` (custom imapsync parameters are restricted to administrators);
  `invalidRegex` (not a valid regular expression); `immutable` (the value cannot be changed after
  creation).
- Domains (feature 002): `invalidFormat` also uses `format: domainName`, `dkimSelector` and
  `email`; `tooLong` may carry `unit: bytes`; `immutable` also covers read-only members sent back
  with a different value; `notMultipleOf` (a quota that is not a whole multiple of a unit, param
  `factor`); `mustNotExceed` (a value above another field's value, params `field` and `value`);
  `belowInUse` (a limit below current usage, param `inUse`); `reserved` (a name reserved by the
  server, such as its own host name).
- DKIM, MTA-STS and DNS (feature 010): `invalidFormat` also uses `format: mxHost` (a host name
  with an optional `*.` prefix); `invalidPrivateKey` (not exactly one PEM-encoded PKCS #1 or
  PKCS #8 private key); `encryptedPrivateKey` (the private key is encrypted);
  `unsupportedKeyType` (not an RSA key, param `allowed`); `keyLengthOutOfRange` (key length in
  bits outside `min` and `max`); `sameAsSource` (a copy target equal to its source). None of them
  echoes the key text.
- Mailboxes (feature 003): `invalidFormat` also uses `format: localPart`, `email` and
  `attributeName`; `notEligible` uses `kind: aliasDomain` for a creation domain that is an alias
  domain; `notMultipleOf` (param `factor: 1048576`) for quotas; `outOfRange` on a quota carries
  `limit` (`maxMailboxQuota`, `domainQuotaLeft` or `largestAllowedQuota`) next to `min` and
  `max` in bytes; `immutable` for any read-only member sent in a change; `tooShort` on a password
  is the policy's minimum length; `missingCharacterClass` (a password lacks a class the policy
  requires, param `characterClass`: `letter`, `digit`, `special` or `lowerAndUpper`);
  `conflictsWith` (a value not allowed together with another field's value, params `field` and
  `value`, for example a password with an external `authSource`); `unchanged` (a rename to the
  current local part).
- Identity providers and OAuth2 clients (feature 012): `invalidFormat` also uses `format:
  httpUrl` (absolute `https` or `http` URL), `hostName` (also an IPv6 address for LDAP hosts),
  `keycloakRealm`, `keycloakVersion`, `scopeList`, `ldapAttribute`, `ldapFilter`, `redirectUri`
  (absolute URI with a scheme, no fragment, no whitespace) and `oauthErrorCode`; `notFound` on a
  mapped or default template carries `resource: mailboxTemplate`; `conflictsWith` (params
  `field: type`, `value`) for a member that is not a setting of the configuration's type, and
  for an LDAP `attributeField` left empty while `importUsers` or `periodicSync` is on;
  `immutable` for a different `type` in a change or a different OAuth2 `clientId` or `scope`;
  `secretRequired` (the client secret or bind password must be sent, param `reason`:
  `noStoredSecret`, `typeChanged` or `addressChanged`, with `field` naming the changed address
  for the latter); `duplicate` (a value that must be unique appears twice, param
  `duplicateOf` with the path of the first occurrence).
- Administrators and domain administrators (feature 007): `invalidFormat` also uses `format:
  accountUsername` (only `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`, with at least one letter or digit);
  `reserved` (param `reserved: [api]`) for the username `api`; `notEligible` uses `kind:
  aliasDomain` for an assigned domain that is an alias domain, and `reason` (`mailboxInactive`,
  `loginDisabled`, `domainInactive`) for a mailbox whose webmail cannot be opened; `immutable` for a read-only member sent back with a different value; password rules
  use feature 003's codes; `unknownField` (a member the schema does not define, for example an
  unknown permission flag, named by its path).
- Routing (feature 009): `invalidFormat` also uses `format: nextHop` (`host`, `host:port`,
  `[host]` or `[host]:port`), `transportDestination`, `recipientMapDestination`,
  `tlsPolicyDestination`, `tlsPolicyParameters`, `domainName`, `email` and `ipNetwork`;
  `invalidRegex` for an MX-based transport pattern MariaDB cannot evaluate; `immutable` for a
  read-only member sent back with a different value; `notFound` for an unknown or out-of-scope BCC
  local destination or relayhost; `tooMany` (`max: 1`) for several BCC destinations;
  `notResolvable` (a forwarding host name that resolves to no address); `invalidCharacter` (a value
  containing a forbidden character, param `characters`, for example `[":"]` in an SMTP username);
  `required` with param `because: password` for a password without a username.
- Monitoring and operations (feature 011): `invalidFormat` also uses `format: ipNetworkOrHostname`
  (allowlist entry), `ipNetwork` (denylist entry), `queueId` (hexadecimal Postfix queue ID) and
  `logCursor` (a malformed `before` cursor); `outOfRange` on `maxBanTime` carries
  `minField: banTime` when the ban time is the limit, and `mustNotExceed` (params `field:
  maxBanTime`, `value`) is used on `banTime` when only the ban time was sent; `reserved` (param
  `reserved`, the refused networks) for a denylist entry that would ban everything or mailcow's
  internal network; `conflictsWith` (params `field`, `value`) for an entry on both lists;
  `invalidRegex` (param `error`, the Python `re` compiler message) for a ban rule that does not
  compile; `missingCaptureGroup` (a ban rule without a capture group for the client address).
- Quarantine, spam policy and rate limits (feature 006): `invalidFormat` also uses `format:
  email`, `domainName` and `senderPattern` (an allow or block list pattern with characters other
  than `a-z`, `0-9`, `@`, `_`, `.`, `-`, `*`, or without a letter or digit); `notMultipleOf`
  (param `factor`: `1048576` for the maximum message size, `0.1` for spam scores);
  `mustNotExceed` (params `field: rejectScore` and `value`) for a junk score above the reject
  score; `tooLong` with `unit: bytes` for the notification template; `tooMany` (param `max`, the
  bulk limit) for bulk targets; `notFound` for an excluded domain that is neither a domain nor an
  alias domain; `invalidTemplate` (a notification template the legacy notifier cannot use,
  params `reason`: `syntax`, `security`, `render` or `timeout`, and `line` when known).
- System settings (feature 013): `invalidFormat` also uses `format: email`, `singleLine` (no
  line breaks or other control characters), `appLinkUrl` (absolute `http`/`https` URL or a path
  starting with a single `/`), `hexColor` (`#RRGGBB`) and `origin` (`scheme://host[:port]` or
  `*`); `tooLong` with `unit: bytes` for templates, rules, maps, scripts, bodies and logo files
  (reported on `body`); `outOfRange` (`min: 3`, `max: 64`) for the password policy length;
  `notFound` and `notEligible` (param `reason`: `notReceiving` or `outsideSelectedDomains`) for
  mass mail selection entries; `unsupportedImageType` (param `allowed`, the accepted media types);
  `invalidImage` (a raster image that does not decode); `imageDimensionsExceeded` (params
  `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `width`, `height`); `unsafeSvgContent` (params `construct`, for example
  `scriptElement`, `eventHandlerAttribute`, `scriptUrl`, `foreignContent`, `externalReference`,
  `styleImport`, `doctype`, `notWellFormed` or `rootNotSvg`, and `line` when known);
  `insufficientContrast` (params `ratio`, rounded down to two decimals, `minimum` and `surface`);
  `invalidRegexLine` (params `line`, 1-based, and `reason`: `notSlashDelimited`, `tooManyFlags`,
  `innerSlash` or `doesNotCompile`); feature 005's `sieveSyntax` for global Sieve filters (params
  `message`, the legacy parser's message, and `line`); `unbalancedStructure` (params `line` and `construct`: `unclosedBrace`,
  `unexpectedBrace`, `unclosedBracket`, `unexpectedBracket` or `unclosedString`);
  `mutuallyExclusive` (param `with`, the other field); `tooFew` (param `min`) for a mass mail
  selection without recipients and for an empty list of the legacy API's CORS methods.
- Aliases, alias domains, resources and sender settings (feature 004): `invalidFormat` also uses
  `format: aliasAddress` (an address or `@domain`), `emailOrDomain` (an external sender address
  or domain), `senderPermission` (an address, a domain or `*`) and `resourceDescription` (a
  description that yields 1 to 64 ASCII letters or digits for the derived address), next to
  `email`, `domainName` and `dkimSelector`; `tooLong` carries `unit: bytes` for comments (`max`
  160) and `unit: characters` for the joined destination list (`max` 65535); `notEligible` uses
  `kind` (`resource` for a destination, `externalDestination` for an added external destination
  while the server disables them for every role, `relayDomain` or `aliasDomain` for a target or
  resource domain, `localDomain` for an external sender address in a domain of this server) and
  `allowedRoles: [admin]` for "any address"; `conflictsWith` (params `field`, `value`) for a
  destination equal to the alias's own address, an alias domain equal to its target, destinations
  sent with a special action, and a booking limit sent with a rule other than `limited`;
  `reserved` for an alias domain named like the server; `immutable` for a read-only member sent
  back with a different value.
- Account self-service (feature 005): password rules use feature 003's codes (`tooShort` with the
  policy's `min`, `missingCharacterClass`); `preHashedPassword` (a new password that starts with
  a hash-scheme prefix such as `{SSHA512}`, param `scheme`); `sieveSyntax` (a Sieve script the
  legacy parser rejects, params `message`, the parser's message, and `line` when known);
  `invalidFormat` also uses `format: email`, `pushoverCredential` (30 letters or digits),
  `soundName` and `digits`; `invalidRegex` for a sender pattern that does not compile;
  `secretRequired` (param `reason: noStoredSecret`) for a Pushover token or user key missing while
  none is stored; `notInList` (param `allowed`) for a temporary-alias domain; `tooLong` with `unit:
  bytes` for scripts and with `stored: true` for names whose HTML-encoded form exceeds 255;
  `mutuallyExclusive` (param `with`) for `password` with `generatePassword`; `tooMany` (param `max`,
  the bulk limit) for bulk targets.

FieldViolation.description: One violated validation rule of one field.

params.description:
Parameters of the rule, for building a translated message. Known keys: `min`, `max`
(numbers), `allowed` (list of allowed values), `format` (name of the expected format, see
`ValidationRuleCode`), `expected` (expected JSON type) and `allowedRoles`.

message.description: English message for logs and scripts. Clients translate from `code` and `params`.

ValidationProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/validation-failed` (status `422`). `errors` maps each invalid
field to its violations. Body fields use their dot-separated path in the request body
(`allowedNetworks.2`); query parameters use their name (`limit`); the key `body` stands for the
request body as a whole (for example an empty merge patch).

language.message: The selected language is not enabled on this server.

TooManyRequestsProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/too-many-requests` (status `429`). The `Retry-After` header
carries the same value as `retryAfter`.

retryAfter.description: Seconds until the next attempt will be considered.

Base64Url.description: Unpadded base64url encoding (RFC 4648, section 5) of binary data.

WebAuthnRequestOptions.description:
`PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3. Pass it to
`PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON()` and then to `navigator.credentials.get()`.

rpId.description: Host name serving the API and the web app.

allowCredentials.description: Empty for passkey sign-in (discoverable credentials); the account's WebAuthn second factors otherwise.

extensions.description: Client extension inputs. The second-factor challenge sets `appid` as legacy mailcow does.

WebAuthnChallenge.description: A single-use WebAuthn challenge bound to the session.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after issue. The challenge is consumed by the first verification attempt.

TotpSecondFactor.description:
A code from the authenticator app enrolled as method `methodId`. A code accepted once is not
accepted again within its validity window.

methodId.description: `id` of a `totp` method of the pending sign-in.

WebAuthnAuthenticationResponse.description:
`AuthenticationResponseJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3, as returned by
`PublicKeyCredential.prototype.toJSON()` after `navigator.credentials.get()`.

WebAuthnSecondFactor.description:
Assertion for the challenge from `POST /session/pending-sign-in/webauthn-challenge`. The
credential must be one of the pending sign-in's `webauthn` methods.

YubiOtpSecondFactor.description:
A Yubico OTP. The key is identified by the OTP's public ID among the account's active Yubico OTP
methods and verified against the Yubico service with the credentials stored in mailcow.

SecondFactorVerification.description: Proof for one of the pending sign-in's methods.

PasskeySignInRequest.description:
Assertion for the challenge from `POST /session/passkey-challenge`. The account is the owner of
the credential. With `role`, the sign-in fails unless that account is of that role.

IdentityProviderType.description:
Type of the external identity provider, stored by mailcow as `keycloak`, `generic-oidc` or
`ldap` (setting `authsource` of table `identity_provider`, and `mailbox.authsource`).
- `keycloak`: a Keycloak realm. Single sign-on, and password sign-in through the mailpassword
  flow when it is on. User import and periodic full synchronisation.
- `genericOidc`: any OpenID Connect provider. Single sign-on only, no synchronisation.
- `ldap`: an LDAP directory. Password sign-in against the directory, user import and periodic
  full synchronisation. No single sign-on.

ApiKeyAccessLevel.description: `readOnly` keys may only call safe methods (GET, HEAD); `readWrite` keys may also change state.

IdentityAuthentication.description:
How the caller authenticated. `apiKey` is present only when `method` is `apiKey`.
`identityProvider` is present only for sign-ins through the identity provider (`singleSignOn`,
`directoryPassword*`, `providerPassword*`, feature 012).

prefix.description: Non-secret leading characters of the key.

Scope.description:
Objects the caller may reach: every domain for an administrator, the managed domains for a
domain administrator (active assignments in mailcow's `domain_admins`), the own mailbox for a
mailbox user. A domain administrator without domains has an empty list.

PermissionFlags.description:
Effective permission flags, named after the columns of mailcow's `user_acl` and `da_acl` tables
in camelCase. An administrator has every flag. A domain administrator has every `user_acl` flag,
overridden by its own `da_acl` row where the names overlap (`syncjobs`, `quarantine`,
`appPasswds`, `pushover`, `spamPolicy`). A mailbox user has its `user_acl` row and `false` for
the flags that exist only in `da_acl`. This is the legacy `acl('to_session')` logic.

Preferences.description:
Per-account web app preferences, stored by this API and shared by every device. Defaults: the
server's default language and `system`. A stored language that is no longer enabled falls back
to the default language.

language.description: One of the enabled language codes from `GET /public-config`.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing the resource.

Identity.description:
The authenticated caller. Role, scope, permission flags, account status and pending actions are
evaluated from mailcow's current data on every request, so changes made in either UI apply to
the next request. For an API key, `username` and `role` are those of the key's owner.

pendingActions.description: Pending actions of a session. Always empty for an API key, which is never restricted.

impersonation.description:
Present while the session impersonates another account (feature 007). `username`, `role`,
`scope` and `permissions` then describe the impersonated account, with the permission flags
legacy grants to impersonators; `authentication`, `pendingActions` and `preferences` are the
impersonator's.

webmailOnBehalfEnabled.description:
Present for administrators and domain administrators (feature 007): whether the server
setting `ALLOW_ADMIN_EMAIL_LOGIN` allows opening a mailbox's webmail on the user's behalf. A
domain administrator also needs the `loginAs` flag, and no webmail sign-in is possible while
impersonating.

PreferencesPatch.description: JSON Merge Patch of `Preferences`. Omitted members stay unchanged.

language.description: Must be one of the enabled language codes.

Passkey.description:
A passkey of the signed-in account: a discoverable WebAuthn credential stored where legacy
mailcow stores FIDO2 credentials (table `fido2`), so it works in both UIs.

id.description: Non-secret identifier, the SHA-256 of the credential ID in hex (the legacy `cid`).

name.description: Display name chosen by the user (`fido2.friendlyName`), `null` when never set.

authenticatorDescription.description:
Subject of the attestation certificate (`fido2.certificateSubject`), `null` when the
