authenticator sent none. Legacy shows "Unknown" with the registration date in that case.

hostName.description: Host name the passkey is bound to (`fido2.rpId`). It only works on that host.

active.description: Inactive passkeys cannot sign in (`fido2.active`).

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing the resource.

ListMeta.description: Pagination metadata of a list response.

total.description: Number of items matching the filters, ignoring `limit` and `offset`.

WebAuthnRegistrationResponse.description:
`RegistrationResponseJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3, as returned by
`PublicKeyCredential.prototype.toJSON()` after `navigator.credentials.create()`.

PasskeyRegistrationRequest.description: Authenticator response to the options from `POST /me/passkeys/registration-options`.

name.description: Optional display name. It can be set or changed later with `PATCH`.

WebAuthnCreationOptions.description:
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` of WebAuthn Level 3. Pass it to
`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON()` and then to `navigator.credentials.create()`.

alg.description: COSE algorithm identifier (for example -7 for ES256, -257 for RS256).

excludeCredentials.description: Passkeys already registered to the account, so the authenticator refuses duplicates.

attestation.description:
As legacy requests it: `none` when mailcow's `FIDO2_FORMATS` only allows `none`, `direct`
when only trusted vendors are accepted (`WEBAUTHN_ONLY_TRUSTED_VENDORS=y`, whose attestation
certificates are verified), `indirect` otherwise, so that browsers show no attestation
privacy prompt.

PasskeyRegistrationOptions.description: Single-use passkey registration options bound to the session.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after issue. The options are consumed by the first registration attempt.

PasskeyPatch.description: JSON Merge Patch of a passkey. Only the display name can change.

ApiKeyStatus.description:
`revoked` once revoked (final), otherwise `expired` once `expiresAt` has passed, otherwise
`active`. A key whose owner is inactive or deleted keeps its status but is rejected as invalid
(see `owner.active`).

ApiKeyOwner.description:
The account whose role, scope and permission flags the key acts with, evaluated on every
request. `role` is `null` when the account no longer exists.

active.description: `false` when the owner is deactivated or deleted. The key is then rejected as invalid.

AccountRef.description: Reference to a mailcow account by username.

ApiKey.description: An API key. The secret is never returned after creation.

prefix.description: Non-secret leading characters of the secret, for recognising the key.

allowedNetworks.description: Normalised IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes. Empty means any address.

lastUsedAt.description: Accurate to the minute. `null` when never used.

lastUsedFrom.description: Client address of the last use.

revocationReason.description:
Feature 007: why the key was revoked. `manual`: an administrator revoked it. `ownerDeleted`:
its owner's account was deleted, and `revokedBy` is the deleting administrator. `null` while
the key is not revoked.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings (not of `lastUsedAt`, `lastUsedFrom` or `status`), equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing the resource.

ApiKeyCreateRequest.description:
A new API key. Keys cannot be edited: to change the access level, networks or expiry, create a
new key and revoke the old one.

ownerUsername.description: An existing administrator or domain administrator. Mailbox users cannot own keys.

expiresAt.description: Must be in the future. Omit or send `null` for a key that never expires.

allowedNetworks.description: IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or prefixes. Omit or send an empty list to allow any address.

ApiKeyCreated.description: A newly created API key with its secret. The secret is shown only in this response.

secret.description: Send it in the `X-API-Key` header. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.

ApiKeyOwnerCandidate.description: An active administrator or domain administrator that can own an API key.

Logo.description:
A logo. When the operator uploaded one, `url` points to `GET /public-config/logos/{variant}`
with a version parameter that changes with the image. Otherwise `url` is the default logo of
the deployed legacy UI (`/img/cow_mailcow.svg` upstream), served by the legacy web root.

Announcement.description: Announcement banner (`UI_ANNOUNCEMENT_*`). The text is plain text.

active.description: Show the banner only when `active` is `true` and `text` is not `null`.

LoginPageOptions.description: Login page options (`CUSTOM_LOGIN`). All default to `false`.

hideDomainAdminLogin.description: Hide the domain administrator login link (`hide_domainadmin_quicklink`).

hideMailboxUserLogin.description: Hide the mailbox user login link (`hide_user_quicklink`).

forceSingleSignOn.description:
Legacy hides the password form in favour of identity-provider sign-in (`force_sso`). When it
is set and `externalIdentityProvider.singleSignOnAvailable` is `true`, clients offer single
sign-on instead of the password form on the mailbox-user sign-in screen and keep passkey
sign-in. Display-only: the API refuses no sign-in method because of it (feature 012).

name.description: Native name as configured in mailcow.

AppLink.description:
A link of the apps menu. Built-in apps (`source: builtIn`) come from mailcow's `$MAILCOW_APPS`
(by default Webmail at `/SOGo/so`). Operator links (`source: operator`) come from the legacy
customisation "App links" (Redis `APP_LINKS`). Addresses are as configured: relative to the
mailcow host or absolute.

url.description: Address used on the login page (legacy `link`).

signedInUrl.description:
Address used for signed-in users (legacy `user_link`, or `link` when unset). It may contain
the placeholder `%u`, which the client replaces with the signed-in username, as legacy does.

description.description: Tooltip text of a built-in app (`$MAILCOW_APPS` `description`), `null` otherwise.

showOnLoginPage.description:
`false` when the link is hidden (legacy `hide`). Hiding applies only to the login page; the
apps menu of signed-in users shows every link.

EffectiveBrandColor.description:
A brand colour in effect for one theme, with the foreground colour (black or white) that has the
higher WCAG 2.2 contrast on it, at least 4.5:1.

EffectiveBrandColors.description:
Brand colours in effect for the light and dark themes. `null` for a theme means no brand colour:
the client uses its own palette there. The light colour applies to the light theme. The dark
theme uses the dark colour, or the light colour when no dark colour is set and the light colour
reaches 4.5:1 against the dark reference surface `#1d2939`, otherwise none.

PublicConfig.description:
Branding and login page settings for signed-out clients. Values come from mailcow's existing
customisation (the legacy admin UI's "Customize" screen) and language settings, so the
operator configures them in one place. Unset values fall back to the defaults the deployed
legacy UI shows. Contains no secrets and nothing account-specific.

`loginHelpHtml` and `footerHtml` contain operator-authored HTML, rendered unescaped by the
legacy UI. Clients must sanitise them before rendering. Every other text is plain text.

productName.description: Name shown on the login page (`MAIN_NAME`). Same default as `pageTitle`.

loginHelpHtml.description: Operator HTML shown below the login form (`HELP_TEXT`), `null` when unset.

configured.description:
`true` when mailcow has an external identity provider (Keycloak, generic OIDC or LDAP)
configured. Mailboxes of an LDAP provider, or of Keycloak with the mailpassword flow,
sign in with their password through `POST /session` (feature 012).

singleSignOnAvailable.description:
`true` when a complete Keycloak or generic OIDC configuration exists, so that mailbox
users can sign in with `POST /session/single-sign-on` (feature 012). Offer it on the
mailbox-user and role-neutral sign-in screens, never on the administrator screens.

appsLabel.description:
Label of the apps menu set by the operator (`APPS_NAME`, plain text). `null` when unset; the
client then shows its own translated "Apps".

appLinks.description:
App links in legacy order: built-in apps first, then operator links in their stored order.
Built-in apps that point to SOGo are left out when SOGo is disabled (`SKIP_SOGO=y`). Show the
login-page block only when at least one link has `showOnLoginPage: true`.

brandColors.description:
Brand colours in effect for the light and dark themes, with their foregrounds, set by
administrators through feature 013 (`PATCH /settings/brand-colors`) and stored by this API.
`null` for a theme means the client uses its own palette there. Every colour reaches at least
4.5:1 against its theme's reference surface and with its foreground. Added by feature 013:
a server without it omits the member, which clients treat like two `null` themes.

AuditEventType.description: Audited event. Later features add values; clients must tolerate unknown ones.

AuditActor.description:
Who acted. For a failed sign-in, `username` is the attempted username when one is known and
`role` may be `null`. `apiKeyId` is set when the request was authenticated by an API key.

AuditFailureReason.description:
Why an audited operation failed. Later features add values.

- `invalidCredentials`: unknown account, wrong password or malformed username.
- `accountInactive`: inactive account, inactive domain or resource mailbox.
- `externalIdentitySource`: the mailbox authenticates against LDAP or an OIDC provider.
- `unknownPasskey`, `passkeyInactive`, `roleMismatch`, `passkeyVerificationFailed`.
- `challengeExpired`: pending sign-in, challenge or registration options missing, used or expired.
- `secondFactorFailed`, `secondFactorUnavailable`, `verificationUnavailable` (Yubico service).
- `throttled`: refused by sign-in throttling without checking credentials.
- `registrationFailed`: the authenticator's registration response was rejected.
- Refused changes of mail objects (feature 002 onwards; `details.problemType` holds the
  problem type and `details.errors` the field errors): `attributeNotPermitted`,
  `versionOutdated` (`If-Match` or bulk item version mismatch), `validationFailed`, `conflict`
  (for example an existing name or a non-empty domain), `temporaryFailure` (shared store
  unavailable).
- Sync jobs (feature 008) also use `permissionDenied` (the caller lacks the permission flag that
  gates the operation, here `syncjobs`) and `notFound` (the object or a referenced object does
  not exist or lies outside the caller's scope).
- Identity providers (feature 012), for sign-ins through a provider and session ends:
  `signInStateInvalid` (single sign-on state unknown, expired, used or foreign),
  `singleSignOnNotAvailable`, `providerRefused` (the provider refused the code, the token
  renewal or the user details), `providerReturnedError` (the provider returned the browser with
  an error; `details.providerError` holds its code), `identityProviderUnavailable` (unreachable,
  timed out, server error or service account refused), `noEmailAddress`, `mailboxNotLinked`
  (the mailbox's authentication source is not the configured type), `autoCreationOff`,
  `noMatchingMapping` (no mapping entry and no default template), `mailboxCreationFailed`
  (`details.cause` holds the reason, for example `templateMissing`, `domainNotFound`,
  `addressInUse` or `mailboxLimitReached`), `passwordNotVerifiable` (no `mailcow_password`
  value, or the source cannot verify passwords). Connection tests use `connectionTestFailed`
  with `details.failureCategory`.
- Mailboxes (feature 003) also use `outcomeUnknown` (the container API timed out; the step is in
  `details.steps` or `details.mailStoreCleanup`) and `partiallyCompleted` (a rename could neither
  complete nor be undone; `details.steps` lists every step).
- Monitoring and operations (feature 011) use `permissionDenied` (role, read-only key or
  restricted session, told apart by `details.problemType`), `validationFailed`, `conflict`
  (container protected, container or mail service not running; `details.problemType` names it),
  `notFound`, `versionOutdated`, `temporaryFailure` and `outcomeUnknown` (the container service
  timed out), plus
  `serviceFailure` (the container service or Postfix reported a failure; `details.serviceMessage`)
  and `rulesNotRestored` (the ban rules were reset but the defaults did not reappear in time).
- System settings (feature 013) use `validationFailed`, `versionOutdated`, `notFound`,
  `permissionDenied` (the caller's role may never use the operation), `conflict` (mass mail
  already running, recipient count changed, cancelling a completed job), `temporaryFailure`,
  `serviceFailure` and `outcomeUnknown` (container service), plus `demoMode` (customisation
  refused in demo mode), `featureDisabled` (license verification disabled) and `fileUnavailable`
  (the shared map or filter file does not exist).
- Account self-service (feature 005) uses `externalIdentitySource` (password managed
  externally), `permissionDenied` (a missing permission flag, `details.requiredFlags`), `versionOutdated`,
  `validationFailed`, `temporaryFailure`, `notFound`, `throttled`, `challengeExpired` (enrolment
  expired), `registrationFailed` (enrolment rejected), `secondFactorFailed`,
  `secondFactorUnavailable`, `verificationUnavailable` and `featureDisabled` (groupware disabled,
  password reset unavailable), plus `currentPasswordIncorrect`, `lastSecondFactor`,
  `secondFactorRequiredByPolicy`, `notConfigured` (no Pushover credentials stored),
  `invalidResetToken`, and for reset requests `unknownAccount`, `accountNotEligible` (inactive,
  resource or external-source mailbox), `noRecoveryEmail`, `tokenLimitReached` and
  `messageNotSent`.

AuditImpersonatedAccount.description: The account that was impersonated when the audited action happened.

AuditEvent.description:
One immutable audit record. Never contains passwords, one-time codes, WebAuthn assertions, key
secrets or session identifiers.

clientAddress.description: Real client address as seen by mailcow's reverse proxy.

details.description:
Non-secret event details with stable camelCase keys, for example `requestedRole`,
`secondFactorType`, `changedFields` or `accessLevel`. The keys of each event type, their
types and whether they can be absent are documented in `docs/audit-events.md`. Show
unknown keys verbatim.

impersonatedAccount.description:
Feature 007: the impersonated account when the record was written during an impersonation,
by any feature. `actor` is then the impersonator. `null` (or absent in records written before
feature 007) outside impersonations.

HealthCheckStatus.description:
`ok`, or `failed`. For `schema`, `failed` means the mailcow database schema version
(`versions.db_schema`) is not one this release supports.

ReadinessProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/service-unavailable` (status `503`) returned by the readiness
check, with the result of each dependency check.

SyncJobLastResult.description:
Result of the job's last run, as the imapsync runner recorded it (`imapsync.success`):
`succeeded` (1), `failed` (0) or `unknown` (empty: the job never ran, a run is in progress, or the
result was cleared by a reschedule).

SyncJobEncryption.description:
Transport encryption to the remote IMAP server. `ssl`: implicit TLS (imapsync `--ssl1`, stored
as `SSL`). `starttls`: STARTTLS on a plain connection (imapsync `--tls1`, stored as `TLS`).
`plain`: no encryption (stored as `PLAIN`), as in legacy.

SyncJobRunStatus.description:
Run status maintained by mailcow's imapsync runner in the dovecot container. It is read-only,
except that rescheduling (`POST /sync-jobs/{syncJobId}/schedule-reset`) clears `lastRunAt` and
`lastResult`. It is not covered by the job's version tag, so a run never makes an open editor's
version stale.

lastRunAt.description: End of the last run (`imapsync.last_run`), `null` when the job never ran or was rescheduled.

exitStatus.description:
Short machine-readable exit code that the runner parsed from imapsync's output
(`imapsync.exit_status`), `null` when `lastResult` is `unknown` or the runner found none.
Legacy translates these codes: `EX_OK` (success), `EXIT_CONNECTION_FAILURE`,
`EXIT_CONNECTION_FAILURE_HOST1` (cannot connect to the remote server), `EXIT_TLS_FAILURE`,
`EXIT_AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE`, `EXIT_AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE_USER1` (wrong remote username or
password) and `EXIT_OVERQUOTA` (target mailbox over quota). Other codes mean "check the log".

running.description: Whether a run is in progress (`imapsync.is_running`).

logAvailable.description: Whether the runner stored a log for the last run. Read it with `GET /sync-jobs/{syncJobId}/log`.

SyncJob.description:
A sync job: an imapsync task that pulls mail from a remote IMAP account into a local mailbox
(mailcow table `imapsync`). The legacy UI and `/api/v1` edit the same rows.

The remote password is write-only: a response only says whether one is set
(`remotePasswordSet`). It is stored in plain text because the imapsync runner needs it to log in
to the remote server, and it never appears in any response, log or audit record of this API.

mailbox.description: Local mailbox the mail is synced into (`imapsync.user2`). Fixed at creation.

remoteHost.description: Host name or IPv4 address of the remote IMAP server (`imapsync.host1`).

remotePort.description: Port of the remote IMAP server (`imapsync.port1`).

authMechanism.description: Authentication mechanism to the remote server. Always `plain`, as legacy stores it; not settable.

remotePasswordSet.description: Whether a remote password is stored (`imapsync.password1` is not empty). The password itself is never returned.

exclude.description:
Regular expression of remote folders to skip (imapsync `--exclude`, `imapsync.exclude`).
Empty means no exclusion.

destinationSubfolder.description: Folder of the local mailbox that receives the synced folders (imapsync `--subfolder2`). Empty means the mailbox root.

intervalMinutes.description: Minimum time between the end of one run and the start of the next, in minutes (`imapsync.mins_interval`).

maxAgeDays.description: Only messages younger than this many days are synced (imapsync `--maxage`). `0` ignores the age.

maxBytesPerSecond.description: Transfer speed limit in bytes per second (imapsync `--maxbytespersecond`). `0` is unlimited.

remoteTimeoutSeconds.description: Connection timeout to the remote server in seconds (imapsync `--timeout1`).

localTimeoutSeconds.description: Connection timeout to the local mailbox in seconds (imapsync `--timeout2`).

deleteFromSource.description: Delete messages on the remote server after they were synced (imapsync `--delete1`, `imapsync.delete1`).

deleteFromDestination.description: Delete local messages that do not exist on the remote server (imapsync `--delete2`, `imapsync.delete2`).

deleteDuplicatesOnDestination.description: Delete duplicate messages in the local mailbox (imapsync `--delete2duplicates`).

automap.description: Map well-known remote folders (Sent, Trash, …) to the local ones (imapsync `--automap`).

skipCrossDuplicates.description: Skip messages that exist in another folder of the local mailbox (imapsync `--skipcrossduplicates`).

subscribeAll.description: Subscribe the local mailbox to every synced folder (imapsync `--subscribeall`).

dryRun.description: Simulate the sync without transferring anything (imapsync `--dry`).

customParameters.description:
Additional imapsync options, as stored (`imapsync.custom_params`), for example
`--maxsize=10000000 --nofoldersizesatend`. Only options on the server's allow-list are
accepted; see `SyncJobCreateRequest.customParameters`.

active.description: Inactive jobs are never run.

modifiedAt.description:
Last change of the row (`imapsync.modified`), including the runner's status updates. `null`
when the row never changed after its creation.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored configuration (remote connection, remote password, options,
custom parameters, active flag and target mailbox), equal to the `ETag` header of a single
read. It does not cover `runStatus` or `modifiedAt`, so runs and reschedules never change it.
Send it in `If-Match` when changing or deleting the job.

SyncJobPermissionFlagProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required` (status `403`): the caller is a domain
administrator or mailbox user without the `syncjobs` permission flag (`da_acl.syncjobs` or
`user_acl.syncjobs`), which every sync-job operation needs. The flag is checked before any object
is looked up, so the answer reveals nothing about objects outside the caller's scope. Nothing
changed.

requiredFlags.description: Names of the missing flags, as in `PermissionFlags`. For sync jobs always `[syncjobs]`.

SyncJobCreateRequest.description:
A new sync job. Omitted members take the defaults of the legacy "Add sync job" form, which the
capabilities read (`GET /capabilities/sync-jobs`, `defaults`) also lists. The remote host, port,
user and password are always required. Unknown members are ignored.

Every invalid member is reported at once in a `422` problem, with these rule codes besides the
common ones (`required`, `invalidType`, `tooShort`, `tooLong`, `outOfRange`, `notInList`,
`invalidFormat`):

- `remoteHost`: `invalidFormat` with `format: hostName`.
- `exclude`: `invalidRegex`.
- `customParameters`: `optionNotAllowed` (param `option`), `optionContainsSpace` (param `token`)
  and `customParamsNotPermitted`.
- `mailbox`: `notEligible` (param `kind`: `resource`, `alias` or `aliasDomainAddress`) when the
  address is not a mailbox that can receive synced mail.

mailbox.description:
Local mailbox to sync into. Required for administrators and domain administrators. A mailbox
user may omit it or send their own address; their job always targets their own mailbox. An
address that does not exist or lies outside the caller's scope answers `404`. A resource, an
alias or an address of an alias domain is refused with `notEligible`.

remoteHost.description:
Host name (letter/digit labels with inner hyphens, at most 253 characters, labels at most
63; internationalised names are accepted) or IPv4 address. IPv6 literals are refused, as in
legacy. Stored in lower case.

remotePassword.description: Password of the remote account. Stored for the runner, never returned.

exclude.description:
Regular expression of remote folders to skip. Send an empty string for no exclusion. It must
compile as a PCRE pattern between `/` delimiters, exactly as legacy checks it, so a literal
`/` must be escaped as `\/`.

customParameters.description:
Additional imapsync options, written `--option` or `--option=value` and separated by spaces,
for example `--maxsize=10000000 --nofoldersizesatend`. The value is trimmed and checked
exactly as legacy checks it: it is split at every hyphen, and each piece's option name (the
text before `=`) must be on the server's allow-list (`optionNotAllowed`) and must not contain
a space (`optionContainsSpace`, so `--option value` is refused; write `--option=value`). A
value that itself contains a hyphen is therefore refused unless the text after the hyphen is
an allowed option name. `showpasswords` is always refused, so the remote password can never
be written into the run log. The allow-list in effect is in the capabilities read. When the
server restricts custom parameters to administrators, any non-empty value from another role
is refused with `customParamsNotPermitted`.

active.description: An active job is picked up by the imapsync runner on its next cycle.

SyncJobRange.description: Inclusive range of a whole-number field.

SyncJobDefaults.description:
Values a new sync job gets for omitted members: the values the legacy "Add sync job" form
pre-fills. The remote host, port, user and password have no default.

SyncJobCapabilities.description:
Server settings and limits a client needs before it submits a sync job, computed from the
server's current configuration for the calling account. Contains no secret.

allowed.description:
Whether the caller may set custom imapsync parameters. `false` when the server restricts
them to administrators and the caller is not one; such a caller may still send the
stored value unchanged.

restrictedToAdministrators.description: The server setting that restricts custom parameters to administrators (legacy default `false`).

allowedOptions.description:
Option names on the allow-list in effect, as configured (without leading hyphens), in the
server's order. A custom option is accepted when its lower-cased name equals one of them.
Never contains `showpasswords`.

bulkLimit.description: Maximum number of sync jobs in one bulk action (default 100).

limits.description: Ranges of the whole-number fields and maximum lengths of the text fields.

SyncJobBulkAction.description:
Action of a sync-job bulk request, as the legacy mass actions offer them. `activate` and
`deactivate` set the active flag. `reschedule` clears the last run time and last result, so the
runner picks the job up on its next cycle; it ignores version tags, because it changes only run
status. `delete` removes the job.

BulkTarget.description:
One target of a bulk action. Features reference this schema or extend it with `allOf`. `version`
is the object's version tag as last read. When present and outdated, the item's outcome is
`outdated` and the other items proceed. When absent, the item is not version-checked. An object
named twice is processed once.

id.description: Identifier of the object, as used in the object's own path.

version.description:
The object's version tag as last read: the exact value of its `ETag` header or `etag` member,
which carries the quotes of a strong ETag (`"Zm9v…"`). The value is also accepted without the
quotes. When it no longer matches, the item's outcome is `outdated` with a `412` problem.

SyncJobBulkActionRequest.description:
One action applied to several sync jobs. The number of targets must not exceed the bulk limit
(default 100, see `GET /capabilities/sync-jobs`); a larger request is refused with `tooMany`
(param `max`) on `targets`. A malformed target refuses the whole request, with every bad target
named. A job named twice is processed and reported once.

BulkItemOutcome.description:
Result of one item of a bulk action (see `docs/conventions.md`). `done`: the action was applied.
`notFound`: the object does not exist or is outside the caller's scope. `refused`: the action is
not allowed for this object, or the object's state does not permit it (the item's `problem` says
why). `outdated`: the item carried a version tag that no longer matches. `failed`: an unexpected
or downstream failure, including an unknown outcome after a timeout.

BulkItemResult.description: Outcome of one target of a bulk action. Results are returned in request order.

id.description: Identifier of the target, as sent.

version.description: The object's new version tag after a `done` outcome, if the object still exists.

problem.description: Present for `refused`, `outdated` and `failed`. Explains the item's outcome.

bulkRequestId.description: Identifier of the bulk request (its request ID).

SyncJobPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a sync job. Omitted members keep their values; a body without any of the
members below is refused (`required` on `body`). `null` is refused for every member
(`invalidType`). A member whose value differs from the stored one is validated with the rules of
`SyncJobCreateRequest`; a member sent with its stored value, and every member not sent, is
accepted as stored, even if it predates the current rules. Unknown and read-only members (`id`,
`runStatus`, `etag`, …) are ignored, so a client may send back what it read.

- `active` activates or deactivates the job; the change takes effect from the runner's next
  cycle and never interrupts a run in progress.
- `remotePassword`: a non-empty value replaces the stored password; an empty string keeps it.
- `mailbox` cannot change: the current address is accepted, any other is refused with the rule
  code `immutable`. To sync into another mailbox, create a new job.
- `customParameters`: when the server restricts custom parameters to administrators, a value
  from another role that differs from the stored one is refused with `customParamsNotPermitted`;
  the stored value sent unchanged is accepted.

SyncJobLog.description:
The run log of a sync job: the output of its last imapsync run as the runner stored it
(`imapsync.returned_text`). The text is produced by the remote server and by imapsync, not by
this API. The runner masks passwords in it, and this API refuses the `showpasswords` option, so
the remote password does not appear. Clients must render it as plain text, never as HTML. It can
be large (several megabytes for big mailboxes).

log.description: The stored output, empty when there is none. Invalid UTF-8 sequences are replaced by U+FFFD.

DomainTagList.description:
Tags of a domain, sorted alphabetically without regard to letter case. Tags that differ only in
letter case are one tag. Each tag is trimmed, 1 to 255 characters long. A request may not leave a
domain with more tags than the server's tagging limit (`DomainCapabilities.taggingLimit`, 25 by
default); a domain that already has more can only shrink. Sending tags replaces the whole set.

DomainRelayhost.description:
The relayhost assigned to a domain (mailcow `domain.relayhost`, an ID in `relayhosts`). Read-only
in this feature; relayhosts and their assignment are managed by the routing feature.

hostname.description: Host name of the relayhost, `null` when the referenced relayhost no longer exists.

DomainRateLimit.description:
A rate limit: at most `value` messages per `frame`. mailcow stores it in its shared store
(`RL_VALUE`, for example `10 / 1h`).

DomainUsage.description:
Usage figures, computed from mailcow's data on every request exactly as the legacy UI computes
them. They are not covered by the version tag. Resources are mailboxes of kind location, thing or
group. Quotas and storage are bytes.

mailboxes.description: Mailboxes of the domain, not counting resources.

resources.description: Resources of the domain. Like mailboxes, they block a deletion.

aliases.description:
Aliases whose address is in the domain or in one of its alias domains, not counting aliases
whose address is itself a mailbox.

aliasDomains.description: Alias domains that point to the domain.

mailboxesLeft.description: `maxMailboxes` minus `mailboxes`. Negative when the limit is below usage.

aliasesLeft.description: `maxAliases` minus `aliases`. Negative when the limit is below usage.

largestMailboxQuota.description:
Largest quota of an existing mailbox, not counting resources. `maxMailboxQuota` cannot be set
below it.

quotaAllocated.description:
Sum of the quotas of the domain's mailboxes, not counting resources. Mailboxes with unlimited
quota allocate nothing. `domainQuota` cannot be set below it.

storageUsed.description: Bytes stored by all mailboxes of the domain, resources included.

messages.description: Messages stored by all mailboxes of the domain, resources included.

maxNewMailboxQuota.description:
Largest quota a new mailbox may get: `domainQuota` minus `quotaAllocated`, capped at
`maxMailboxQuota`, never below zero.

DomainFooterSummary.description:
A summary of the domain's footer (G28), so that the domain page needs no footer read: whether a
footer adds text, the sizes of its texts and the numbers of exclusions. Read the footer itself
with `getDomainFooter`. Not covered by the domain's version tag (the footer has its own).

set.description: Whether a footer with a non-empty HTML or plain text is stored.

htmlBytes.description: Size of the HTML text in bytes (UTF-8); 0 without a footer.

plainBytes.description: Size of the plain text in bytes (UTF-8); 0 without a footer.

Domain.description:
A mail domain (mailcow tables `domain` and `tags_domain`). Quotas are bytes; mailcow stores them in
whole mebibytes, so they are always multiples of 1,048,576. `relayhost` and `rateLimit` are
read-only here: the routing feature assigns relayhosts, and the spam policy feature changes rate
limits.

name.description: Lower-case ASCII (punycode) name, the identifier used in paths. Never changes.

unicodeName.description: Readable (Unicode) form of `name`. Equal to `name` for ASCII-only names.

description.description: Free text. Defaults to the domain name.

active.description:
Inactive domains receive no mail. They stay visible and editable for their domain
administrators.

maxMailboxQuota.description: Maximum quota of one mailbox, bytes (`domain.maxquota`).

domainQuota.description: Total quota that the domain's mailboxes may allocate, bytes (`domain.quota`).

relayUnknownOnly.description:
Relay only recipients that are not existing mailboxes (`domain.relay_unknown_only`). Implies
`relayAllRecipients` and `backupMx`.

globalAddressList.description:
Whether the groupware shows the domain's Global Address List (`domain.gal`). The groupware
reads it only when it starts: a change takes effect at its next restart.

relayhost.description: Assigned relayhost, `null` for none. Read-only in this feature.

rateLimit.description:
Rate limit of the domain from mailcow's shared store, `null` for none. Read-only after
creation in this feature.

modifiedAt.description: Last change of the domain row, `null` when never modified.

domainAdmins.description:
Usernames of the domain administrators assigned to the domain (mailcow `domain_admins`),
sorted. Present for administrators only; domain administrators never receive it.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings and tags (not of `usage`, `rateLimit` or
`domainAdmins`), equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. It changes whenever the
stored settings change, also through the legacy UI or `/api/v1`. Send it in `If-Match`.

DomainCreateRequest.description:
A new domain. Only `name` is required. Every omitted attribute takes its value from the chosen
template (`templateId`), or from the Default template when none is named. When the Default
template is missing, the built-in values apply: 10 mailboxes, 400 aliases, 10,240 MiB maximum
mailbox quota, 10,240 MiB domain quota, active, Global Address List on, no relay options, no tags,
no rate limit, the server's default DKIM selector and 2,048-bit keys.

Rules: quotas are whole multiples of 1 MiB (`notMultipleOf`); `maxMailboxQuota` ≤ `domainQuota`
(`mustNotExceed`); relay options are normalised (`relayUnknownOnly` implies `relayAllRecipients`,
which implies `backupMx`).

mailcow's default mailbox quota of a domain is not part of this API (owner decision 2026-10-18:
an upstream leftover that mailbox templates replace). The server keeps the column valid for the
classic interface: a new domain gets the template's default mailbox quota capped at
`maxMailboxQuota`, or `maxMailboxQuota` when the template has none.

name.description:
ASCII or Unicode, any letter case. It is trimmed, lower-cased and converted to ASCII
(UTS #46). It must consist of dot-separated labels of letters, digits and inner hyphens, at
most 253 characters with labels of at most 63 (`invalidFormat`, `format: domainName`). It may
not equal the server's host name (`reserved`). A name that exists as a domain or alias domain
is refused with `409 domain-exists`.

templateId.description: Domain template whose values pre-fill omitted attributes. An unknown ID is refused (`notFound`).

description.description: Empty or omitted means the domain name.

maxMailboxQuota.description: Bytes, a whole multiple of 1 MiB.

domainQuota.description: Bytes, a whole multiple of 1 MiB.

rateLimit.description: Initial rate limit, applied after the domain is stored. `null` means none, overriding the template.

dkimSelector.description:
Selector of the DKIM key generated for the domain. An empty string means "no DKIM key". When
omitted, the template's selector applies, else the server's default selector
(`DomainCapabilities.dkim.defaultSelector`). No key is generated when one already exists for
the name.

dkimKeySize.description: RSA key size in bits. When omitted, the template's size applies, else 2,048.

restartGroupware.description:
Restart the groupware (SOGo) after the creation, so that it knows the new domain (legacy "Add
domain and restart SOGo"). On a server whose groupware is disabled, this is not an error.

DomainCreationReport.description:
Outcome of each follow-up step of a domain creation. The domain, its tags and its domain map entry
are stored together before these steps run; a failed step never undoes the creation. The same
report is stored in the creation's audit record. Like legacy, a creation does not rebuild the
groupware directory: the new domain has no mailboxes yet.

dkimKey.description: `notRequested` when the selector was explicitly empty.

dkimDnsPublication.description:
Publication of the new DKIM key to the ISPConfig DNS server (FeldHost setting, off by
default). `noZone`: the ISPConfig server has no zone for the domain. `notConfigured`: the
publication is disabled. `skipped`: no new key was generated.

groupwareRestart.description: `failed` also covers a restart whose outcome is unknown after the container service timed out.

messages.description: English explanation of each failed step, keyed by step name. Never contains secrets.

DomainCreated.description: The created domain and the outcome of its follow-up steps.

DomainBulkActionRequest.description:
One action applied to several domains, as the legacy mass actions of the domain list do. Each
target is authorised, version-checked, processed and audited on its own, exactly as the single
operation for it (`updateDomain` with `active`, or `deleteDomain`); one failure does not stop the
others. A target is the domain name in ASCII or Unicode form; a name given twice, also in both
forms, is processed and reported once. At most 100 targets may be sent (`tooMany` on
`targets`, with `max: 100`).

mailboxes.description: Mailboxes that remain in the domain.

resources.description: Resources that remain in the domain.

DomainPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a domain. Omitted members keep their values. A sent value, including zero, is
applied or refused by the rules, never ignored; only the relay normalisation can override a sent
relay option (`relayUnknownOnly` implies `relayAllRecipients`, which implies `backupMx`).

**Who may change what**:
- Administrators: `description`, `active`, `maxMailboxes`, `maxAliases`, `maxMailboxQuota`,
  `domainQuota`, `backupMx`, `relayAllRecipients`, `relayUnknownOnly`, `globalAddressList` and
  `tags`.
- Domain administrators: `globalAddressList` and `tags`, and `description` only with the
  `domainDesc` permission flag. Any other change is refused with `403 attribute-not-permitted`,
  which names the attributes, and nothing changes.

**Unchanged values are always accepted**, so that a client may send back a whole form. The
read-only members (`name`, `unicodeName`, `relayhost`, `rateLimit`, `createdAt`, `modifiedAt`,
`usage`, `footer`, `domainAdmins` and `etag`) are accepted when equal to the current value and refused with
the rule code `immutable` otherwise. Usage figures change with every delivered message, so clients
should not send `usage`.

**Rules**: as for creation, plus: a changed limit may not be below current usage (`belowInUse`,
with the value in use as `inUse`): `maxMailboxes` ≥ `usage.mailboxes`, `maxAliases` ≥
`usage.aliases`, `maxMailboxQuota` ≥ `usage.largestMailboxQuota`, `domainQuota` ≥
`usage.quotaAllocated`. A limit that is not changed is not checked. `maxMailboxQuota` ≤
`domainQuota` (`mustNotExceed`) is checked on the resulting values only when the patch changes
one of the two, so stored quotas that break it never block an edit of other attributes. An
empty `description`, or `null`, stores the domain name.

mailcow's default mailbox quota of a domain is not part of this API (owner decision 2026-10-18).
An edit that changes `maxMailboxQuota` lowers a larger stored default to the new maximum, so that
the classic interface keeps accepting the domain; this is not recorded as a change.

globalAddressList.description: Takes effect in the groupware at its next restart. An edit never restarts it.

name.description: Read-only. Accepted when equal to the current value (ASCII or Unicode form).

etag.description: Read-only. Use `If-Match` for the version check.

DomainAttributeNotPermittedProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/attribute-not-permitted` (status `403`): the request would
change attributes that the caller's role or permission flags do not allow it to change.

attributes.description: Names of the attributes that may not be changed, as in the request body.

DomainAddressSample.description: A count of objects and up to 100 of their addresses, sorted.

DomainDeletionPreview.description:
What deleting the domain would currently be blocked by, remove and keep, computed by the same
rules as the deletion. A snapshot: the deletion checks and computes everything again.

allowed.description: `true` when the domain has no mailboxes and no resources.

aliasDomains.description: ASCII names of the alias domains that point to the domain, sorted.

footer.description: Whether a footer is stored for the domain.

domainAdminsToDelete.description:
Domain administrator accounts that would be deleted because they would be left without any
domain assignment, as legacy mailcow does. Their API keys stop working.

dkimKeyKept.description: Whether a DKIM key exists for the name. A deletion keeps it.

etag.description: The domain's current version tag, to send in `If-Match` with the deletion.

DomainFooter.description:
The domain-wide footer that mailcow's mail filter adds to outgoing mail from the domain and its
alias domains (mailcow table `domain_wide_footer`). A domain without a stored footer returns empty
texts, `skipReplies: false` and no exclusions.

The texts may use these placeholders: `{= auth_user =}` (authenticated user), `{= from_user =}`
(local part of the sender), `{= from_name =}` (sender's display name), `{= from_addr =}` (sender
address), `{= from_domain =}` (sender domain) and `{= <attribute> =}` for a custom attribute of
the sending mailbox. `html` is operator-authored HTML: clients must render it safely (sandboxed or
sanitised), never inject it into their own page.

An exclusion that stopped belonging to the domain, for example a deleted mailbox, stays stored and
is shown, but must be removed or made valid before the footer can be saved again.

skipReplies.description: Do not add the footer to replies.

excludedAddresses.description: Senders (mailbox or alias addresses) whose mail gets no footer.

excludedAliasDomains.description: Alias domains whose mail gets no footer.

etag.description:
Version tag of the footer content. An absent footer and a stored empty footer have the same
tag. Send it in `If-Match`.

DomainFooterReplace.description:
A complete footer that replaces the stored one. Empty texts without exclusions mean that no footer
is added. Each text may be at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes in UTF-8; `tooLong` with `max` and
`unit: bytes`). Duplicate exclusions are stored once.

Each entry of `excludedAddresses` must be the address of a mailbox or alias in the domain or in
one of its alias domains, and each entry of `excludedAliasDomains` the name of one of the domain's
alias domains. Any other entry is refused (`notFound`, keyed by its position, for example
`excludedAddresses.2`), and the stored footer stays unchanged.

DomainDkimCapabilities.description: DKIM defaults for the domain and template forms. Returned to administrators only.

defaultSelector.description: Server setting, `dkim` upstream (`feldhost` on the FeldHost deployment).

defaultKeySize.description: Built-in default key size in bits.

dnsPublicationEnabled.description: Whether new DKIM keys are published to an ISPConfig DNS server (FeldHost setting, off by default).

DomainTemplateDefaults.description:
The values a new domain template gets for every value it omits, which are also the built-in
values of a domain created while no Default template exists (G29). `dkimSelector` is the server's
default selector (`dkim` upstream, `feldhost` on the FeldHost deployment).

DomainCapabilities.description:
Server settings and limits that shape the domain forms, read from the current configuration on
every request. Contains no secret and no connection detail.

groupwareEnabled.description:
`false` when the groupware is disabled (mailcow `SKIP_SOGO=y`). Clients then hide the Global
Address List flag of the creation form and the restart option, as legacy does.

taggingLimit.description: Maximum number of tags per domain (legacy `TAGGING_LIMIT`, 25 by default).

footerTextMaxBytes.description: Maximum size of each footer text in bytes.

bulkLimit.description: Maximum number of targets of one bulk action (100 for every bulk action of the API).

quotaUnit.description: Quotas must be whole multiples of this number of bytes (1 MiB).

templateDefaults.description:
The values of a new domain template that omits them, and the built-in values of a domain
created without a Default template (G29). Returned to administrators only.

DomainTagSummary.description:
One distinct tag among the domains in the caller's scope. Tags that differ only in letter case
are counted together.

name.description: The tag. When domains spell it differently, the alphabetically first spelling.

domainCount.description: Number of domains in the caller's scope that carry the tag.

DomainTemplate.description:
A domain template (mailcow table `templates`, `type = 'domain'`): named values that pre-fill new
domains. Templates only pre-fill: editing or deleting one never changes a domain, and a domain
does not record its template. The template named "Default" (compared case-insensitively) always
exists; it can be edited but not renamed or deleted.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the protected Default template.

dkimSelector.description: Selector for the DKIM key of new domains. Empty means "no DKIM key".

etag.description: Version tag of the template's stored name and values. Send it in `If-Match`.

DomainTemplateCreateRequest.description:
A new domain template. Only `name` is required. Omitted values get the legacy defaults: 10
mailboxes, 400 aliases, 10,240 MiB maximum mailbox quota, 10,240 MiB domain quota, no rate limit, active, Global Address List on, no relay options, no tags, the server's
default DKIM selector and 2,048-bit keys (the `default` keywords below;
`DomainCapabilities.templateDefaults` gives all of them, the selector included). Sent values,
including zero, are kept when valid.

The values follow the domain rules, so that a template always produces a valid domain: quotas
are whole multiples of 1 MiB, `maxMailboxQuota` ≤ `domainQuota`, tags as for domains, and the
relay options are normalised. The name must be unique among domain templates, compared
case-insensitively (`409 domain-template-name-exists`).

The default mailbox quota that mailcow keeps in domain templates (`def_quota_for_mbox`) is not
part of this API (owner decision 2026-10-18: an upstream leftover that mailbox templates
replace). The server stores `maxMailboxQuota` as that value, so that the classic interface's
add-domain form keeps working.

DomainTemplateBulkActionRequest.description:
One action applied to several domain templates, as the legacy mass deletion of the domain
template list does (`delete_selected`). Each target is version-checked, deleted and audited on
its own, exactly as `deleteDomainTemplate`; one failure does not stop the others. A target's `id`
is the template ID as in the template's own path; an unknown ID, a mailbox template's ID or a
value that is not an ID gets `notFound`, and an ID given twice is processed and reported once. At
most 100 targets may be sent (`tooMany` on `targets`, with `max: 100`).

action.description: `delete` deletes the template. The Default template is refused (`domain-template-protected`).

DomainTemplatePatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a domain template. Only the sent values change; every other value is kept.
The rules of `DomainTemplateCreateRequest` apply to the resulting template, except that
`maxMailboxQuota` ≤ `domainQuota` (`mustNotExceed`) is checked only when the patch changes one of
the two, so stored quotas that break it never block an edit of other values. Renaming the Default
template is refused with `409 domain-template-protected` (sending its current name is accepted).
The read-only members (`id`, `isDefault`, `createdAt`, `modifiedAt`, `etag`) are accepted when
equal to the current value and refused with the rule code `immutable` otherwise.

The stored default mailbox quota of the template, which this API does not expose (owner decision
2026-10-18), is lowered to `maxMailboxQuota` when it exceeds it and set to `maxMailboxQuota` when
it is missing or zero; this is not recorded as a change.

etag.description: Read-only. Use `If-Match` for the version check.

AliasKind.description:
`regular`: an address such as `info@example.org`. `catchAll`: an address of the form `@domain`,
which receives mail for every address of the domain that does not otherwise exist on the server.
When a catch-all alias allows sending, its destinations may send as any address of the domain
that has no alias of its own allowing sending (legacy behaviour). Catch-all aliases are never
offered as sender identities in the groupware.

AliasDestinationType.description:
What the alias does with mail.

- `addresses`: delivers to the addresses in `destinations`.
- `discard`: silently discards the mail (stored as the reserved destination `null@localhost`).
- `learnSpam`: passes the mail to spam training as spam (`spam@localhost`).
- `learnHam`: passes the mail to spam training as ham (`ham@localhost`).

The special actions are stored exactly as the legacy UI stores them, so the mail server treats
aliases saved by either UI the same way.

Alias.description:
An alias of mailcow (`alias` table). The row through which a mailbox receives mail at its own
address belongs to the mailbox (feature 003) and is never represented as an alias.

address.description:
Address in ASCII form: the local part with the letter case it was given, the domain part in
lower-case ASCII (punycode). A catch-all alias has the form `@domain`.

addressUnicode.description: The address with its domain part in readable (Unicode) form.

domain.description: The alias's own domain in ASCII form. It may be an alias domain.

domainUnicode.description: The alias's own domain in readable (Unicode) form.

primaryDomain.description:
The target domain when the alias lives in an alias domain, otherwise `domain`. The alias
counts towards this domain's alias limit.

destinations.description:
Destination addresses, exactly as stored and in stored order, when `destinationType` is
`addresses`. Empty for a special action. Destinations stored by another tool are shown even
when the current rules would refuse them.

destinationsUnicode.description:
`destinations` in the same order with each domain part in readable (Unicode) form (G13).
Entries without a domain part are shown as stored.

active.description: Whether mail to the address is accepted.

senderAllowed.description:
Whether the destination mailboxes may send as the address ("allowed to send as"). An explicit
sender permission of a mailbox overrides `false` for that mailbox.

groupwareVisible.description:
Whether the address is offered as a sender identity in the webmail of the destination
mailboxes. It takes effect only when the alias is active and not a catch-all, and only when
the groupware is enabled on the server (see `getAliasesCapabilities`).

internal.description:
Whether the mail filter refuses mail to the address from senders outside the alias's domain
and that domain's alias domains.

publicComment.description:
Public comment, empty when none is stored. New values may have at most 160 bytes in UTF-8;
longer comments stored by another tool are shown as stored.

privateComment.description:
Private comment, empty when none is stored. New values may have at most 160 bytes in UTF-8;
longer comments stored by another tool are shown as stored.

modifiedAt.description: Last modification time, or `null` when the alias was never modified.

orphaned.description:
`true` when `domain` no longer exists as a domain or an alias domain (possible after legacy
deletions). Orphaned aliases are visible to administrators only. They can be deleted, and a
change is accepted only when it moves the alias to an existing domain.

etag.description:
Version tag over the stored settings of the alias, equal to the `ETag` header of a single
read. Send it in `If-Match`, or as `version` of a bulk target.

AliasCreateRequest.description:
One alias. The web app sends one request per address of the legacy multi-address form.

- `address` is trimmed, its domain part converted to lower-case ASCII (UTS #46); the local part
  keeps its letter case. It must be a valid address or `@domain` for a catch-all, lie in an
  existing domain or alias domain in the caller's scope (relay and inactive domains are allowed),
  and not be in use by a mailbox, resource, alias or temporary alias, nor reach a mailbox through
  an alias domain (`409 address-in-use`).
- Give either `destinations` (with `destinationType` omitted or `addresses`) or a special action
  in `destinationType`, never both.
- The primary domain's alias limit is enforced (`409 domain-alias-limit-reached`).
- A destination whose domain is neither an active domain nor an active alias domain of this server
  is external. External destinations are refused with `422` (`notEligible`,
  `kind: externalDestination`) when the server disables them for every role, and with
  `403 attribute-not-permitted` when the caller is a domain administrator without the
  `aliasExternalGoto` permission.
- The defaults are those of the legacy form: active, allowed to send as, visible in the
  groupware, not internal, no comments.

destinations.description:
Destination addresses. Each is trimmed and its domain part converted to lower-case ASCII. Each
must be a valid address, differ from the alias's own address and not be a resource.
Addresses that differ only in letter case are stored once, in the order first given. Joined
by commas, the list may have at most 65,535 characters. A destination that does not exist is
accepted, as in legacy: mail to it bounces.

publicComment.description: At most 160 bytes in UTF-8 (`tooLong` with `max` 160 and `unit` `bytes`).

privateComment.description: At most 160 bytes in UTF-8 (`tooLong` with `max` 160 and `unit` `bytes`).

AliasLimitReachedProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/domain-alias-limit-reached` (status `409`). Creating or moving
aliases would make the primary domain's aliases in use exceed its alias limit. Aliases in use are
counted as feature 002 counts them: aliases in the domain and its alias domains, not counting the
rows through which mailboxes receive mail at their own address.

domain.description: The primary domain whose limit applies, in ASCII form.

count.description: Aliases in use in the domain now.

requested.description:
Number of aliases the request would add to the domain, for example the aliases of an
alias domain whose target changes. `1` for a creation or an address change.

AliasCapabilities.description:
Server settings and limits that clients of aliases, alias domains, resources and sender settings
need before they submit. The values reflect the server's current configuration and contain no
secret or connection detail. Whether the caller holds `aliasDomains`, `aliasExternalGoto` or
`extendSenderAcl` comes from `GET /me` (`Identity.permissions`).

groupwareEnabled.description:
`false` when the groupware is disabled on the server (mailcow's `SKIP_SOGO=y`). Clients can
then hide the groupware visibility option and the `showInGroupware` and `hideInGroupware`
bulk actions, as legacy does. The flag is still stored.

externalDestinationsDisabled.description:
`true` when external alias destinations are disabled for every role, administrators
included (the legacy setting `ALIAS_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_DOMAINS`, off by default).

bulkLimit.description: Maximum number of objects per bulk request.

commentMaxBytes.description: Maximum length of each alias comment in UTF-8 bytes.

destinationsMaxLength.description: Maximum length of an alias's destination list, joined by commas, in characters.

resourceDescriptionMaxLength.description: Maximum length of a resource description in characters.

resourceBookingLimit.description: Allowed range of `bookingLimit` for the booking rule `limited`.

rateLimitFrames.description: Allowed time frames of an alias domain's initial rate limit.

dkimKeySizes.description: Allowed DKIM key sizes in bits.

selector.description: The server's default DKIM selector (feature 002's setting; upstream `dkim`).

dkimDefaults.description:
Values that pre-fill the alias domain creation form. `null` for a domain administrator
without the `aliasDomains` permission.

dkimDnsPublicationEnabled.description:
Whether new DKIM keys are also published to a DNS server (fork-only, off by default).
Administrators only; `null` for domain administrators.

AliasBulkActionRequest.description:
One action on up to 100 aliases, as the legacy mass actions do. Each alias is authorised,
checked, changed and audited on its own and gets one result; one failure does not stop the
others. An alias named twice is processed once. Each target may carry the version tag the client
read (for example `etag` of a list entry); an outdated target gets `outdated` and stays unchanged.

- `activate` / `deactivate`: set `active`.
- `showInGroupware` / `hideInGroupware`: set `groupwareVisible`. When the groupware is disabled on
  the server, the flag is stored but has no effect.
- `delete`: delete the alias and the explicit sender permissions to send as its address.
- `copyOverAliasDomains`: the legacy mass action "Expand alias over alias domains", processed for
  each alias as `copyAliasOverAliasDomains` would process it. The per-alias-domain outcomes are
  in the response's `meta.copies`; an alias that lives in an alias domain is `refused` with
  `not-primary-domain-alias`.

targets.description: The aliases, identified by `id` as a decimal string (`"4711"`).

AliasCopyOutcome.description:
Outcome of copying one alias to one alias domain of its primary domain. The copy is
`<local part>@<alias domain>` (for a catch-all, `@<alias domain>`), created with the checks,
follow-up steps and audit record of a creation by the caller.

- `created`: the copy exists now; `aliasId` is its identifier.
- `skipped`: the copy was not created; `reason` says why: `addressInUse`, `aliasLimitReached`,
  or `destinationNotPermitted` (the alias has external destinations, which the server disables
  or the caller's `aliasExternalGoto` permission does not allow).
- `failed`: an unexpected failure; `problem` explains it.

address.description: Address of the copy in ASCII form.

addressUnicode.description: Address of the copy with its domain part in readable (Unicode) form (G13).

aliasId.description: Identifier of the created copy, else `null`.

reason.description: Why the copy was skipped, else `null`.

AliasPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of an alias. Members that are not sent keep their values. A member that is sent
is applied or refused, never ignored.

- `address`: the rules of creation apply, except that the alias's own current address does not
  count as in use, so a change of letter case alone is possible. Moving the alias into another
  primary domain checks that domain's alias limit. Explicit sender permissions to send as the old
  address move to the new address.
- `destinations` or a special action in `destinationType` replaces the whole destination. Only
  destinations that the request adds are checked against the external-destination rules;
  destinations already on the alias are kept, so changing any other attribute never needs the
  `aliasExternalGoto` permission.
- Read-only members (`id`, `addressUnicode`, `kind`, `domain`, `domainUnicode`, `inAliasDomain`,
  `primaryDomain`, `primaryDomainUnicode`, `createdAt`, `modifiedAt`, `orphaned`) may be sent with
  their current value, so a client can send back the representation it read. `kind` and the
  domain members are compared with the values that follow from the resulting address. A
  different value is refused with `immutable`. `destinationsUnicode` follows from `destinations`
  and `etag` is ignored; send the version in `If-Match`.
- A change to an orphaned alias is refused unless it moves the alias to an existing domain.

AliasCopyReport.description:
Result of copying one alias over the alias domains of its primary domain, one entry per alias
domain in name order. An alias domain whose copy address is in use is reported as skipped. A
domain without alias domains gives an empty list.

AliasDomainRateLimit.description:
Rate limit of an alias domain, stored in mailcow's shared store (Redis hash `RL_VALUE`, value
`<value> / 1<s|m|h|d>`). Read-only after creation; it is changed in feature 006.

value.description: Number of messages per time frame.

AliasDomain.description:
An alias domain (`alias_domain` table): every mailbox of the target domain also receives mail
under this name with the same local part. It can hold aliases of its own.

name.description: Name in lower-case ASCII (punycode) form. It never changes.

targetDomain.description: The target domain in ASCII form.

active.description: Whether mail to addresses of the alias domain is accepted.

targetIsRelayDomain.description:
Whether the target domain is a relay (backup MX) domain. New alias domains cannot target a
relay domain, but a target may become one later, as in legacy.

aliasCount.description: Number of aliases that live in the alias domain.

rateLimit.description: The alias domain's rate limit, or `null` when none is set. Read-only.

etag.description:
Version tag over the stored settings (name, target and active state). It does not change
with `aliasCount`, `targetIsRelayDomain` or `rateLimit`.

AliasDomainCreateRequest.description:
One alias domain. The name and the target are normalised like domain names in feature 002
(trimmed, lower-cased, UTS #46). The name must be a valid domain name, must differ from the
server's host name and from the target, and must not exist as a domain or alias domain
(`409 alias-domain-already-exists`). The target must be an existing domain (not an alias domain)
in the caller's scope and must not be a relay (backup MX) domain.

Domain administrators need the `aliasDomains` permission ("Add alias domains"; otherwise
`403 permission-flag-required`), and the `ratelimit` permission to give `rateLimit` (otherwise
`403 attribute-not-permitted`). Both are checked before anything is stored.

A DKIM key is generated unless one already exists for the name or `dkimSelector` is the empty
string, with the given selector or the server's default selector (see `getAliasesCapabilities`),
and the given key size or 2,048 bits, as the legacy form pre-fills.

rateLimit.description: Initial rate limit. Omitted or `null` sets none.

dkimSelector.description:
DKIM selector: letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`. Omitted means the server's default
selector; the empty string means "no DKIM key".

AliasDomainCreationReport.description:
Outcome of each follow-up step of an alias domain creation, with the values of feature 002's
domain creation report. The alias domain and its domain map entry are stored together before
these steps run, and a failing step never undoes the creation. The same report is stored in the
creation's audit record.

dkimKey.description:
`alreadyExisted`: a key for the name was already stored (for example kept from an earlier
domain or alias domain with this name), and it is used unchanged. `notRequested`: the request
sent an empty `dkimSelector`.

dkimDnsPublication.description:
Publication of the new DKIM key to the ISPConfig DNS server (FeldHost setting, off by
default). `noZone`: the ISPConfig server has no zone for the name. `notConfigured`: the
publication is disabled. `skipped`: no new key was generated.

messages.description: English explanation of each failed step, keyed by step name. Never contains secrets.

AliasDomainCreated.description: The created alias domain and the outcome of each follow-up step.

AliasDomainAlreadyExistsProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/alias-domain-already-exists` (status `409`). The name of a new
alias domain already exists as a domain or as an alias domain. Nothing was created.

name.description: The normalised name in ASCII form.

AliasDomainBulkActionRequest.description:
One action on up to 100 alias domains, as the legacy mass actions do. Each alias domain is
authorised, checked, changed and audited on its own, exactly as the single operation would, and
gets one result. An alias domain named twice is processed once. Each target may carry the version
tag the client read; an outdated target gets `outdated` and stays unchanged.

- `activate` / `deactivate`: set `active`.
- `delete`: delete the alias domain with everything `deleteAliasDomain` removes.

targets.description: The alias domains, identified by `id` = the name (ASCII or Unicode form).

AliasDomainPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of an alias domain. Only `targetDomain` and `active` can change; members that
are not sent keep their values. No permission flag is needed (legacy behaviour).

- A new `targetDomain` must meet the target rules of creation: an existing domain (not an alias
  domain) in the caller's scope that is not a relay (backup MX) domain. The aliases that live in
  the alias domain then count towards the new target's alias limit
  (`409 domain-alias-limit-reached`).
- Read-only members (`name`, `nameUnicode`, `targetDomainUnicode`, `targetIsRelayDomain`,
  `aliasCount`, `rateLimit`, `createdAt`, `modifiedAt`) may be sent with their current value, so a
  client can send back the representation it read; a different value is refused with
  `immutable`. `targetDomainUnicode` and `targetIsRelayDomain` are compared with the values that
  follow from the resulting target.
  The rate limit is changed in feature 006, and is not covered by the version tag, so a client
  should send back only the members it changes. `etag` is ignored; send the version in
  `If-Match`.

ResourceBookingRule.description:
How the groupware handles overlapping bookings (mailcow's `mailbox.multiple_bookings`).

- `alwaysFree`: always shown as free (stored `0`).
- `unlimited`: unlimited bookings, shown as busy when booked (stored `-1`). The legacy default.
- `limited`: at most `bookingLimit` concurrent bookings (stored as that number); further
  overlapping bookings are declined by the groupware.

Resource.description:
A groupware resource (a `mailbox` row with kind `location`, `thing` or `group`, password
`RESOURCE` and no quota). It does not count towards the domain's mailbox limit or quota. Mail
sent to its address is discarded by the mail server; bookings go through the groupware.

address.description:
Address in ASCII form, derived at creation from the ASCII letters and digits of the
description (letter case kept) and never changed afterwards.

description.description: Description, shown as the resource's name in the groupware.

active.description: Whether the resource can be booked. An inactive resource disappears from the groupware.

etag.description: Version tag over the stored settings of the resource.

ResourceCreateRequest.description:
One resource. Its address is derived from the description as legacy derives it: the ASCII letters
and digits of the description, in their letter case, followed by `@` and the domain. Other
characters are left out (`Raum Süd` → `RaumSd@…`). A description that yields no letter or digit,
or more than 64, is refused with `invalidFormat` (`format: resourceDescription`) on
`description`. A derived address
that is in use is refused with `409 address-in-use`. The domain must be an existing domain in the
caller's scope; alias domains are refused. Resources do not count towards the domain's mailbox
limit.

bookingLimit.description: Required with `bookingRule` `limited`, and refused with the other rules.

ResourceBulkActionRequest.description:
One action on up to 100 resources, as the legacy mass actions do. Each resource is processed and
audited on its own, exactly as the single operation would, and gets one result. A resource named
twice is processed once. Each target may carry the version tag the client read; an outdated target
gets `outdated` and stays unchanged.

targets.description: The resources, identified by `id` = the address.

ResourcePatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a resource. `description`, `kind`, `bookingRule`, `bookingLimit` and `active`
can change; members that are not sent keep their values. The address stays the same when the
description changes. `bookingLimit` is required when `bookingRule` becomes `limited`. Read-only
members (`address`, `addressUnicode`, `domain`, `domainUnicode`, `createdAt`, `modifiedAt`) may
be sent with their current value; a different value is refused with `immutable`. `etag` is
ignored; send the version in `If-Match`.

MailboxImplicitSenderAddress.description:
An address the mailbox may send as without an explicit permission.

- `ownAddress`: the mailbox's own address.
- `aliasDomainAddress`: the mailbox's local part in one of its domain's alias domains.
- `alias`: an alias that delivers to the mailbox. It lets the mailbox send only when
  `senderAllowed` is `true`, unless the mailbox holds an explicit permission for the address,
  which overrides `false`. A catch-all alias that allows sending lets the mailbox send as any
  address of its domain that has no alias of its own allowing sending.

aliasId.description: Identifier of the alias for `alias`, else `null`.

senderAllowed.description: For `alias`, the alias's "allowed to send as" flag; `true` for the other sources.

catchAll.description: Whether the alias is a catch-all alias (`@domain`); `false` for the other sources.

MailboxSenderPermissionKind.description:
What a sender permission entry names (G12): a domain (`domain`), an alias domain (`aliasDomain`),
the address of an alias (`alias`) or of a mailbox (`mailbox`), or any address (`anyAddress`, the
entry `*`). Clients label entries with it; they tolerate values added later.

MailboxSenderPermission.description:
An explicit sender permission of the mailbox (a `sender_acl` row with `external = 0`).

- `address`: the mailbox may send as this address (an alias or another mailbox). The mail server
  accepts it at once, but the groupware offers another mailbox's address as a sender identity only
  after that mailbox delegates access to this one in the groupware.
- `domain`: the mailbox may send as any address of the domain and of that domain's alias domains.
  `value` has the form `@domain`.
- `anyAddress`: the mailbox's sender check is disabled (`value` `*`). Only administrators grant
  it, and it is stored alone.

value.description: Stored form, which a client sends back to keep the entry.

valueUnicode.description: The value with its domain part in readable (Unicode) form.

kind.description:
What the entry names, for labels (G12): `domain` or `aliasDomain` for a domain entry,
`mailbox` or `alias` for an address entry, `anyAddress` for `*`. `null` for a stale entry,
whose domain or address no longer exists.

changeable.description:
Whether the caller may remove this entry. For a domain administrator, entries outside their
domains (and "any address") are not changeable: they are kept even when a replacement leaves
them out.

stale.description:
Whether the entry's domain or address no longer exists. An administrator removes a stale
entry by saving the permissions without it.

MailboxSenderSettings.description:
What a mailbox may send as. Explicit permissions and external sender addresses are stored where
legacy stores them (`sender_acl`), so the mail server applies a change to the next submission.

mailbox.description: The mailbox's address in ASCII form.

implicitAddresses.description:
Addresses the mailbox may send as without an explicit permission: its own address, its
addresses in its domain's alias domains, and the aliases that deliver to it (including
catch-all aliases), each with whether the alias allows sending.

senderCheckDisabled.description: Whether the mailbox holds the "any address" permission.

externalSenderAddresses.description:
Addresses (`news@mailer.example`) and whole domains (`@partner.example`) outside this server
that the mailbox may send as. Full addresses become selectable sender identities in its
webmail. For an external domain, a DKIM key should be imported for it and this server must be
added to the domain's SPF record, or receivers may reject the mail.

externalSenderAddressesUnicode.description:
`externalSenderAddresses` in the same order with each domain part in readable (Unicode) form
(G13).

etag.description:
Version tag over the stored explicit permissions and external sender addresses. It does not
change with `implicitAddresses`.

MailboxSenderSettingsPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a mailbox's sender settings. Each list that is sent replaces the stored list
as a whole; a list that is not sent stays unchanged. Duplicates are stored once.

`explicitPermissions` entries are strings:
- an address of an existing alias or mailbox in the caller's scope;
- an existing domain or alias domain in the caller's scope, as `domain` or `@domain`;
- `*` for "any address", which only administrators may grant. When `*` is among the resulting
  entries, it is stored alone.

An entry for an alias that delivers to the mailbox and allows sending is accepted but not stored,
because the mailbox already has that right (if sending is later turned off for the alias, the
mailbox loses it). An entry for such an alias that does not allow sending is stored and overrides
the alias's setting. For a domain administrator, stored entries outside their scope are kept even
when the request leaves them out, and may be sent back unchanged; the request cannot add such
entries (`notFound`, as for entries that do not exist; `*` gives `notEligible`).

`externalSenderAddresses` entries are valid addresses or domain names (`domain` or `@domain`)
whose domain is not a domain or alias domain of this server (`notEligible` with `kind`
`localDomain`). Domain administrators need the `extendSenderAcl` permission to change them; the
list sent back unchanged needs no permission.

`mailbox`, `mailboxUnicode`, `implicitAddresses`, `senderCheckDisabled`,
`externalSenderAddressesUnicode` and `etag` are derived
and ignored when sent, so a client can send back the representation it read. A request with any
invalid or refused entry is refused as a whole, naming every such entry.

MailboxSenderPermissionCandidate.description:
An entry the caller could add to a mailbox's explicit sender permissions: a domain or alias
domain in the caller's scope (`@domain`), `*` for administrators, or the address of an alias or
mailbox in the caller's scope. The mailbox itself, the aliases that deliver to it, catch-all
aliases and entries already granted are left out, as in the legacy selection list.

MailboxStatus.description:
Status of a mailbox (mailcow's `mailbox.active`). `active` (1): receives mail and may sign in.
`loginDisabled` (2): receives mail, every sign-in is refused, and it is hidden from the webmail
address book. `inactive` (0): receives no mail and may not sign in. The mailbox's own alias always
has the same status.

MailboxAuthSource.description:
Where the mailbox's password is verified (mailcow's `mailbox.authsource`). `mailcow`: the password
hash stored by mailcow. `keycloak`, `genericOidc` (`generic-oidc`) and `ldap`: the external
identity provider of that type. Only `mailcow` and the type of the provider currently configured
on the server (`MailboxCapabilities.authSources`) may be chosen.

MailboxProtocolAccess.description:
Protocol access of a mailbox (`mailbox.attributes.*_access`). A setting missing from an older
mailbox's stored data is reported as `true`, which is how mail sign-in treats it.

MailboxUserPermissions.description:
What the mailbox user may do in the web apps (mailcow's `user_acl` row), in camelCase. Five
permissions overlap with domain-administrator flags of the same name: `syncjobs`, `quarantine`,
`appPasswds`, `pushover` and `spamPolicy`. For a domain administrator who lacks such a flag, the
matching permission is omitted from every representation and cannot be changed, as in legacy.

spamPolicy.description: Allow and block lists (`spam_policy`). Overlaps with the domain-administrator flag.

syncjobs.description: Sync jobs (`syncjobs`). Overlaps with the domain-administrator flag.

pushover.description: Push notifications (`pushover`). Overlaps with the domain-administrator flag.

quarantine.description: Quarantine actions (`quarantine`). Overlaps with the domain-administrator flag.

appPasswds.description: App passwords (`app_passwds`). Overlaps with the domain-administrator flag.

MailboxTagSet.description:
Tags of a mailbox (mailcow's `tags_mailbox`). Each tag is trimmed and 1 to 255 characters long.
Tags that differ only in letter case are one tag; the first spelling sent is kept. A request may
not leave a mailbox with more tags than the server's tagging limit
(`MailboxCapabilities.taggingLimit`, 25 by default); a mailbox that already has more (possible
through legacy) is shown in full and can only shrink. Sending tags replaces the whole set, so
removing a tag means sending the set without it. Representations sort them alphabetically
without regard to letter case.

MailboxCustomAttributes.description:
Custom attributes of a mailbox (`mailbox.custom_attributes`): named text values that mailcow's
domain footers insert in place of `{= name =}`. Values written through this API have names of 1
to 255 characters without whitespace and values of at most 4,096 characters, and a mailbox has at
most 100 attributes (`MailboxCapabilities.customAttributeLimit`). Attributes stored by legacy
mailcow, which has no limits, are returned as stored.

MailboxLastLogins.description:
The most recent recent-login record (`sasl_log`) of each service. Every member is `null` when the
mailbox never signed in to that service, and all are `null` when the server does not report last
logins (`MailboxCapabilities.lastLoginsReported` is `false`). Not part of the version tag.

MailboxTaggedMailHandling.description:
What happens to mail sent to `local+tag@domain` (mailcow's Redis hashes `RCPT_WANTS_SUBFOLDER_TAG`
and `RCPT_WANTS_SUBJECT_TAG`). `subfolder`: filed into the folder `INBOX/<tag>`. `subject`: the tag
is added to the subject. `none`: no special handling.

MailboxQuarantineNotification.description: How often the mailbox user is told about new quarantine items (`attributes.quarantine_notification`).

MailboxQuarantineCategory.description:
Which quarantine items the notifications cover (`attributes.quarantine_category`). `rejected`
(`reject`): rejected mail. `junk` (`add_header`): mail moved to the junk folder. `all`: both.

MailboxRateLimit.description:
A rate limit: at most `value` messages per `frame` (mailcow's Redis hash `RL_VALUE`, stored as
`<value> / 1<s|m|h|d>`).

Mailbox.description:
