A mailbox of mailcow (a `mailbox` row with `kind = ''`). Resources (locations, things and groups)
share the table but are never mailboxes. Usage figures and last logins are read on every request
and are not part of the version tag. Members marked read-only are managed by other features or
computed, and a change request that sends them is refused (`immutable`).

address.description: Full address in lower case with the domain in ASCII form (`mailbox.username`). Identifies the mailbox in paths.

quota.description: Quota in bytes, a whole multiple of 1 MiB. `0` means unlimited.

quotaUsed.description: Storage used in bytes, from Dovecot's usage record (`quota2`, or `quota2replica` on a non-master node).

percentUsed.description: Storage used divided by the quota, rounded to a whole percent. `null` for an unlimited quota.

largestAllowedQuota.description:
The largest quota this mailbox may be given, in bytes: the domain quota minus the quotas of
the domain's other mailboxes, capped at the domain's maximum mailbox quota and never below
zero.

forcePasswordChange.description: The user must change the password at the next sign-in (`attributes.force_pw_update`). Always `false` for an external authentication source.

forceSecondFactorSetup.description: The user must set up a second factor at the next sign-in (`attributes.force_tfa`). Always `false` for `genericOidc`.

webmailRedirect.description:
After signing in to the web UI, the user is sent to webmail (legacy "SOGo access",
`attributes.sogo_access`). Has no effect when the groupware is disabled
(`MailboxCapabilities.groupwareEnabled`).

recoveryEmail.description:
Password recovery address set by an administrator (`attributes.recovery_email`). Only for the
`mailcow` authentication source. Values written through this API are valid addresses; legacy
mailcow does not validate them, so a stored value is returned as is.

passwordChangedAt.description: When the password was last set (`attributes.passwd_update`). `null` when never recorded.

taggedMailHandling.description: Read-only here, changed through feature 005. May be given at creation.

tlsEnforceInbound.description: Inbound TLS is enforced (`attributes.tls_enforce_in`). Read-only here, changed through feature 005. May be given at creation.

tlsEnforceOutbound.description: Outbound TLS is enforced (`attributes.tls_enforce_out`). Read-only here, changed through feature 005. May be given at creation.

mailSettingsVersion.description:
The version tag of the mailbox's mail settings (`taggedMailHandling`, `tlsEnforceInbound`,
`tlsEnforceOutbound`), equal to the `etag` of `GET /mailboxes/{mailbox}/mail-settings`. Send it
as a target's `version` in `POST /mailboxes/mail-settings/bulk-actions` (feature 005, G22).

quarantineNotification.description: Read-only here, changed through feature 006. May be given at creation.

quarantineCategory.description: Read-only here, changed through feature 006. May be given at creation.

rateLimit.description: The effective rate limit, from the mailbox or else from its domain. Read-only here, changed through feature 006. May be given at creation.

relayhostId.description: Assigned relayhost (`attributes.relayhost`, `"0"` means none). Read-only here, managed by feature 009. Never set at creation.

activeTemporaryAliases.description: Temporary aliases of the mailbox that are permanent or not yet expired (feature 005).

pushNotificationsActive.description: Whether push notifications are configured and active (feature 005).

domainRelayed.description: Whether the mailbox's domain is relayed as a backup MX (`domain.backupmx`).

etag.description:
Version tag of the mailbox's stored settings (the `mailbox` row without usage figures, its
`user_acl` row and its tags), equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. It changes
whenever a stored setting changes, whichever implementation changed it, and never because
of usage figures or last logins. Send it in `If-Match`, or as `version` of a bulk target.

MailboxRenameStep.description:
One step of a mailbox rename and its outcome. Steps run in this order:
`sharedFolderPermissionsRemoval` (the IMAP ACLs the mailbox granted and received, read and
removed), `sharedStoreMove` (rate limit and tagged-mail handling moved to the new address),
`database` (every row, including the carried-over second factors, passkeys, temporary aliases,
spam settings, quarantine items and recent logins, the optional alias and the groupware
directory entry), `mailStoreMove` (the maildir), `webmailRename` (SOGo data, skipped when the
groupware is disabled) and `sharedFolderPermissionsRecreation`.

Outcomes: `done`; `undone` (done, then reverted); `notDone` (never started); `failed` (refused or
failed, nothing changed by it); `unknown` (no answer within the container API timeout);
`undoFailed` (done, and reverting it failed); `skipped`.

MailboxTemporaryFailureProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/temporary-failure` (status `503`): a mailcow service the
operation needs is unavailable or reported a failure, and nothing was changed (for a rename: every
step already done was undone). Retry after the `Retry-After` header.

dependency.description:
The unavailable service. Known values: `mailStore` (the container API or the Dovecot
container, for maildir moves and shared-folder permissions), `webmail` (the SOGo
container), `sharedStore` (mailcow's Redis). Later features may add values.

steps.description: For a rename, the outcome of every step.

MailboxProtocolAccessInput.description:
Protocol settings to set. Only the protocols sent are set; the others keep their current value
(change) or take the template's or default value (creation). A domain administrator needs the
`protocolAccess` permission flag to choose a value other than the current one (change) or the
template's (creation).

MailboxUserPermissionsInput.description:
User permissions to set. Only the permissions sent change. A domain administrator may not choose
a value for a permission that overlaps with a domain-administrator flag they lack (`syncjobs`,
`quarantine`, `appPasswds`, `pushover`, `spamPolicy`), unless it equals the current value
(change) or the template's value (creation).

MailboxCreateRequest.description:
A new mailbox. Each value not given is taken, in this order, from the named template, the Default
template, and the built-in defaults (server settings with the upstream values: active, no forced
password change or second-factor setup, webmail redirect on, all six protocols allowed, no TLS
enforcement, no tagged-mail handling, hourly quarantine notifications of rejected mail, no rate
limit, every user permission except `syncjobs` and `sogoProfileReset`, an unlimited quota).
Exceptions:

- `quota` follows the same order; the domain's default mailbox quota does not apply (owner
  decision 2026-10-18), so without a quota from the request or a template the mailbox is
  unlimited, as in legacy's server;
- `displayName`, when absent or empty, is the local part;
- for an external `authSource`, `forcePasswordChange` (and for `genericOidc` also
  `forceSecondFactorSetup`) is off whatever the template says.

Domain administrators need the `unlimitedQuota` flag for a quota of `0` (also from a template),
`protocolAccess` to choose protocol settings, `sogoAccess` to choose `webmailRedirect`,
`ratelimit` to choose `rateLimit`, and the overlapping flags to choose the matching user
permissions. Apart from the quota, a value equal to what the template and defaults would give is
not a choice. Recovery e-mail, custom attributes, sender permissions and relayhost cannot be set
at creation, as in legacy.

localPart.description:
Trimmed and lower-cased, then 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits and ``! # $ % & ' * + / = ? ^ _ `
{ | } ~ - .``, without a leading or trailing dot or two dots in a row (`invalidFormat` with
`format: localPart`). The full address must be a valid address of at most 255 characters
(`format: email`).

domain.description:
A primary domain in the caller's scope, in ASCII or Unicode form and any letter case. A
domain that does not exist or lies outside the caller's scope gives `notFound`; an alias
domain gives `notEligible` with `kind: aliasDomain`. Inactive and backup-MX domains are
accepted, as in legacy.

password.description:
Required for the `mailcow` authentication source, refused for an external one
(`conflictsWith`). Checked against the password policy (`GET /password-policy`): each unmet
rule is reported (`tooShort` with `min`, `missingCharacterClass` with `characterClass`).
Stored in mailcow's configured hash scheme (`MAILCOW_PASS_SCHEME`). A value that starts with
a hash-scheme prefix legacy recognises (exactly the list of
`MailboxCapabilities.preHashedPasswordSchemes`, such as `{BLF-CRYPT}` or `{SSHA512}`) is stored
as given without the policy check. Never returned.

displayName.description: Leading `<` and trailing `>` are removed, as in legacy.

templateId.description: Mailbox template that pre-fills omitted values. An unknown ID gives `notFound`.

quota.description:
Bytes, a whole multiple of 1 MiB (`notMultipleOf` with `factor: 1048576`), `0` for unlimited. It must not exceed the
domain's maximum mailbox quota (`outOfRange` with `max` and `limit: maxMailboxQuota`) or the
domain quota left (`outOfRange` with `max` and `limit: domainQuotaLeft`).

rateLimit.description: Initial rate limit of the mailbox. `null` means none, overriding the template.

MailboxCreationReport.description:
Outcome of each follow-up step of a mailbox creation. The mailbox, its usage records, its own
alias, its user permissions and its tags are stored together before these steps run; a failed
step never undoes the creation. The same report is stored in the creation's audit record.

rateLimit.description: The initial rate limit in mailcow's shared store (`RL_VALUE`).

taggedMailHandling.description: The tagged-mail handling in mailcow's shared store. `notRequested` for `none`.

groupwareDirectoryUpdate.description:
The mailbox's entry in the groupware directory view (`_sogo_static_view`) and the groupware
cache flush. `notRequired` for a mailbox that is not active.

messages.description: English explanation of each failed step, keyed by step name. Never contains secrets.

MailboxCreated.description: The created mailbox and the outcome of its follow-up steps. Never contains the password or its hash.

MailboxAttributeNotPermittedProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/attribute-not-permitted` (status `403`): a domain administrator
would choose mailbox settings that their permission flags do not allow. The whole request is
refused and nothing changed. A value equal to the current one (change) or to the template's
(creation) is not a choice; an unlimited quota is always one unless the mailbox already has it.

attributes.description: The refused members as dot-separated paths in the request body.

requiredFlags.description: For each refused member, the permission flag it needs (a `PermissionFlags` name).

MailboxPermissionFlagRequiredProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required` (status `403`): the operation needs a
permission flag that the caller lacks (`docs/conventions.md`, "Permission refusals"). For
mailboxes this is a bulk `allowProtocol` or `disallowProtocol` by a domain administrator without
the `protocolAccess` flag; the whole request is refused and nothing changed.

requiredFlags.description: Flag names as in `PermissionFlags`; any one of them allows the operation.

MailboxAddressInUseProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/address-in-use` (status `409`): the address is already used by
another object, so no mailbox can be created with it or renamed to it. Nothing was changed.

holder.description: The kind of object that holds the address.

MailboxLimitReachedProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/mailbox-limit-reached` (status `409`): the domain already has
as many mailboxes as its limit allows. Resources are not counted. Nothing was created.

limit.description: The domain's maximum number of mailboxes.

MailboxAliasLimitReachedProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/domain-alias-limit-reached` (status `409`), as for alias
creation (feature 004): a rename that keeps the old address as an alias needs room for one more
alias in the domain. Nothing was changed.

MailboxTemplateDefaults.description:
The built-in values a new mailbox or mailbox template gets for every value that neither the
request nor a template gives (API server settings with the upstream values, legacy
`MAILBOX_DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTES`). `quota` is unlimited, for a new mailbox without a quota from the
request or a template as for a new template. User permissions are omitted for a domain
administrator who lacks the overlapping flag, as in `Mailbox.userPermissions`.

MailboxCapabilities.description:
Server settings and limits a client needs before it submits a mailbox form. They reflect the
server's current configuration and contain no secret or connection detail.

identityProviderType.description: The external identity provider configured in mailcow (`identity_provider.authsource`).

authSources.description: The authentication sources a mailbox may be given or switched to now (`mailcow` plus the configured provider type).

groupwareEnabled.description: `false` when SOGo is disabled (`SKIP_SOGO=y`). `webmailRedirect` then has no effect.

lastLoginsReported.description: `false` when the operator turned off the display of last logins (legacy `SHOW_LAST_LOGIN`). `lastLogins` is then always empty.

garbageRetentionMinutes.description: How long mailcow keeps the mail of a deleted mailbox before purging it (`MAILDIR_GC_TIME`, 7200 by default).

preHashedPasswordSchemes.description:
The hash-scheme prefixes legacy recognises (G31): a password that starts with `{<scheme>}`, in
any letter case, is stored as given without the policy check. Exactly legacy's list, in its
order: `ARGON2I`, `ARGON2ID`, `BLF-CRYPT`, `CLEAR`, `CLEARTEXT`, `CRYPT`, `DES-CRYPT`,
`LDAP-MD5`, `MD5`, `MD5-CRYPT`, `PBKDF2`, `PLAIN`, `PLAIN-MD4`, `PLAIN-MD5`, `PLAIN-TRUNC`,
`SHA`, `SHA1`, `SHA256`, `SHA256-CRYPT`, `SHA512`, `SHA512-CRYPT`, `SMD5`, `SSHA`, `SSHA256`,
`SSHA512`.

templateDefaults.description: The built-in values of new mailboxes and templates (G32).

MailboxTagUsage.description:
A distinct tag of the mailboxes in the caller's scope. Tags that differ only in letter case form
one entry, shown in the spelling that sorts first in binary order. Tags found only on mailboxes
outside the caller's scope are never listed.

mailboxCount.description: Number of mailboxes in the caller's scope that carry the tag.

MailboxBulkActionRequest.description:
One action applied to several mailboxes, as the legacy mass actions of the mailbox list do. Each
target is authorised, version-checked, processed and audited on its own, exactly as the single
operation for it (`updateMailbox` with `status` or `protocolAccess`, or `deleteMailbox`); one
failure does not stop the others. A target's `id` is the mailbox address, in any letter case and
with the domain in ASCII or Unicode form; an address given twice is processed and reported once.
At most the server's bulk limit of targets (`MailboxCapabilities.bulkLimit`, 100 by default) may
be sent (`tooMany` on `targets`).

The whole request is refused (`403`) when the caller may never apply the action: a mailbox user
(`forbidden`), a read-only key (`insufficient-key-scope`), or a domain administrator without the
`protocolAccess` flag for `allowProtocol` and `disallowProtocol` (`permission-flag-required`
with `requiredFlags: [protocolAccess]`).

action.description:
`activate`, `disableLogin` and `deactivate` set `status` to `active`, `loginDisabled` and
`inactive`. `delete` deletes the mailbox. `allowProtocol` and `disallowProtocol` turn
`protocol` on or off.

MailboxOutcomeUnknownProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/outcome-unknown` (status `504`): mailcow's container API did not
answer within its timeout (`DOCKER_TIMEOUT`, 60 seconds), so the outcome of that step is unknown.
A deletion then removed no records and is safe to retry. A rename undid every step known to be
done; `steps` shows which step is unknown.

step.description: The step whose outcome is unknown, for example `mailStoreCleanup` or a `MailboxRenameStep` name.

MailboxPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) of a mailbox: only the members sent change. Nested objects merge, so
`protocolAccess` and `userPermissions` change only the members they contain, and
`customAttributes` adds or replaces the names sent with a text value and removes those sent with
`null`. `tags` replaces the whole set. Any other member of the mailbox representation is
read-only and refused (`immutable`); the address changes only through `renameMailbox`.

Domain administrators need the flags listed for `createMailbox` to choose these settings; a value
equal to the current one is not a choice. A quota of `0` needs `unlimitedQuota` unless the
mailbox is already unlimited. A refused setting refuses the whole request
(`attribute-not-permitted`) and nothing changes.

displayName.description: An empty value sets the local part. Leading `<` and trailing `>` are removed.

quota.description:
Must not exceed `largestAllowedQuota` (`outOfRange` with `max` and `limit:
largestAllowedQuota`). A quota below the storage already used is accepted, as in legacy.

password.description:
As for `createMailbox`. Updates `passwordChangedAt`; it does not change
`forcePasswordChange`, app passwords or sessions. Refused for an external authentication
source unless the same request switches `authSource` to `mailcow`, in which case it is
applied to the switched mailbox.

forcePasswordChange.description: Turning it on is refused for an external authentication source (`conflictsWith`).

forceSecondFactorSetup.description: Turning it on is refused for `genericOidc` (`conflictsWith`).

authSource.description:
Switching to an external source turns off `forcePasswordChange` (and for `genericOidc`
`forceSecondFactorSetup`) and keeps the stored password hash, as in legacy. Switching to
`mailcow` without `password` is refused (`required` on `password`) when the mailbox has no
stored password.

recoveryEmail.description: A valid address, or `null` or an empty string to clear it. Only for the `mailcow` authentication source (`conflictsWith`).

customAttributes.description: Names to add or replace (text value) or remove (`null`). Limits as in `MailboxCustomAttributes`.

MailboxAddressSample.description: A count of addresses and up to 100 of them, sorted.

MailboxDeletionPreview.description:
What deleting the mailbox would currently remove and move, and whether it could proceed, computed
by the same rules as the deletion. A snapshot: the deletion checks and computes everything again,
and refuses an outdated version tag. Reading it changes nothing and writes no audit record.

canProceed.description: `false` when a service the deletion needs is unreachable (see `blockers`).

dependency.description: `mailStore`: the container API or the Dovecot container. `sharedStore`: mailcow's Redis.

exclusiveAliases.description: Aliases whose only recipient is the mailbox, which would be deleted. The mailbox's own alias is not counted.

sharedAliases.description: Aliases that would only lose the mailbox as a recipient.

counts.description: Numbers of dependent records that would be removed.

senderPermissionsHeld.description: `sender_acl` rows where the mailbox may send as others.

senderPermissionsGranted.description: `sender_acl` rows that let others send as the mailbox.

syncJobs.description: Sync jobs that deliver into the mailbox.

spamFilterSettings.description: Spam filter settings and allow and block list entries (`filterconf`).

bccMaps.description: BCC maps whose local destination is the mailbox.

oauthGrants.description: OAuth access tokens, refresh tokens and authorisation codes.

present.description: Whether these settings exist. The shared-store values are `null` while the shared store is unreachable.

webmailData.description: Profile, folders, contacts, appointments or sharing permissions in the groupware tables.

mail.description: The mail that would move to the garbage area.

garbageRetentionMinutes.description: How long mailcow keeps the moved mail before purging it (`MAILDIR_GC_TIME`).

etag.description: The mailbox's current version tag. Send it in `If-Match` with the deletion.

MailboxRenameRequest.description:
A new local part in the same domain. It is trimmed, lower-cased and validated like
`MailboxCreateRequest.localPart`, and must differ from the current one (`unchanged`). The new
address must not be used by a mailbox, resource, alias or temporary alias (`address-in-use`).

keepOldAddressAsAlias.description:
Whether to create an active alias from the old address to the new one, visible in the
webmail address book, with the private comment "Mailbox was renamed from <old> to <new>".
It needs room for one more alias in the domain (`domain-alias-limit-reached`).

MailboxRenamed.description: The renamed mailbox under its new address.

previousAddress.description: The address before the rename, which now answers "not found" as a mailbox.

MailboxRenameIncompleteProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/mailbox-rename-incomplete` (status `500`): a rename step failed
and undoing the steps already done failed as well, so the mailbox is partly renamed. `steps` lists
every step and its outcome; the audit record holds the same. An administrator must complete or
revert the remaining steps (see `docs/problems.md`).

MailboxTemplate.description:
A mailbox template (a `templates` row with `type = 'mailbox'`): the values a new mailbox starts
with. Templates only pre-fill new mailboxes; changing or deleting one changes no mailbox. The
Default template always exists and supplies the values when no template is named. Values a stored
template lacks are reported with the built-in defaults (see `MailboxCreateRequest`), with an
unlimited quota as in the legacy Default template. User permissions are omitted for a domain
administrator who lacks the overlapping flag, as in `Mailbox.userPermissions`.

isDefault.description: The Default template, which cannot be renamed or deleted.

quota.description: Bytes, a whole multiple of 1 MiB. `0` means unlimited.

etag.description: Version tag of the template's name and values, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read.

MailboxTemplateCreateRequest.description:
A new mailbox template. Only the name is required; omitted values get the built-in defaults (see
`MailboxCreateRequest`), with an unlimited quota as in the legacy Default template. The name must
be unique among mailbox templates, compared case-insensitively (`mailbox-template-name-exists`).

name.description: Trimmed; must not be empty afterwards.

MailboxTemplateBulkActionRequest.description:
One action applied to several mailbox templates, as the legacy mass deletion of the mailbox
template list does (`delete_selected`). Each target is version-checked, deleted and audited on
its own, exactly as `deleteMailboxTemplate`; one failure does not stop the others. A target's `id`
is the template ID as in the template's own path; an unknown ID, a domain template's ID or a value
that is not an ID gets `notFound`, and an ID given twice is processed and reported once. At most
100 targets may be sent (`tooMany` on `targets`, with `max: 100`).

action.description: `delete` deletes the template. The Default template is refused (`mailbox-template-protected`).

MailboxTemplatePatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) of a mailbox template: only the members sent change, and nested
`protocolAccess` and `userPermissions` change only the members they contain. `tags` replaces the
whole set and `rateLimit: null` removes the rate limit. Renaming the Default template is refused
(`mailbox-template-protected`).

PasswordPolicy.description:
The password policy that mailcow applies when a password is set (Redis hash `PASSWD_POLICY`).
Rules never saved by the operator are reported with the legacy defaults: a minimum length of 6
and no character class required. A password meets the policy when it is at least `minLength`
bytes long and contains each required class: letters `[A-Za-z]`, digits `[0-9]`, special
characters (anything else), and both a lower-case and an upper-case letter. A password set
through this API is checked against the same values. The policy is changed through feature 013,
which returns and accepts the same version tag.

etag.description:
Version tag of the effective policy values (defaults included), equal to the `ETag` header.
It is the SHA-256 of `length=<minLength>;chars=<0|1>;special_chars=<0|1>;lowerupper=<0|1>;numbers=<0|1>`,
base64url-encoded without padding and quoted, so feature 013 computes the same value.

PasswordPolicyPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of the password policy (feature 013). Members that are not sent keep their
values. `minLength` is a whole number from 3 to 64 (`outOfRange`, params `min`, `max`); legacy
silently keeps the old value instead.

DkimKeyState.description:
Key state of a DKIM entry.
- `valid`: a key exists for a domain or an alias domain.
- `missing`: the domain or alias domain has no key, so its outgoing mail is not signed.
- `unused`: a key exists for a name that is neither a domain nor an alias domain, for example after
  a domain was deleted, or because legacy stored it under an upper-case or Unicode name. It is
  never used for signing. Only administrators see unused keys.

A name has a key when a public key or a selector is stored for it.

DkimKeyKind.description: What the name of a DKIM entry is.

DkimDnsRecord.description:
The DNS TXT record a DKIM key needs. Publish it in the domain's zone so that receivers can verify
the signatures.

name.description: Fully qualified record name `<selector>._domainkey.<name>`, without a trailing dot.

value.description: The record value as one text, `v=DKIM1;k=rsa;t=s;s=email;p=<public key>`.

valueParts.description:
The same value split into consecutive pieces of at most 255 characters, for DNS providers that
need the character strings of a TXT record entered separately. Joined, they equal `value`.

DkimKeyDetails.description:
The stored key of a DKIM entry, without its private part. A key is complete when its public key,
its selector and its private key are all stored. An incomplete key, for example after a partial
legacy write, is never used for signing; delete it, or replace it by an import or a generation
with overwrite.

selector.description: Selector, or `null` when only a public key is stored.

keyLength.description:
Key length in bits, computed exactly from the public key. `null` when no public key is stored
or the stored text is not a valid RSA public key.

publicKey.description:
Public key as stored by mailcow: the base64 text of the DER `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`, without PEM
header, footer or line breaks. `null` when only a selector is stored.

record.description: The DNS record to publish, or `null` when the selector or the public key is missing.

complete.description: `true` when the public key, the selector and the private key are all stored.

missingParts.description: The parts that are not stored. Empty when `complete` is `true`.

DkimKey.description:
The DKIM entry of one name: a domain, an alias domain, or the name of a key left without a domain.
Rspamd signs outgoing mail (DKIM, by envelope sender domain) and seals forwarded mail (ARC, by
recipient domain) with the stored key. Never contains the private key.

name.description:
ASCII (punycode) name. For an unused key that legacy stored under a name that is not
lower-case ASCII, the exact stored spelling, which also addresses the entry.

targetDomain.description: For an alias domain, the domain it points to; otherwise `null`.

key.description: The stored key, or `null` when the state is `missing`.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored key (selector, public key and private key), equal to the `ETag`
header of a single read. It changes whenever the key changes, whichever UI or API changed it.
`null` when the name has no key. Send it in `If-Match` when overwriting, publishing again or
deleting the key.

DkimKeyGenerateRequest.description:
Generates a new RSA key pair for one domain or alias domain. Rules, each refused with its rule
code in a `422` problem:
- `selector`: letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.` only (`invalidFormat`, `format: dkimSelector`),
  1 to 255 characters (`required`, `tooLong`).
- `keySize`: 1024, 2048, 3072 or 4096 (`notInList`).

name.description:
A domain or an alias domain in the caller's scope, in ASCII or Unicode form and in any letter
case. Any other name answers `404`.

selector.description: Omit to use the server's default selector (see `getDnsCapabilities`).

overwrite.description:
Replace an existing key of the name. Administrators only: a domain administrator who sends
`true` gets `403 forbidden`. The whole old key, including the private key stored under the
old selector, is replaced by the new key in one atomic step, so no message is sent unsigned.
Without it, a name that already has a key answers `409` with type
`/api/v2/problems/dkim-key-exists`.

DkimDnsPublicationStatus.description:
Outcome of one attempt to update the ISPConfig DNS zone of a name (FeldHost DKIM DNS publication).
- `published`: the TXT record `<selector>._domainkey` was created or updated with the current key.
  When the selector changed, the old selector's record was removed as well.
- `removed`: the record of a deleted key was removed.
- `noRecordToRemove`: the key was deleted, and the zone held no record for its selector.
- `noZone`: the ISPConfig server has no zone whose origin is exactly the name, so nothing was
  published. A name inside a parent zone (`mail.example.org` in `example.org`) counts as having no
  zone.
- `failed`: the update did not complete within 15 seconds or was refused; see `reason`. The key
  change itself stands.
- `notConfigured`: the DKIM DNS publication is disabled on this server (the default), or enabled
  without the ISPConfig remote API address, user and password, so ISPConfig was not contacted.

DkimDnsPublicationReasonCode.description:
Stable reason of a failed DKIM DNS publication. Clients must treat unknown codes as a generic
failure, because later releases may add codes.
- `unreachable`: the ISPConfig remote API could not be reached (connection or TLS failure).
- `timeout`: the publication did not complete within 15 seconds.
- `authenticationFailed`: ISPConfig refused the remote user's sign-in.
- `remoteFault`: ISPConfig answered a call with an error.
- `invalidResponse`: ISPConfig answered with something that is not a valid remote API answer.
- `staleRecordRemovalFailed`: the new record was published, but the old selector's record could not
  be removed.

DkimDnsPublicationOutcome.description:
Outcome of the DKIM DNS publication that accompanied a key change. A failed publication never
undoes or fails the key change; an administrator can publish the record again with
`publishDkimDnsRecord`.

recordName.description:
Record name relative to the zone (`<selector>._domainkey`) that was published or removed;
`null` for `notConfigured`.

detail.description:
Technical detail for operators, in English, at most 500 characters (for example the
ISPConfig fault message). Never contains the remote password or key material.

DkimKeyChangeResult.description:
The DKIM entry after a key change (generation, import, copy or publishing again), together with
the outcome of the DKIM DNS publication of that change. Never contains the private key.

DkimKeyBulkActionRequest.description:
One action applied to several DKIM keys, as the legacy "ARC/DKIM keys" screen's mass remove does.
Each target is authorised, version-checked, processed and audited on its own, exactly as
`deleteDkimKey` for it; one failure does not stop the others. A target `id` is the name as used
in the key's own path (ASCII or Unicode form; for an unused key stored by legacy under another
spelling, that exact stored name). A name given twice, also in different forms, is processed and
reported once. At most 100 targets may be sent (`tooMany` on `targets`, with `max: 100`).

DkimKeyImportRequest.description:
Imports an existing RSA private key for the name in the path. Rules, each refused with its rule
code in a `422` problem that never echoes any part of the key text:
- `privateKey`: required; at most 16,384 bytes (`tooLong`, `max: 16384`); one PEM-encoded
  private key, PKCS #1 (`RSA PRIVATE KEY`) or PKCS #8 (`PRIVATE KEY`) (`invalidPrivateKey`); not
  encrypted (`encryptedPrivateKey`); RSA (`unsupportedKeyType`, `allowed: [rsa]`); 1,024 to 8,192
  bits (`keyLengthOutOfRange`, `min: 1024`, `max: 8192`). Line endings are normalised to line
  feeds and surrounding whitespace is removed before the key is stored.
- `selector`: as for generation (`invalidFormat`, `format: dkimSelector`; `tooLong`).
- The name in the path must be a valid domain name (`invalidFormat`, `format: domainName`, on
  the key `dkimName`).

privateKey.description: PEM text of the private key. Never logged, audited or returned by this operation.

selector.description: Omit to use the server's default selector.

overwrite.description:
Replace an existing key of the name, including the private key stored under the old
selector, in one atomic step. Without it, a name that already has a key answers `409` with
type `/api/v2/problems/dkim-key-exists`.

DkimKeyCopyRequest.description:
Copies the selector, public key and private key of the name in the path (the source) to one
target. Rules, each refused with its rule code in a `422` problem:
- `target` must be an existing domain or alias domain (`notFound`);
- `target` must differ from the source (`sameAsSource`).

target.description: Target domain or alias domain, in ASCII or Unicode form and in any letter case.

overwrite.description:
Replace an existing key of the target, including the private key stored under its old
selector, in one atomic step. Without it, a target that already has a key answers `409` with
type `/api/v2/problems/dkim-key-exists`. `If-Match` applies to the target's key.

DkimPrivateKey.description:
The private key of one name, exactly as stored. Returned only by `exportDkimPrivateKey`, only to
administrators, and only while the operator setting `SHOW_DKIM_PRIV_KEYS` is enabled. Every export
is audited, without the key.

privateKey.description: PEM text, unchanged from storage (legacy stores PKCS

MtaStsMode.description:
MTA-STS policy mode (RFC 8461): `enforce` (sending servers must not deliver without a valid TLS
connection to a listed MX host), `testing` (they deliver anyway and report), `none` (the policy is
withdrawn).

DnsCapabilities.description:
Server values and limits that shape the DKIM, MTA-STS and DNS diagnostics forms, read from the
current configuration on every request. Contains no secret and no connection detail.

serverHostname.description:
The server's host name (`MAILCOW_HOSTNAME`), lower-case ASCII. It is the expected mail
exchanger and the target of the `mta-sts.` and autodiscover names, so clients can pre-fill
the MTA-STS MX hosts with it.

defaultSelector.description: Server setting, `dkim` upstream (`feldhost` on the FeldHost deployment).

privateKeyMaxBytes.description: Maximum size of an imported private key text.

importKeyLengthMin.description: Smallest RSA key length in bits accepted by an import.

importKeyLengthMax.description: Largest RSA key length in bits accepted by an import.

bulkLimit.description: Most targets one `applyDkimKeyBulkAction` request may name.

dnsPublicationEnabled.description:
Whether key changes are published to an ISPConfig DNS server: the FeldHost setting is on
(off by default) and the ISPConfig remote API address, user and password are configured.

privateKeyExportEnabled.description:
Whether administrators may export private keys (legacy `SHOW_DKIM_PRIV_KEYS`, off by
default). `null` for domain administrators, who can never export.

defaultActive.description: Active state of a policy created without one (`false`, as in legacy).

mxMaxLength.description: Maximum length of the MX hosts joined by commas, as mailcow stores them.

runsPerMinute.description: Runs each caller may start per minute.

serverChecks.description:
Whether the caller's runs include the server-wide checks (host addresses, reverse names,
TLSA). `true` for administrators, `false` for domain administrators.

MtaStsDnsRecord.description: A DNS record that an MTA-STS policy needs.

name.description: Fully qualified record name, without a trailing dot.

MtaStsPolicy.description:
The MTA-STS policy of one domain. While it is active, mailcow's publication endpoint (which stays
in the legacy stack) serves `policyText` at `policyUrl` for the domain and for each of its alias
domains, from the next request on. mailcow's certificate service requests certificates for
`mta-sts.<domain>` and the `mta-sts.` names of the alias domains at its next run, which can take
up to one day. An alias domain never has a policy of its own; it publishes its target domain's.

mxHosts.description: Host names that sending servers may deliver to, in order. `*.` marks a wildcard.

maxAge.description: Seconds for which senders may cache the policy.

policyId.description:
Policy identifier, a 14-digit timestamp (`YYYYMMDDhhmmss`, server time zone) as legacy writes
it. It changes whenever the version, the mode, the MX hosts or their order, or the maximum age
changes, and stays the same when only the active state changes.

policyUrl.description: Address at which the policy is published.

policyText.description: The policy text that the publication endpoint serves while the policy is active.
examples:
version: STSv1
mode: enforce
max_age: 86400
mx: mail.example.org

dnsRecords.description:
The records to publish: `_mta-sts.<domain>` TXT `v=STSv1;id=<policyId>;` and
`mta-sts.<domain>` CNAME to the server's host name. Alias domains need the same two records
under their own names.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored policy, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing the policy.

MtaStsPolicyCreateRequest.description:
A new MTA-STS policy for a domain. Rules, each refused with its rule code in a `422` problem:
- `version`: `STSv1` in any letter case (`notInList`). Omit for `STSv1`.
- `mode`: `enforce`, `testing` or `none` in any letter case (`required`, `notInList`).
- `maxAge`: whole seconds from 1 to 31,557,600 (`required`, `outOfRange`, `min: 1`,
  `max: 31557600`).
- `mxHosts`: at least one entry (`required`). Each entry is trimmed, lower-cased and converted to
  ASCII (UTS #46), may start with `*.`, and must then be a valid domain name
  (`invalidFormat`, `format: mxHost`, on `mxHosts.<index>`). Duplicates are stored once, keeping
  the first occurrence and the order. Joined by commas they must not exceed 255 characters
  (`tooLong`, `max: 255`, on `mxHosts`).

domain.description:
A domain in the caller's scope, in ASCII or Unicode form. Any other name, including an alias
domain's, answers `404`.

active.description: Omit to create an inactive policy, as legacy does.

MtaStsPolicyPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of an MTA-STS policy. Omitted members keep their values; `null` is refused. The
rules of `MtaStsPolicyCreateRequest` apply to each member sent. A change of `version`, `mode`,
`mxHosts` (including their order) or `maxAge` assigns a new `policyId`; a change of only `active`,
or a patch that changes nothing, keeps it.

DnsCheckStatus.description:
Status of one DNS record check.
- `match`: a found value equals the expected value.
- `mismatch`: records were found, but none equals the expected value.
- `missing`: the name has no record of that type.
- `lookupFailed`: the lookup failed, was refused, failed validation or timed out.
- `informational`: records were found for a check that has no exact expected value (DMARC, TLS
  reporting).
- `expectedUnknown`: the expected value could not be determined, for example because the
  server's public address or its certificate could not be read.

Optional checks report their real status; their `optional` flag tells clients not to treat a
missing record as an error.

DnsCheckMessageCode.description:
Stable code of a reason, note or guidance item of DNS diagnostics. Clients translate from the
code and its `params`, and must treat unknown codes as untranslatable (showing `message`), because
later releases may add codes.

Reasons for `lookupFailed`:
- `lookupTimeout`: the lookup reached the resolver's time limit. Params: `timeoutSeconds`.
- `runTimeout`: the run's time limit was reached before this check could start. Params:
  `timeoutSeconds`.
- `lookupError`: the resolver reported a temporary failure or an error, which is also what
  mailcow's validating resolver answers when DNSSEC validation fails. No params.

Reasons for `expectedUnknown`:
- `publicAddressUnknown`: the server's public address could not be determined. Params: `family`
  (`ipv4`).
- `certificateUnavailable`: the certificate presented on SMTP port 25 could not be read. Params:
  `host`, `port`, `cause` (`connectionFailed`, `timeout`, `starttlsRefused`,
  `tlsHandshakeFailed`, `noCertificate`).
- `dkimKeyUnavailable`: the stored DKIM key could not be read from mailcow's shared store.

Reasons for `mismatch`:
- `hostIsAlias`: the server host name is published as an alias (CNAME), which mail exchangers
  must not be. Params: `target`.
- `dkimPublicKeyDiffers`: the DKIM records found carry another public key than the stored one.
- `spfMultipleRecords`: the name publishes more than one SPF record. Params: `count`.
- `spfTooManyLookups`: evaluating the SPF policy needs more than 10 DNS lookups. Params: `limit`.
- `spfTooManyVoidLookups`: evaluating the SPF policy hits more than 2 lookups without an answer.
  Params: `limit`.
- `spfNotPass`: the SPF policy does not authorise a public address of the server. Params:
  `address`, `result` (`fail`, `softfail`, `neutral`, `none`).
- `spfError`: the SPF policy could not be evaluated. Params: `result` (`permerror`,
  `temperror`).

Notes:
- `matchedByAddressRecords`: an alias was expected, and the name instead publishes address records
  equal to the server host name's. Params: `ipv4` (list), `ipv6` (list).
- `nullServiceRecord`: the name publishes a null service record (target `.`), which marks the
  service as not offered; it is accepted as the expected value.
- `noPublicIpv6`: the server has no public IPv6 address, so the IPv6 address and reverse name
  checks are left out and SPF needs to authorise only the IPv4 address (result level).
- `serverChecksOmitted`: the server-wide checks are only run for administrators (result level).
- `propagationDelay`: DNS changes can take up to 24 hours to show, because resolvers cache records
  (result level). Params: `hours`.

Guidance (checks without an exact expected value):
- `spfAuthorizeAddresses`: the SPF policy must authorise these addresses. Params: `ipv4`, `ipv6`
  (either may be `null`).
- `spfSuggestedRecord`: the operator's suggested SPF record. Params: `record`.
- `spfSyntaxReference`: where the SPF syntax is explained. Params: `url`.
- `dmarcPublishPolicy`: publish a DMARC policy. Params: `url`.
- `tlsReportingPublishRecord`: publish a TLS reporting record. Params: `url`.

DnsCheckMessage.description: One reason, note or guidance item of DNS diagnostics.

params.description: Parameters of the code, as documented in `DnsCheckMessageCode`.

message.description: English text for logs and scripts. Clients translate from `code` and `params`.

DnsCheck.description:
One expected DNS record, compared with what mailcow's recursive resolver returns. Values are given
in comparison form: host names in lower case without a trailing dot, IPv6 addresses in full
(expanded) form as legacy shows them, SRV records as `<target> <port>` (priority and weight are not
compared), TLSA records as `<usage> <selector> <matching type> <hex data>`, MX records as the host
name (the preference is not compared), and TXT records with their strings joined.

id.description:
Stable check identifier, unique within a result. Server-wide checks: `a`, `ptr:ipv4`, `aaaa`,
`ptr:ipv6`, `tlsa:25`. Checks of the name: `mx`, `autodiscover`, `srv:autodiscover`,
`autoconfig`, `mta-sts`, `mta-sts-record`, `tls-rpt`, `spf`, `dmarc`, `dkim:<selector>`,
`srv:pop3`, `srv:pop3s`, `srv:imap`, `srv:imaps`, `srv:submission`, `srv:smtps`, `srv:sieve`.
When the stored DKIM key cannot be read, its check has the identifier `dkim` and the status
`expectedUnknown`. Later releases may add identifiers.

scope.description: `server` for the server-wide checks (administrators only), `domain` for the checks of the name.

recordName.description: Fully qualified record name, without a trailing dot.

optional.description: `true` for records whose content is up to the operator (SPF, DMARC, TLS reporting).

expected.description:
The exact expected value in comparison form, or `null` for checks that only give guidance
(SPF, DMARC, TLS reporting) and when the expected value is unknown.

found.description: Every value found, in comparison form. Empty when nothing was found.

guidance.description: What to publish, for checks without an exact expected value.

reason.description: Why the check has its status, where a reason applies; otherwise `null`.

DnsDiagnosticsResult.description:
Result of one DNS diagnostics run for a domain or an alias domain. Nothing is stored and nothing is
audited. Lookups use the same recursive resolver as mailcow's mail services, so the result shows
what they see; DNS changes can take up to 24 hours to show.

name.description: ASCII (punycode) name that was checked.

targetDomain.description: For an alias domain, its target domain, whose MTA-STS policy applies; otherwise `null`.

publicIpv4.description: The server's public IPv4 address used for the checks, or `null` when it could not be determined.

publicIpv6.description: The server's public IPv6 address used for the checks, or `null` when the server has none.

suggestedSpfRecord.description: The operator's suggested SPF record (server setting, empty by default), or `null`.

serverChecksIncluded.description: `true` when the server-wide checks were run (administrators only).

checks.description: The checks in legacy's order, server-wide checks first.

notes.description: Notes about the run as a whole (`noPublicIpv6`, `serverChecksOmitted`, `propagationDelay`).

zoneFile.description:
A zone-file rendering for the name, for import at a DNS provider: an `$ORIGIN` line and one
line per checked record inside the name, with absolute names, MX preference 10, SRV priority 0
and weight 1, and TXT values quoted and split into strings of at most 255 characters. Checks
with an exact expected value contribute that value; SPF, DMARC and TLS reporting contribute
the values found, or a commented placeholder when none was found.

IdentityProviderMappingEntry.description:
One entry of the attribute mapping: users whose mapping attribute equals `attributeValue`
(exactly, letter case included; the first value when the provider sends several) get the
mailbox template `template`. The mapping attribute is the `mailcow_template` value of the user
details for single sign-on, the user's `mailcow_template` attribute for the Keycloak
mailpassword flow, and the configured attribute field for LDAP.

templateExists.description:
`false` when no mailbox template of this name exists any more (renamed or deleted in feature
003). Mailbox creation with this entry then fails, and the update on sign-in is skipped.

IdentityProviderMailboxCounts.description:
Number of mailboxes per external authentication source, counted over all rows of mailcow's
`mailbox` table exactly as the "identity provider in use" checks count them. A deletion is
refused while any count is above zero; a save of another type is refused while a count of a type
other than the saved one is above zero. Usage figures: not part of the version tag.

IdentityProviderCommon.description: Settings and derived values shared by every identity provider type.

attributeMapping.description:
Attribute mapping in stored order (legacy settings `mappers` and `templates`). Entries of a
legacy-stored mapping whose two lists differ in length are shown only where they pair up.

defaultTemplate.description:
Mailbox template for new mailboxes whose mapping attribute matches no entry (`default_template`).
Never used to update existing mailboxes. `null` when unset.

defaultTemplateExists.description: Whether `defaultTemplate` names an existing mailbox template; `null` when unset.

createMailboxOnSignIn.description: Create a mailbox at a user's first sign-in through the provider (`login_provisioning`, default `true`).

ignoreTlsErrors.description:
Do not verify the provider's TLS certificate (`ignore_ssl_error`, default `false`). Applies to
every connection to the provider, including the Keycloak service account calls.

complete.description:
The configuration has every setting legacy requires before it uses a provider. An incomplete
configuration (possible only when stored by legacy) is readable but used for no sign-in, and
single sign-on is unavailable.

missingSettings.description: Names of the members whose stored value is missing when `complete` is `false`; empty otherwise.

modifiedAt.description: Last change of a stored setting (the cached Keycloak service token excluded).

etag.description:
Version tag over every stored setting, secrets included (as an HMAC keyed with the server's
application key, never a plain hash), but not the cached Keycloak service token, the mailbox
counts or the synchronisation status. Equal to the `ETag` header of a
single read; send it in `If-Match`.

IdentityProviderReturnUrls.description: Return addresses of a Keycloak or generic OIDC provider.

legacyReturnUrl.description:
Return URL of the legacy UI's single sign-on (`redirect_url`). Required for a complete
configuration; the legacy UI uses it.

additionalReturnUrls.description:
Further legacy UI return URLs (`redirect_url_extra`); the legacy UI picks the one whose host
name is the host name the user is on.

appReturnUrls.description:
Sign-in return addresses of the new web app, one per host name of the server
(`MAILCOW_HOSTNAME` first, then `ADDITIONAL_SERVER_NAMES`), of the form
`https://<host>/ng/sso/return`. The operator registers them at the provider as allowed
redirect URIs, in addition to the legacy return URLs. Derived from the server's
configuration, not stored.

IdentityProviderSynchronisation.description:
Status of the user import and periodic full synchronisation of a Keycloak or LDAP provider. The
jobs run in mailcow's legacy PHP container (`crons/keycloak-sync.php`, `crons/ldap-sync.php`),
started every minute by mailcow's scheduler; this API never runs or triggers them. Each run reads
the configuration when it starts, so a change applies to the next run; a run in progress finishes
with the settings it started with. A job runs only when user import or periodic full
synchronisation is on, at most once per sync interval counted from the end of its previous run.
User import creates a mailbox, authenticating against the provider, for each provider user that
has none, from the mapped template or else the default template. Periodic full synchronisation
re-applies the mapped template to each existing mailbox of the configured type; the default
template is never used for updates. The jobs log their progress to the scheduled-job log (feature
011).

The status is **derived read-only from that log** (mailcow's Redis list `CRON_LOG`, which keeps
`LOG_LINES` entries, 9,999 by default) and from the sync interval. A failure that the jobs do not
log (for example an LDAP server that cannot be reached at the start of a run) shows only as an
overdue run. Runtime status: not part of the version tag.

enabled.description: User import or periodic full synchronisation is on.

state.description:
- `disabled`: neither user import nor periodic full synchronisation is on.
- `running`: the log shows progress of a run within the last 2 minutes and no end yet.
- `waiting`: the last run completed and the next run is not yet due.
- `overdue`: the next run was expected more than 2 minutes ago and the log shows neither its
  progress nor its end.
- `unknown`: the log holds no entry of the job.

lastCompletedAt.description: End of the newest completed run found in the log.

lastFailedAt.description: Time of the newest run-level failure logged after the last completed run.

nextRunExpectedAt.description:
When the scheduler is expected to start the next run: the first full minute at least one sync
interval after `lastCompletedAt`, or the next full minute after a logged failure. `null` when
disabled or unknown.

IdentityProviderKeycloak.description:
Keycloak configuration. Single sign-on uses the endpoints below
`<serverUrl>/realms/<realm>/protocol/openid-connect/` and requests the scopes `profile` and
`email`, plus `openid` when `version` is 20.0.0 or later. The mailpassword flow, user import and
synchronisation need a service account for the client with the `view-users` permission.

serverUrl.description: Base URL of the Keycloak server, without trailing slashes (`server_url`).

clientSecretSet.description: Whether a client secret is stored. The secret itself is never returned.

version.description: Keycloak version (`version`), which selects the default scopes.

mailpasswordFlow.description:
Password sign-in of Keycloak mailboxes against the password hash in the user's
`mailcow_password` attribute (`mailpassword_flow`).

importUsers.description: Create mailboxes for provider users without one in each synchronisation run (`import_users`).

periodicSync.description: Re-apply the mapped template to existing Keycloak mailboxes in each run (`periodic_sync`).

syncInterval.description: Minutes between the end of a run and the start of the next (`sync_interval`, default 15).

IdentityProviderGenericOidc.description:
Generic OpenID Connect configuration. Single sign-on only; a generic OIDC provider has no
synchronisation and no password sign-in.

clientSecretSet.description: Whether a client secret is stored. The secret itself is never returned.

scopes.description: Requested scopes, separated by single spaces (`client_scopes`).

IdentityProviderLdap.description:
LDAP configuration. A mailbox with the LDAP source signs in with its directory password: the API
looks up the entry whose username field equals the username, below the base DN and within the
filter, and binds as that entry with the password.

hosts.description: Directory hosts, tried in order (`host`, stored comma-separated).

effectivePort.description: Port used for connections. 636 when SSL is on and the stored port is 389, as legacy does.

usernameField.description: Attribute compared with the username, lower-cased (`username_field`, default `mail`).

attributeField.description: Attribute holding the mapping value, lower-cased (`attribute_field`), `null` when unset.

bindPasswordSet.description: Whether a bind password is stored. The password itself is never returned.

importUsers.description: Create mailboxes for directory users without one in each synchronisation run (`import_users`).

periodicSync.description: Re-apply the mapped template to existing LDAP mailboxes in each run (`periodic_sync`).

syncInterval.description: Minutes between the end of a run and the start of the next (`sync_interval`, default 15).

IdentityProvider.description:
The server's external identity provider configuration. At most one exists. It is stored where
legacy stores it (table `identity_provider`), so the legacy UI, `/api/v1`, the legacy single
sign-on, the mail clients' sign-in check and the synchronisation jobs use the same settings.
Secrets (client secret, bind password) are write-only: only whether each is set is shown.
Settings of another type that legacy left stored are not shown and are removed by the next save.

IdentityProviderMappingEntryInput.description:
One entry of the attribute mapping. `template` must name an existing mailbox template when the
configuration is saved (rule code `notFound`); a connection test does not check it.

attributeValue.description: Unique within the mapping, compared exactly (rule code `duplicate`).

IdentityProviderCommonInput.description:
Settings shared by every type in a whole-configuration save or a connection test. An omitted
value takes its default.

attributeMapping.description: Replaces the whole mapping. Default empty.

defaultTemplate.description: Name of an existing mailbox template, or `null` for none (default).

legacyReturnUrl.description: Required. Absolute `https` or `http` URL (rule code `invalidFormat`, format `httpUrl`).

additionalReturnUrls.description: Absolute `https` or `http` URLs; duplicates are stored once. Default empty.

IdentityProviderKeycloakInput.description:
Whole Keycloak configuration. `clientSecret` is required when no Keycloak configuration is stored
and when `serverUrl` differs from the stored one (rule code `secretRequired`); otherwise an
omitted secret keeps the stored one.

serverUrl.description: Absolute `https` or `http` URL; trailing slashes are removed.

scopes.description:
1 to 50 scope names separated by single spaces, each of printable characters other than
space, `"` and `\` (rule code `invalidFormat`, format `scopeList`).

IdentityProviderLdapInput.description:
Whole LDAP configuration. `bindPassword` is required when no LDAP configuration is stored and when
`hosts` differ from the stored ones (rule code `secretRequired`); otherwise an omitted password
keeps the stored one. When both `useSsl` and `useStartTls` are `true`, StartTLS is stored off.

hosts.description: Host names or IP addresses (rule code `invalidFormat`, format `hostName`).

filter.description:
Empty or `null` for none, or a search filter of at most 1,000 characters that starts with
`(`, ends with `)` and has balanced parentheses (format `ldapFilter`).

attributeField.description:
Empty or `null` for none, or an attribute name, stored lower-cased (format
`ldapAttribute`). Required while `importUsers` or `periodicSync` is on.

IdentityProviderInput.description:
A whole identity provider configuration of one type: the body of a save (`PUT /identity-provider`)
and of a connection test. Settings not sent take their defaults. Members that are not settings of
the given type, including read-only members of the representation, are refused (rule code
`conflictsWith` with `field: type`).

IdentityProviderInUseProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/identity-provider-in-use` (status `409`): mailboxes still
authenticate against an external source that the save or deletion would remove.

blockingMailboxes.description: Number of mailboxes that block the request.

IdentityProviderPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) of the stored configuration: only the members sent change, the others
keep their stored values, and the rules of a whole save apply to the result. Arrays
(`attributeMapping`, `additionalReturnUrls`, `hosts`) replace the stored list. `null` clears
`defaultTemplate`, `filter` and `attributeField`; secrets cannot be cleared.
- `type` may be sent only with the stored type (rule code `immutable`); change the type with a
  whole save.
- Members that are not settings of the stored type are refused (rule code `conflictsWith`, `field: type`).
- A changed Keycloak `serverUrl`, generic OIDC `tokenEndpoint` or LDAP `hosts` requires the
  secret in the same request (rule code `secretRequired`).

IdentityProviderConnectionTestResult.description:
Result of a connection test of candidate settings. A failed connection is a successful request
that reports the failure. Nothing is stored. Contains no secret.
- Keycloak: a service token is requested from the token endpoint with the client credentials
  (client credentials grant); success when one is issued. The `view-users` permission that the
  mailpassword flow and the synchronisation need is not checked.
- Generic OIDC: an authorization code exchange with a random, invalid code is sent to the token
  endpoint with the client credentials; success when the endpoint answers and does not reject the
  client credentials (`invalid_client` or status 401 is "credentials rejected").
- LDAP: a connection with the SSL, StartTLS and certificate settings and a bind with the bind DN
  and password.

testedAddress.description: The token endpoint, or the LDAP connection URIs separated by spaces.

failureCategory.description:
`null` on success.
- `unreachable`: name resolution or connection failed.
- `timedOut`: no answer within 7 seconds.
- `tlsCertificateRejected`: the TLS handshake or certificate verification failed.
- `credentialsRejected`: the client credentials or the bind DN and password were rejected.
- `unexpectedResponse`: any other answer; `providerStatus` holds its status.

providerStatus.description: HTTP status, or LDAP result code, of the provider's answer when one was received; `null` otherwise.

SingleSignOnStart.description:
A started single sign-on. Send the browser to `authorizationUrl` in the same tab (no pop-up, no
frame). The provider returns it to the new web app's sign-in return address with `code` and
`state`, or with `error` and `state`.

authorizationUrl.description:
The provider's authorization endpoint with the client ID, the return address for the host
name the client used, the scopes, a single-use `state` and a PKCE `code_challenge` (S256).

expiresAt.description: The pending single sign-on expires 10 minutes after it was started.

SingleSignOnCompletionRequest.description: The `code` and `state` query parameters with which the provider returned the browser, unchanged.

SingleSignOnProviderErrorRequest.description:
The `error` and `state` query parameters with which the provider returned the browser instead of a
code. Do not send `error_description` or `error_uri`; the provider's free text is never accepted.

error.description:
The OAuth 2.0 error code, for example `access_denied`, `login_required` or
`temporarily_unavailable` (rule code `invalidFormat`, format `oauthErrorCode`).

Oauth2Client.description:
An OAuth2 client of mailcow's own OAuth2 provider (table `oauth_clients`). Applications use the
unchanged legacy endpoints `/oauth/authorize`, `/oauth/token` and `/oauth/profile`. The client
secret is returned only when the client is created and when its secret is regenerated.

clientId.description: 12 lowercase hexadecimal characters for clients created by this API or the legacy UI.

redirectUris.description:
Registered redirect URIs in stored order (stored joined by single spaces). Legacy may have
stored values that break the rules of a change, for example an empty list; they are shown as
stored.

scope.description: Always `profile` for clients created by this API or the legacy UI.

activeAccessTokens.description: Number of unexpired access tokens. Usage figure, not part of the version tag.

activeRefreshTokens.description: Number of unexpired refresh tokens. Usage figure, not part of the version tag.

etag.description:
Version tag over the stored client (redirect URIs included, the secret as an HMAC keyed with
the server's application key, tokens excluded). Equal
to the `ETag` header of a single read; send it in `If-Match`.

Oauth2ClientCreateRequest.description: A new OAuth2 client. The server generates the client ID, the secret and the scope `profile`.

redirectUris.description:
Absolute URIs with a scheme, without a fragment and without whitespace (rule code
`invalidFormat`, format `redirectUri`). Duplicates are stored once. Joined by single spaces
they may not exceed 2,000 characters (rule code `tooLong` on `redirectUris`). When several are
registered, applications must name their redirect URI in the authorization request, because
the token endpoint then requires it.

Oauth2ClientWithSecret.description:
An OAuth2 client with its secret. Returned only by the creation and by a secret regeneration;
the secret is never shown again.

Oauth2ClientBulkTarget.description: One OAuth2 client of a bulk action, by its numeric identifier, with an optional version tag.

Oauth2ClientBulkActionRequest.description:
A bulk action on up to 100 OAuth2 clients (rule code `tooMany` beyond). Each client is processed
as a single request for it would be: `delete` as `DELETE /oauth2-clients/{oauth2ClientId}`,
`revokeTokens` as `POST /oauth2-clients/{oauth2ClientId}/token-revocation`, `renewSecret` as
`POST /oauth2-clients/{oauth2ClientId}/secret-regeneration`, whose new secret is returned once in
the item's result (API gap G42, legacy's "renew secret" of the selected clients).

Oauth2ClientBulkItemResult.description:
Outcome of one client of an OAuth2 client bulk action. It has the members of `BulkItemResult`
plus `clientSecret`, the new secret of a `done` `renewSecret` item: shown only in this response,
never again.

id.description: Identifier of the target, as sent.

version.description: The client's new version tag after a `done` outcome, if the client still exists.

clientSecret.description: The new secret (24 lowercase hexadecimal characters) of a `done` `renewSecret` item.

problem.description: Present for `refused`, `outdated` and `failed`. Explains the item's outcome.

Oauth2ClientBulkResult.description:
Result of an OAuth2 client bulk action: the shape of `BulkResult`, whose `done` `renewSecret`
results also carry the new secret. Every audit record of the request carries `bulkRequestId`.

bulkRequestId.description: Identifier of the bulk request (its request ID).

results.description: One result per distinct client, in request order.

Oauth2ClientPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of an OAuth2 client. Only `redirectUris` can change; it replaces the whole list
under the rules of the creation. `clientId` and `scope` are accepted only with their current
values (rule code `immutable` otherwise).

AccountSecondFactorStatus.description:
Second-factor status of an administrator or domain administrator account, over its TOTP,
WebAuthn and Yubico OTP entries (mailcow table `tfa`). Deprecated U2F and HOTP entries never
count, because this API never accepts them.

- `none`: the account has no such entry.
- `active`: at least one entry is active.
- `suspended`: entries exist, but none is active, for example after an administrator suspended
  them until the next sign-in.

Admin.description:
An administrator account (mailcow table `admin`, `superadmin = 1`). Administrators have full
access to the server. Passwords and password hashes are never returned.

username.description: Username as stored. Addressed in paths in any letter case.

active.description: Inactive accounts cannot sign in, and their API keys are refused until reactivated.

forcePasswordChange.description:
The account must change its password at its next sign-in in either UI (mailcow attribute
`force_pw_update`). The session is restricted until then.

forceSecondFactorSetup.description:
The account must set up a second factor at its next sign-in when it has none (mailcow
attribute `force_tfa`).

modifiedAt.description:
Last change of the account row (username, password, status or forced flags), `null` when
never modified.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings (username, status and forced flags; not the second-factor
status or the passkey count), equal to the `ETag` header of a single read. Send it in
`If-Match` when changing or deleting the account, and as `version` in bulk actions.

AdminCreateRequest.description:
A new administrator account. The username is trimmed and lower-cased, and must then be 1 to 255
characters of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-` with at least one letter or digit (rule codes
`tooLong`, `invalidFormat` with `format: accountUsername`), must not be `api` (`reserved`) and
must not be used by any administrator or domain administrator (`409 account-exists`, compared
without regard to letter case).

password.description:
Given once, without a confirmation field. It must meet the server's password policy
(readable through feature 003; each unmet rule is named with its own rule code and
parameter) and is stored in mailcow's configured hash scheme. A value that begins with a
hash-scheme prefix mailcow recognises (for example `{BLF-CRYPT}` or `{SSHA512}`) is stored
as given, without the policy check.

AccountBulkActionRequest.description:
One action applied to several accounts of one role, as the legacy mass actions of the
administrator and domain administrator lists do. A target's `id` is the username in any letter
case; `version` is the account's version tag as read, for example from the list. Each distinct
account is authorised, version-checked, processed and audited on its own, in the order given,
exactly as the single operation for it (`active` in the account's `PATCH`, the second-factor
suspension, or the deletion); one failure does not stop the others. A username given twice is
processed and reported once. At most the bulk limit of targets (`AccountCapabilities.bulkLimit`,
100) may be sent (`tooMany` on `targets`, with the limit as `max`).

- `activate`, `deactivate`: set the account's status (for a domain administrator also every
  assignment's).
- `suspendSecondFactors`: deactivate every TOTP, WebAuthn and Yubico OTP entry until the next
  password sign-in.
- `delete`: delete the account with every effect of the single deletion.

AdminPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of an administrator account. Members that are not sent keep their values; every
member that is sent is applied or refused, never ignored. An empty object is refused (`required`
on `body`) and an unknown member with `unknownField`.

- `username` renames the account (same rules as at creation; `409 account-exists`). Second
  factors, passkeys, API keys and preferences follow the account. The account's other sessions
  and every impersonation of it end; a caller renaming their own account stays signed in under
  the new name.
- `password` sets a new password (same rules as at creation). Forced flags, sessions and API keys
  are not changed.
- `active: false` is refused with `409 last-active-admin` when no other active administrator
  would remain. Changes that do not reduce the number of active administrators are never
  refused by this rule.
- The read-only members of `Admin` (`createdAt`, `modifiedAt`, `secondFactorStatus`,
  `activePasskeyCount`, `etag`) may be sent back unchanged; a different value is refused with
  rule code `immutable`.

DomainAdminPermissions.description:
The 19 permission flags of a domain administrator (mailcow table `da_acl`), named in camelCase
after the legacy columns. Without a stored permission record every flag reads as `false`. The
defaults of a new account are those of the server's mailcow schema, readable through
`GET /capabilities/accounts`. Each flag is enforced by the feature that owns the matching
operations.

loginAs.description: Log in as mailbox users and open their webmail (`da_acl.login_as`).

sogoAccess.description: Manage the webmail access of mailboxes (`da_acl.sogo_access`).

extendSenderAcl.description: Extend sender permissions by external addresses (`da_acl.extend_sender_acl`).

smtpIpAccess.description: Change the allowed hosts for SMTP (`da_acl.smtp_ip_access`).

AccountCapabilities.description:
Server values a client needs before it submits an administrator or domain administrator form.
Read from the server's current mailcow schema and configuration on every request.

domainAdminPermissionDefaults.description:
The flags a new domain administrator gets when they are not sent: the column defaults of the
server's mailcow schema, which can differ between supported mailcow releases.

newAccountDefaults.description: Values a new account gets when they are not sent.

bulkLimit.description: Maximum number of targets of one bulk action.

ssoTokenLifetime.description: Lifetime of a single sign-on token in seconds.

DomainAdminPermissionName.description: Name of one domain administrator permission flag (see `DomainAdminPermissions`).

DomainAdminAssignment.description:
One domain assigned to a domain administrator (mailcow table `domain_admins`). Only active
assignments of existing primary domains grant access. Assignments to names that are not an
existing primary domain (an alias domain name, a removed domain or legacy's `ALL`) are shown with
`domainExists: false`, grant nothing in this API and are dropped the next time the domain set is
saved.

domain.description: Assigned name as stored, in ASCII form.

active.description: The assignment's own status, shown as stored even when a legacy tool made it differ from the account's.

createdAt.description: When the assignment was created. Kept when the domain set is changed and the domain stays.

domainExists.description: `false` when the name is not an existing primary domain.

DomainAdmin.description:
A domain administrator account (mailcow table `admin`, `superadmin = 0`) with its assigned
domains and permission flags. Accounts without any assignment are included and shown with an
empty `domains` list. Passwords and password hashes are never returned.

username.description: Username as stored. Addressed in paths in any letter case.

active.description:
The account's own status. Inactive accounts cannot sign in, and their API keys are refused
until reactivated. Changing it also changes the status of every assignment.

forcePasswordChange.description: The account must change its password at its next sign-in (mailcow attribute `force_pw_update`).

forceSecondFactorSetup.description: The account must set up a second factor at its next sign-in when it has none (mailcow attribute `force_tfa`).

modifiedAt.description: Last change of the account row, `null` when never modified. Assignment and permission changes do not update it.

etag.description:
Version tag of the stored settings (username, status, forced flags, assignments and
permission flags; not the second-factor status or the passkey count), equal to the `ETag`
header of a single read. Send it in `If-Match` when changing or deleting the account, and as
`version` in bulk actions.

DomainAdminPermissionsPatch.description:
Any subset of the 19 domain administrator permission flags. Only the flags sent are changed;
the others keep their values. A name that is not one of the 19 flags is refused with rule code
`unknownField` on `permissions.<name>`, and nothing changes. When the account has no stored
permission record, a change creates it with the sent flags and every other flag `false`.

DomainAdminCreateRequest.description:
A new domain administrator account. `username` and `password` follow the rules of
`AdminCreateRequest`. Each entry of `domains` is normalised (trimmed, lower-cased, converted to
ASCII with the UTS #46 rules) and must be an existing primary domain: an invalid name is refused
with `invalidFormat` (`format: domainName`), an alias domain name with `notEligible`
(`kind: aliasDomain`) and an unknown name with `notFound`, each on `domains.<index>`.
Duplicates are merged. Permission flags that are not sent get this server's defaults, the values
`GET /capabilities/accounts` reports. The account, its assignments (with the account's status) and
its permission record are stored together or not at all; an orphaned permission record left by
legacy for the same username is replaced.

domains.description: Domain names in ASCII or Unicode form.

DomainAdminAssignmentInput.description:
An assignment sent back in a domain set, as read from `DomainAdmin.domains`. Only `domain`
counts. The other members are read-only: they are accepted when equal to the stored assignment
of that domain and refused with rule code `immutable` otherwise (a domain that is not assigned
yet accepts only `domain`).

DomainAdminPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a domain administrator account. Members that are not sent keep their values;
every member that is sent is applied or refused, never ignored. An empty object is refused
(`required` on `body`) and an unknown member with `unknownField`.

- `username`, `password`, `forcePasswordChange` and `forceSecondFactorSetup` follow the rules of
  `AdminPatch`. A rename also moves the assignments (with their creation times), the permission
  record, the API keys and the preferences, removes unused single sign-on tokens, and ends the
  account's sessions and every impersonation of it.
- `active` changes the account and every one of its assignments.
- `domains` replaces the whole domain set. It must contain at least one domain (`required`), and
  each entry follows the rules of `DomainAdminCreateRequest`. Assignments to domains that stay
  keep their creation time and status; new assignments get the account's status. Assignments to
  names that are not existing primary domains are dropped.
- `permissions` changes only the flags it names (see `DomainAdminPermissionsPatch`).
- The read-only members of `DomainAdmin` may be sent back unchanged; a different value is refused
  with rule code `immutable`.

domains.description: Domain names in ASCII or Unicode form, or assignments as read.

DomainAdminSsoToken.description:
A single sign-on token for one domain administrator. It signs the account in once, without a
password and without a second factor, within 30 seconds of issue: either at the legacy domain
administrator login (`/domainadmin?sso_token=<token>`) or through `POST /session/sso-token`.
Using it in one place consumes it for both. This is the only response that ever contains the
token.

token.description: Five groups of six upper-case hexadecimal characters, as legacy mailcow issues them.

SsoTokenSignInRequest.description:
A single sign-on token issued for a domain administrator, through this API
(`POST /domain-admins/{username}/sso-token`) or legacy `/api/v1` (`add/sso/domain-admin`).
Surrounding whitespace is ignored and letter case does not matter.

ImpersonationStartRequest.description:
The account to impersonate. `role` names its type: `mailboxUser` with the mailbox address
(normalised as feature 003 does: trimmed, lower-cased, domain in ASCII form), or `domainAdmin`
with the domain administrator's username (trimmed, lower-cased). Administrators can never be
impersonated.

ImpersonationStarted.description:
The impersonation that started, the caller's new identity, and the session's new anti-forgery
token. The session identifier and the anti-forgery token were renewed: use `csrfToken.token` for
every further state-changing request.

ImpersonationPermissionFlagProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required` (status `403`) for impersonation and
webmail on behalf (feature 007): the caller is a domain administrator without the `loginAs`
permission flag (`da_acl.login_as`). The flag is checked before the target is looked up, so the
answer never reveals whether a target outside the caller's scope exists. Nothing changed.

requiredFlags.description: The missing flags, named as in `PermissionFlags`; any one of them would allow the operation.

MailboxWebmailSignIn.description:
A single-use webmail sign-in for a mailbox, obtained on the user's behalf. The response sets the
webmail hand-off cookie of feature 005 in the requesting browser; opening `url` in that browser
shows the mailbox's webmail without a sign-in prompt. The caller's session in this API is not
changed. The hand-off replaces a legacy UI sign-in of the same browser.

url.description: Address of the webmail to open in the same browser.

InstallationVersion.description:
The installed mailcow version, as the legacy UI shows it in its dashboard and footer. Read from
