The uploaded logo of one theme (legacy `MAIN_LOGO` or `MAIN_LOGO_DARK`), or the fact that none is
set. The image itself is served by `GET /public-config/logos/{variant}`. A logo uploaded through
the legacy UI that this API would now refuse stays readable here.

isSet.description: `false` when no logo is uploaded; clients then show the deployment's default logo.

mediaType.description: Media type the logo is stored with. `null` when not set.

sizeBytes.description: File size in bytes. `null` when not set.

width.description:
Width in pixels. For an SVG, its declared width when it has one with an absolute unit or no
unit, otherwise `null`.

height.description: Height in pixels, with the same rules as `width`.

url.description: Address of the image (`GET /public-config/logos/{variant}` with its version), `null` when not set.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored logo, equal to the `ETag` header.

text.description: Plain text, stored as given. The legacy UI escapes it when it renders it. Empty when not set.

type.description:
Style of the banner. `null` means none; an active announcement without a type is shown in the
client's neutral style, as legacy allows.

active.description: The banner is shown only while `active` is `true` and `text` is not empty.

UiTexts.description:
The UI texts of the legacy customisation. `pageTitle`, `productName`, `appsHeading` and
`announcement.text` are plain text. `loginHelpHtml` and `footerHtml` are operator-authored HTML,
stored and returned as given: clients must sanitise them before rendering, as for the public
configuration. Empty values mean the defaults described for each field.

pageTitle.description:
Browser title (`TITLE_NAME`, stored HTML-escaped as legacy does and returned as plain text).
Empty means `pageTitleDefault`.

pageTitleDefault.description: The deployment default used while `pageTitle` is empty, as in the public configuration.

productName.description: Name shown on the login page (`MAIN_NAME`, stored like `pageTitle`). Empty means `productNameDefault`.

appsHeading.description:
Heading of the apps list (`APPS_NAME`, stored like `pageTitle`). Empty means the web app's
translated default.

loginHelpHtml.description: Operator HTML shown below the login form (`HELP_TEXT`). Empty when not set.

footerHtml.description:
Operator HTML footer (`UI_FOOTER`). When it is empty and the footer key of older mailcow
releases (`UI_IMPRESS`) holds a value, that value is returned here and moved to `UI_FOOTER` by
the next change of the UI texts.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored UI texts, equal to the `ETag` header.

UiTextsPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of the UI texts. Members that are not sent keep their values. An empty string
clears a text. Single-line texts must not contain line breaks or other control characters.

LoginPageSettings.description:
The login page options (`CUSTOM_LOGIN`) with their version tag. Forcing single sign-on is a
presentation option: it takes effect only while single sign-on is available (feature 012) and
never makes the API refuse another sign-in method, as in legacy.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored options, equal to the `ETag` header.

LoginPageSettingsPatch.description: JSON Merge Patch of the login page options. Members that are not sent keep their values.

AppLinkSettingsEntry.description:
One custom app link (an entry of legacy `APP_LINKS`). Addresses are absolute `http` or `https`
URLs, or paths on the mailcow host that start with a single `/`. Script and other schemes are
refused.

name.description: Shown name, without line breaks. Names need not be unique.

url.description: Address on the login page and for signed-out users (legacy `link`).

signedInUrl.description:
Address for signed-in users (legacy `user_link`), which may contain `%u` for the signed-in
username. `null` means `url` is used, as legacy does.

showOnLoginPage.description: `false` hides the link on the login page only (legacy `hide`). Signed-in users always see it.

AppLinkSettings.description:
The custom app links in their stored order, and the built-in links of the operator's
configuration (`$MAILCOW_APPS`), which are read-only here. Clients read the effective links,
built-in first, from the public configuration (`GET /public-config`).

builtInLinks.description: Built-in links, as the legacy screen shows them. Never changed by this API.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored custom links, equal to the `ETag` header.

AppLinkSettingsPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of the app links. `links` replaces the whole list of custom links, in the given
order. Every entry is validated; one invalid entry refuses the request and names that entry
(`links.3.url`).

BrandColors.description:
The brand colours stored by this API (not visible in the legacy UI), and the colours in effect.
A light colour reaches at least 4.5:1 against `#ffffff`, a dark colour at least 4.5:1 against the
dark reference surface `#1d2939` (WCAG 2.2 contrast formula). Both references are agreed with
mailcowui-ng, which shows brand colours only on surfaces at least as contrasting; changing them is
a contract change.

light.description: Stored light-theme colour, lower case. `null` when not set.

dark.description: Stored dark-theme colour, lower case. `null` when not set.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored colours, equal to the `ETag` header.

BrandColorsPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of the brand colours. A colour is a six-digit hexadecimal sRGB colour
(`#RRGGBB`, either letter case); `null` clears it. A colour below the minimum contrast is refused
with the rule code `insufficientContrast` and the parameters `ratio` (measured, rounded down to
two decimals), `minimum` and `surface`.

IpCheckSetting.description:
The IP check opt-in (`IP_CHECK`). While it is on, administrators may look up the server's public
addresses through third-party services (feature 011); while it is off, that lookup is refused
without any outbound request. Off by default.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored setting, equal to the `ETag` header.

IpCheckSettingPatch.description: JSON Merge Patch of the IP check opt-in.

PasswordResetNotification.description:
The e-mail that self-service password reset (feature 005) sends (`PW_RESET_FROM`,
`PW_RESET_SUBJ`, `PW_RESET_TEXT`, `PW_RESET_HTML`). Password reset is available only while both
a sender and a subject are set: clearing either switches it off.

Placeholders, replaced in the subject and both templates: `{{link}}` (the reset link; without it
the e-mail is useless), `{{username}}` (the mailbox), `{{username2}}` (the recovery address),
`{{date}}` (the request time), `{{token_lifetime}}` (minutes the link stays valid) and
`{{hostname}}` (the server's host name).

sender.description: Sender address. Empty when not set.

textTemplate.description: Plain-text template, or mailcow's default when `templatesAreDefault` is `true`.

htmlTemplate.description: HTML template, or mailcow's default when `templatesAreDefault` is `true`.

templatesAreDefault.description:
`true` when both stored templates are empty, so that mailcow's default templates apply and
are returned here.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored notification, equal to the `ETag` header.

PasswordResetNotificationPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of the password reset notification. An empty `sender` or `subject` switches
password reset off. Sending both templates empty, or one empty while the other is stored empty,
restores mailcow's default templates. Templates are at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes) each.

sender.description: Empty, or a valid e-mail address without control characters.

subject.description: At most 255 characters, without line breaks.

QuotaNotificationSettings.description:
The e-mail Dovecot sends to a user whose mailbox crosses 80% and, again, 95% of its quota
(`QW_SENDER`, `QW_SUBJ`, `QW_HTML`). The values in effect are returned, with markers for those
that are Dovecot's defaults because nothing is stored. A change applies to the next notification.

The template is rendered by Dovecot with the variables `{{username}}` and `{{percent}}`. When
Dovecot cannot parse the stored template it falls back to the default template. Copies to the
per-domain recipients (`GET /domains/{domain}/quota-notification-recipients`) carry the user as
sender and the subject followed by the username in parentheses.

senderIsDefault.description: `true` when no sender is stored and Dovecot uses `quota-warning@localhost`.

subjectIsDefault.description: `true` when no subject is stored and Dovecot uses "Quota warning".

htmlTemplateIsDefault.description: `true` when no template is stored and mailcow's default template applies.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored settings, equal to the `ETag` header.

QuotaNotificationSettingsPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of the quota notification settings. An empty string restores Dovecot's default
for that value. The template is not checked: a template Dovecot cannot parse makes it use its
default template.

sender.description: Empty, or a valid e-mail address without control characters.

subject.description: At most 255 characters, without line breaks.

QuotaNotificationRecipients.description:
The addresses that receive a copy of the quota notifications of one domain's mailboxes, and
whether copies are sent (`QW_BCC`). A domain without stored settings has an empty, inactive list.
Deleting a domain keeps these settings, so they reappear when the domain is created again, as in
legacy.

active.description: Always `false` while `recipients` is empty.

etag.description: Version tag of the domain's stored settings, equal to the `ETag` header.

QuotaNotificationRecipientsPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a domain's copy recipients. `recipients` replaces the whole list. Each entry is
a valid e-mail address without control characters; one invalid entry refuses the request and is
named (`recipients.2`). Entries that differ only in letter case are stored once, keeping the first
spelling. An empty list is stored as inactive, whatever `active` says, as in legacy.

RspamdSettingsRule.description:
A rule of mailcow's Rspamd settings map (table `settingsmap`). Active rules reach Rspamd through
mailcow's generated settings map at Rspamd's next refresh (within about a minute), without a
restart.

content.description: Rule content in Rspamd's UCL syntax, stored trimmed.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored rule, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read.

RspamdSettingsRuleCreateRequest.description:
A new settings rule. The content must not be empty after trimming, must be at most 1 MiB, and
outside comments (`#` to the end of the line) and quoted strings its braces and brackets must be
balanced and properly nested and every quoted string closed (rule code `unbalancedStructure`).
Unknown options are accepted: Rspamd decides. A rule created without `active` is inactive, as in
legacy.

SettingsValidationResult.description:
Result of a request sent with `validateOnly=true` that passed every validation rule. Nothing was
stored, restarted or audited. A request that fails validation answers `422` exactly as a real
request would.

RspamdSettingsRulePatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a settings rule, with the rules of `RspamdSettingsRuleCreateRequest`. An empty
description or empty content is refused (legacy keeps the old value).

RspamdRegexMapSummary.description:
A global regex map as the list returns it: everything but its content, which
`GET /settings/rspamd-regex-maps/{mapId}` returns (docs/api-gaps.md G17: lists stay light, also on
slow connections). The version tag equals the one of the single read.

id.description: The map's file name, its stable identifier.

name.description: English name from the operator's configuration.

available.description: `false` when the map file does not exist on this server; replacing it is then refused.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the map's content in bytes, 0 while the map is unavailable.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored content.

RspamdRegexMap.description:
A global regex map that the operator's configuration makes editable (legacy `$RSPAMD_MAPS['regex']`,
13 by default), read from the map file Rspamd reads. Rspamd reloads a changed map without a
restart.

id.description: The map's file name, its stable identifier.

name.description: English name from the operator's configuration.

available.description:
`false` when the map file does not exist on this server; `content` is then empty and replacing
the map is refused with `regex-map-unavailable`.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored content.

RspamdRegexMapReplaceRequest.description:
New content of a regex map, at most 1 MiB. Every line must be empty, a comment starting with `#`,
or a regular expression `/pattern/` followed by at most one of the flags `i`, `m` or `s`, whose
pattern contains no further `/` and compiles (PCRE). A failing line is refused with the rule code
`invalidRegexLine` on `content`, with the parameters `line` (1-based) and `reason`. The content is
stored trimmed and ending with a line break, as in legacy.

RspamdEffectiveSettingsMap.description:
The settings map as mailcow generates it for Rspamd (`settings.php`), read-only. Each active rule
appears in an `additional_settings_<id>` block, after mailcow's own generated settings.

RspamdUiPasswordRequest.description:
New password of the Rspamd web interface, given once. 6 to 256 characters, without control
characters; quotes and spaces are kept exactly. It is handed to mailcow's container service and
never stored, logged or returned by this API.

GlobalSieveFilter.description:
A global Sieve script that Dovecot compiles when it starts: the pre-filter runs before every
mailbox's own filters, the post-filter after them (by default it files spam into the Junk folder).
It is read from the shared file that the legacy UI edits. An empty script means no global filter.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored script.

GlobalSieveFilterReplaceRequest.description:
New script, at most 1 MiB. Line endings are normalised to line feeds. It must be valid Sieve
syntax as legacy's parser checks it; otherwise it is refused with the rule code `sieveSyntax`
(shared with feature 005's mailbox filters) on `script`, with the parameters `message` (the
parser's message) and `line`. An empty script is
accepted and means no global filter.

deferRestart.description:
`true` saves the script without restarting Dovecot; it then takes effect at Dovecot's next
restart. By default Dovecot is restarted so that it compiles the script, which briefly
interrupts IMAP, POP3 and delivery.

DovecotRestartOutcome.description:
Outcome of the Dovecot restart that follows a saved global Sieve filter. A failed restart does not
undo the saved script, which then takes effect at Dovecot's next start.

outcome.description:
`done`: mailcow's container service restarted Dovecot. `failed`: it reported a failure or did
not answer within its timeout (the restart may still happen). `deferred`: the client asked to
apply the change at the next restart.

detail.description: English explanation of a failure, `null` otherwise.

Preset.description:
An example that mailcow ships (`data/web/inc/presets/<kind>/*.yml`), read-only. Clients translate
the headline through `translationKey` in mailcow's language files and fall back to `headline`.

id.description: The preset's file name without extension.

translationKey.description:
Key of the headline in mailcow's language files (`admin.rsettings_preset_4`,
`mailbox.sieve_preset_1`), `null` when the preset has a literal headline.

content.description: Example content (an Rspamd settings rule or a Sieve script).

MassMailJobStatus.description:
`running`: messages are being delivered. `completed`: every recipient has its final outcome.
`cancelled`: an administrator cancelled the job; recipients that were still pending were skipped.

MassMailSelection.description:
Which mailboxes receive a mass mail. The selection starts from every receiving mailbox: every
mailbox that is not a resource and is active or allowed to receive mail (`active` 1 or 2). It may
be limited to `domains`, and may then either include only the mailboxes in `include` or exclude
the mailboxes in `exclude`, not both (rule code `mutuallyExclusive`). Every named domain must be a
domain of the server (not an alias domain) and every named mailbox a receiving mailbox within the
chosen domains; each failing entry is named (`selection.exclude.2`, rule codes `notFound` or
`notEligible`). An empty object selects every receiving mailbox.

MassMailRecipientCounts.description: Number of recipients per outcome. They add up to the job's recipient count.

MassMailJobSummary.description:
A mass mail job as the list returns it: everything but its bodies, which
`GET /mass-mail-jobs/{jobId}` returns (gap G17: lists stay light, also on slow connections).

MassMailJobCreateRequest.description:
A mass mail job. `expectedRecipients` is the recipient count of the preview the administrator
confirmed: when the selection yields another number at this moment, the job is refused with
`/api/v2/problems/mass-mail-recipient-count-changed` and nothing is sent. A selection without
recipients is refused (rule code `tooFew` on `selection`).

sender.description:
Valid e-mail address without control characters. Legacy suggests `noreply@<server host name>`
(see `GET /capabilities/settings`).

textBody.description: Plain-text body, at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes).

htmlBody.description: Optional HTML body, at most 1 MiB. When given, both bodies are sent as alternatives.

MassMailJob.description:
A mass mail job. Each recipient receives one message addressed only to itself, delivered directly
into the mailbox through Dovecot's local delivery (LMTP), as legacy does: the message does not
pass Postfix or Rspamd, so it is never filtered, quarantined, signed or relayed. Messages carry
`X-Mailer: MooMassMail`. Jobs are kept for the audit retention period (365 days by default) and
change only through their delivery progress and cancellation.

startedAt.description: When the first delivery began, `null` before.

finishedAt.description: When the job completed or its cancellation was confirmed, `null` while running.

cancelledBy.description: The administrator who cancelled the job, `null` otherwise.

MassMailRunningProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/mass-mail-already-running` (status `409`): another job is
running. Nothing was sent.

MassMailRecipientCountProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/mass-mail-recipient-count-changed` (status `409`): the selection
now yields `actualRecipients`, not the confirmed count. Nothing was sent.

MassMailPreviewRequest.description: The selection to preview. Paging and the address search are query parameters.

MassMailPreviewRecipient.description: One mailbox that the selection yields.

MassMailRecipientOutcome.description:
`pending`: not delivered yet (including retries of a temporary refusal). `delivered`: Dovecot
accepted the message into the mailbox. `failed`: Dovecot refused it, temporary refusals persisted
after the retries, or the delivery was interrupted. `skipped`: the job was cancelled first.

MassMailRecipient.description: One recipient of a mass mail job.

failureCode.description: For `failed`, the stable reason of the failure (gap G16); `null` otherwise.

failureReason.description:
For `failed`: Dovecot's reply (for example an over-quota refusal), `interrupted` when this
API stopped during the delivery, or the connection error, in English. `null` otherwise.

LicenseStatus.description:
The server's GUID, which mailcow computes from its host name and mail encryption key, and the last
verification result against mailcow's license service, as the legacy dashboard shows it.

guid.description: The GUID (64 hexadecimal characters), `null` when mailcow marked it invalid or has none.

guidValid.description:
`false` when mailcow marked the GUID invalid (`INVALID`) or has none. It can still be submitted
for verification, as in legacy.

verifiedAt.description: Time of the verification when it was made through this API, `null` otherwise.

customerId.description: Customer ID reported by the license service for a valid GUID, `null` otherwise.

serviceId.description: Service ID reported for a valid GUID, `null` otherwise.

supportLevel.description: Support level for a valid GUID, shown by the legacy dashboard as that many cows. `null` otherwise.

SelfServiceCapabilities.description:
Server settings and limits that clients of the self-service operations need before they submit,
computed from the server's current configuration on every request. Contains no secret.
`passwordReset` is always present, also for signed-out callers. The other members are present
for authenticated callers (a session or an API key), and `account` only for a signed-in session.

available.description:
`false` when the operator's reset message has no sender or no subject, in which case every
reset request answers `password-reset-unavailable`. Offer "Forgot password" only when
`true`.

tokenLifetimeMinutes.description: Validity of a reset link (legacy `PW_RESET_TOKEN_LIFETIME`, 15 by default).

enabled.description: `false` when mailcow runs without the groupware (`SKIP_SOGO=y`): no webmail, no groupware resets.

webmailUrl.description: Address of the webmail on this host.

countryLookup.description: Whether countries of uncached public addresses are looked up with the external service.

bulkLimit.description: Maximum number of mailboxes in one bulk TLS change (100 by default).

limits.description: Size limits of this feature's values.

nameMaxLength.description: Second-factor and app password names (stored form), 255.

descriptionMaxLength.description: Temporary alias and Sieve filter descriptions, 255.

pushoverSounds.description: Pushover's built-in notification sounds, in legacy order. Other sound names are accepted too.

totpIssuer.description: Issuer name shown by authenticator apps (legacy `OTP_LABEL`).

account.description: The signed-in account. Present only for sessions.

secondFactorRequired.description:
The account must keep at least one second factor (legacy `force_tfa`). Removing an entry
or all entries is then refused with `second-factor-required-by-policy`; warn before
offering it.

passwordChangeAvailable.description: `false` for a mailbox whose password lives in an external identity provider.

secondFactorManagementAvailable.description: `false` for a mailbox whose password lives in an external identity provider.

OwnPasswordChangeRequest.description:
A new password for the signed-in account. The password is given once, without a confirmation
field, must meet the password policy (`GET /me/password-policy`) and must not start with a
hash-scheme prefix such as `{SSHA512}` (rule `preHashedPassword`).

currentPassword.description:
Required, for every role, unless the session is restricted by a forced password change
(pending action `passwordChange`), where it is ignored.

endOtherSessions.description:
End the account's other sessions of this API (and their webmail hand-offs). The current
session always stays signed in. Legacy UI sessions are never affected.

sessionsEnded.description: Number of the account's other sessions of this API that were ended.

activeAppPasswords.description: Active app passwords of the mailbox, which keep working (always 0 for administrator accounts).

mailServerCacheSeconds.description:
The mail server may accept the old password from mail clients for up to this many seconds
(its credential cache period), as after a change in the legacy UI.

SelfServicePermissionFlagProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required` (status `403`): the change needs a
permission flag that the caller lacks, a mailbox user's own `user_acl` flag or, for app passwords,
push notifications and Sieve filters, the domain administrator's own `da_acl` flag. Nothing
changed. Values sent with their current value never need the flag, and reading never needs it.

requiredFlags.description:
The flags of which any one allows the change, named as in `PermissionFlags` (camelCase).
The self-service operations always need exactly one.

SelfServiceTemporaryFailureProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/temporary-failure` (status `503`): a service the operation needs
is unavailable or did not answer in time, and nothing was changed. Retry after the `Retry-After`
header.

dependency.description:
The unavailable service. Known values: `sharedStore` (mailcow's Redis), `mailStore` (the
container API or the Dovecot container), `pushover` (the Pushover service),
`addressGeneration` (no free temporary alias address was found). Later features may add
values.

OwnSecondFactorType.description:
Type of a stored second-factor entry (mailcow `tfa.authmech`). `totp` authenticator apps,
`webauthn` security keys, `yubiOtp` Yubico OTP keys. `u2f` and `hotp` are deprecated entries that
this API lists but never accepts; only an administrator can reset them.

OwnSecondFactor.description:
One second-factor entry of the signed-in account, wherever it was enrolled. Never contains a
secret, key handle, public key, certificate or Yubico credential.

name.description: Name given at enrolment (`tfa.key_id`).

active.description:
Inactive entries were disabled by an administrator; they become active again at the next
sign-in that finds no active second factor.

usable.description: Whether this API accepts the entry at sign-in (`false` for `u2f` and `hotp`).

yubicoPublicId.description: Public identifier of a Yubico OTP key (the first 12 characters of its OTPs), `null` for other types.

usedForCurrentSignIn.description: Whether this entry completed the current session's sign-in.

OwnTotpEnrolmentConfirmation.description:
Confirms the session's TOTP enrolment (`POST /me/second-factors/totp-enrolment`) with a current
code from the authenticator app. A wrong code keeps the enrolment open until five wrong codes or
ten minutes; the confirming code is not accepted again for sign-in.

name.description: Trimmed; 1 to 255 characters.

currentPassword.description: Required unless the session is restricted by `secondFactorSetup`.

OwnWebAuthnSecondFactorEnrolment.description:
The authenticator's response to the options from
`POST /me/second-factors/webauthn-registration-options`. The options are consumed by this request.

currentPassword.description: Required unless the session is restricted by `secondFactorSetup`.

OwnYubiOtpEnrolment.description:
A YubiKey in Yubico OTP mode with the Yubico API credentials it is verified with. The OTP is
checked with the Yubico service using these credentials. An existing entry of the account with
the same key (the first 12 characters of the OTP) is replaced.

currentPassword.description: Required unless the session is restricted by `secondFactorSetup`.

OwnSecondFactorEnrolmentRequest.description:
Enrols a second factor for the signed-in account, stored where legacy mailcow stores it (table
`tfa`, active), so it completes the second-factor step of both UIs.

SecondFactorEnrolmentFailedProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-enrolment-failed` (status `400`): the TOTP code was
wrong, the WebAuthn response did not verify, or the Yubico service rejected the OTP. Nothing was
stored.

attemptsRemaining.description: For TOTP, wrong codes left before the enrolment is cancelled.

OwnTotpEnrolment.description:
A started TOTP enrolment, bound to the session. The secret, the provisioning address and the QR
code are returned only here, once. Confirm with `POST /me/second-factors` (`type: totp`) within
`expiresAt`; a new start replaces this enrolment.

secret.description: Random 160-bit secret in base32, for manual entry.

provisioningUri.description: `otpauth://totp/` address naming the account and the issuer.

qrCode.description:
QR code of `provisioningUri` as a data URI (`data:image/svg+xml;base64,…`). The SVG uses only
the elements `svg` (with `width`, `height` and `viewBox`), one white background `rect`, `g`
(with `transform`) and one black `path` (`fill-rule="evenodd"`); no scripts, styles, text or
external references, so clients may render it as an image (G26). Clients that prefer their own
rendering use `provisioningUri`.

OwnSecondFactorWebAuthnCreationOptions.description:
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` (WebAuthn Level 3) for a security key used as a second
factor. Unlike passkeys, the credential need not be discoverable. Pass it to
`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON()` and `navigator.credentials.create()`.

excludeCredentials.description: The account's existing WebAuthn second factors.

OwnSecondFactorWebAuthnOptions.description: Single-use WebAuthn second-factor registration options bound to the session.

expiresAt.description: Five minutes after issue. The options are consumed by the first enrolment attempt.

OwnSecondFactorRemovalRequest.description: Confirms the removal of all second factors with the current password.

OwnRecoveryEmail.description:
The mailbox's password recovery address (mailcow `mailbox.attributes.recovery_email`), where
password reset messages are sent. Shared with the legacy UI, where an administrator can also set
it (feature 003).

etag.description: Version tag of the stored address, equal to the `ETag` header.

OwnRecoveryEmailReplacement.description:
Sets, changes or removes the recovery address. Needs the current password, and the `pwReset`
permission unless the address stays the same.

oneOf.description: A valid e-mail address, or the empty string to remove it.

publicComment.description: The alias's public comment, as plain text.

MailboxOverview.description:
The signed-in mailbox user's own mailbox at a glance, as the legacy user page shows it. Every
text is plain text.

displayName.description: The mailbox's display name, possibly empty.

quota.description: As feature 003 computes it from the mail server's usage record.

percentUsed.description: Rounded whole percent; `null` for an unlimited quota.

enabled.description: Whether the server runs the groupware (`SKIP_SOGO` not set).

redirectAfterSignIn.description:
The legacy "SOGo access" preference: after signing in, the user is sent to webmail. A
client honours it by calling `POST /me/webmail-handoff` and opening the address.

recoveryEmail.description: The recovery address for the mailcow source; `null` when none is set or for an external source.

directAliases.description: Aliases whose only target is this mailbox.

sharedAliases.description: Aliases with this mailbox among several targets.

aliasDomainAddresses.description: The mailbox's local part in each alias domain of its domain.

sendAs.description: What the mailbox may send as (mailcow `sender_acl`), besides its own addresses and aliases.

domains.description: Whole domains (`@domain`), including the alias domains of such a domain.

anyAddress.description: The mailbox may send as any address (`*`).

catchAllAddresses.description: Catch-all aliases (`@domain`) that deliver to this mailbox.

temporaryAliasDomains.description: Domains available for temporary aliases (FR-081), the mailbox's domain first.

activeTemporaryAliases.description: Permanent or not yet expired temporary aliases.

publicComment.description: The alias's public comment, as plain text.

MailboxClientServer.description:
One mail service as mail clients reach it. `tlsPort` uses TLS from the first byte (implicit TLS),
`starttlsPort` starts in plain text and upgrades with STARTTLS. A port the server does not
publish is `null`.

port.description: HTTPS port, TLS from the first byte.

MailboxClientConfiguration.description:
How to set up a mail client by hand for the signed-in mailbox, from the server's autodiscover
settings (the values the legacy client setup help passes to the mailcow documentation). Mail
clients authenticate with the address and the account's password, or with an app password.
CalDAV, CardDAV and ActiveSync are `null` when the groupware is disabled.

authentication.description: Normal password authentication, with the account's password or an app password.

autodiscoverType.description: The server's general autodiscover service type.

outlookUsesActiveSync.description: Whether autodiscover sets Outlook up with ActiveSync (`useEASforOutlook`).

documentationUrl.description: The mailcow client documentation page with the parameters legacy appends.

port.description: HTTPS port, TLS from the first byte.

AppleProfileRequest.description: Options of an Apple connection profile that embeds a newly generated app password.

appPasswordName.description:
Name of the new app password. Default: `iPad`, `iPhone` or `Mac` after the request's user
agent, otherwise the user agent (cut to 255 characters), as legacy names it.

WebmailHandOff.description:
A webmail sign-in handed to the requesting browser. The response sets mailcow's legacy session
cookie (`MCSESSID` by default) for a session that grants webmail only: opening `url` in the same
browser shows the mailbox without a sign-in prompt, while the legacy UI and `/api/v1` treat the
browser as signed out.

url.description: Address of the webmail to open in the same browser.

address.description: The mailbox address whose password was forgotten (any letter case, domain in ASCII or Unicode form).

PasswordResetAcknowledgement.description:
The same acknowledgement for every well-formed request, whether or not a message was sent. If the
address belongs to an eligible mailbox with a recovery address, a message with a reset link valid
for `tokenLifetimeMinutes` is on its way to that recovery address.

token.description: The token from the reset link (five groups of six hexadecimal characters joined by `-`).

PasswordResetTokenInfo.description: What the holder of a valid reset token needs to choose a new password.

address.description: The mailbox whose password will be reset.

secondFactorRequired.description:
The account has active second factors, so the completion must carry one. When `true` and
`secondFactorMethods` is empty, the account's only entries are deprecated ones and the reset
cannot be completed here (`second-factor-unavailable`).

secondFactorMethods.description: The account's usable second factors in the recommended order (feature 001).

PasswordResetCompletionRequest.description:
Completes a reset. The new password must meet the password policy and must not start with a
hash-scheme prefix. When the account has active second factors, `secondFactor` must prove one of
them: a TOTP code (`methodId` from the token check), a Yubico OTP, or a WebAuthn assertion for
the challenge from `POST /password-resets/webauthn-challenge`. The new password is not kept by
the server between requests: send it again with the second factor.

PasswordResetCompleted.description:
The password was reset. Every reset token of the account stopped working, the forced password
change was cleared, and every session of the account in this API ended. Sign in with the new
password.

PasswordResetSecondFactorRequiredProblem.description:
Problem of type `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-required` (status `401`) answered by
`POST /password-resets/completion` when the account has active second factors and the request
carried none. `methods` lists the usable ones in the recommended order. The token stays valid.

MailboxMailSettingsBulkActionRequest.description:
One mail-settings action applied to several mailboxes, as the legacy mailbox list's TLS mass
actions do. `setTlsEnforcement` sets inbound and/or outbound TLS enforcement (at least one of
the two). Each target is authorised, version-checked (against its mail-settings version tag),
changed and audited on its own, exactly as `updateMailboxMailSettings`; one failure does not stop
the others. A target's `id` is the mailbox address, in any letter case and with the domain in
ASCII or Unicode form; an address given twice is processed and reported once. At most the bulk
limit of targets (`tooMany` on `targets`).

AppPasswordProtocol.description:
A protocol an app password may be used for (`app_passwd.*_access`): `imap`, `pop3`, `smtp`
(authenticated submission), `sieve` (ManageSieve), `activeSync` and `dav` (CalDAV and CardDAV).

AppPassword.description:
An alternative password of a mailbox for selected protocols (mailcow `app_passwd`). It
authenticates only to its own protocols, independently of the mailbox's own protocol access, and
never signs in to the web UI or webmail. Changes apply at the mail server's next authentication.
The password and its hash are never returned.

name.description: Plain text. Legacy stores it HTML-encoded; this API encodes and decodes it.

etag.description: Version tag of the stored values, equal to the `ETag` header of a single read.

name.description: Trimmed; its stored (HTML-encoded) form must fit 255 characters.

password.description:
Omit to let the system generate 32 random characters that meet the password policy, returned
once as `generatedPassword`. A given password must meet the policy and must not start with a
hash-scheme prefix, and is never returned.

protocols.description: Default all six. An empty list is accepted; such an app password works nowhere.

AppPasswordResult.description: An app password, with the password the system generated when it generated one.

generatedPassword.description:
The generated password, shown exactly once, in this response only. `null` when the client
gave the password or did not change it.

AppPasswordPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of an app password. Only the members sent change; the mailbox never changes.
Send `password` to set a password, or `generatePassword: true` to have one generated and returned
once; not both. At least one member is required (`required` on `body`).

TemporaryAlias.description:
A generated address that delivers to the mailbox until it expires, or permanently (mailcow
`spamalias`). Expired aliases are not listed and answer `404`; mail to them is refused, and
mailcow's daily clean-up removes them.

TemporaryAliasCreateRequest.description:
Creates a temporary alias with a random, readable address: two dot-separated parts of 6 to 8
letters alternating consonants and vowels, never equal to an existing address.

domain.description:
The mailbox's domain or one of its alias domains (`GET
/mailboxes/{mailbox}/temporary-alias-domains`), in ASCII or Unicode form. Other domains are
refused (`notInList` with `allowed`).

TemporaryAliasPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a temporary alias: either a new lifetime counted from now, or permanence.
Nothing else can change.

TemporaryAliasDomain.description: A domain in which temporary aliases of the mailbox may be created.

PushNotificationSettings.description:
Pushover notifications of a mailbox (mailcow `pushover`): mailcow sends one for each clean message
delivered to the mailbox or its aliases, optionally only for listed senders. The application token
and the user key are never returned. `title` and `text` may use the placeholders `{SUBJECT}`,
`{SENDER}`, `{SENDER_ADDRESS}`, `{SENDER_NAME}`, `{TO_NAME}`, `{TO_ADDRESS}` and `{MSG_ID}`; an
empty title means `Mail`, an empty text `You've got mail 📧`. Without stored settings,
`configured` is `false` and the other members show the defaults.

senders.description:
Only mail from these addresses notifies (empty: every sender, unless `senderPattern` is set).
Dots in the local part of `@gmail.com` addresses are removed, as legacy stores them.

senderPattern.description: A delimited PCRE pattern (for example `/@example\.org$/i`) matched against the sender, or empty.

evaluatePriority.description: Messages flagged high priority notify with Pushover priority 2.

onlyHighPriority.description: Only messages flagged high priority notify.

PushNotificationSettingsReplacement.description:
Replaces the settings as a whole; members not sent take their defaults, except `token` and
`userKey`, which keep the stored values when omitted and are required while none are stored.

PushNotificationVerification.description: Pushover's verdict on the stored credentials. No notification is sent.

reason.description: Pushover's explanation when it did not accept the credentials.

MailboxMailSettings.description:
How mail of a mailbox is handled. `taggedMailHandling` decides what happens to
`local+tag@domain` (mailcow's shared store). `tlsEnforceInbound` refuses mail delivered to the
mailbox over a connection without TLS; `tlsEnforceOutbound` refuses to send its mail to servers
without TLS. TLS enforcement also covers the mailbox's alias-domain addresses and aliases whose
only target is the mailbox; mail that cannot meet it is bounced.

etag.description: Version tag over these three settings only.

RecentLogin.description:
The latest login of one group of a mailbox's logins, grouped by client address, service and app
password, as legacy groups them (mailcow `sasl_log`).

service.description:
The service as stored, upper-cased. The known values are `IMAP`, `POP3`, `SMTP`, `SIEVE`
(Dovecot's service names), `SOGO` (the groupware's own sign-ins, including ActiveSync and DAV),
`SSO` (webmail single sign-on), `EAS`, `DAV` and `WEBUI`. Web UI sign-ins are always `WEBUI`,
whether mailcow stored `MAILCOWUI` (upstream) or `WEBUI` (FeldHost fork). Other mailcow
versions may store other services, which are returned as they are (upper-cased), so clients
show unknown values as given (G24).

internal.description: A private, reserved or internal address (web UI, ActiveSync and internal services); never has a country.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of a public address, when known in time.

name.description: `null` when the app password was deleted since.

SieveFilterKind.description:
`prefilter` runs before the user's own Sieve rules, `postfilter` after them (`sieve_filters.filter_type`).
At most one filter of each kind is active per mailbox.

SieveFilter.description: A Sieve filter that an administrator keeps for a mailbox (mailcow `sieve_filters`).

active.description: Activating a filter deactivates the mailbox's other active filter of the same kind.

SieveFilterCreateRequest.description:
A new filter for the mailbox of the path. The script must pass the Sieve validation legacy mailcow
applies (`sieveSyntax` with the parser's `message`) and fit 65,535 bytes.

SieveFilterPatch.description:
JSON Merge Patch of a filter. Only the members sent change, with the rules of creation; the
mailbox never changes. Changing the kind of an active filter deactivates the mailbox's active
filter of the new kind. At least one member is required.

ActiveSieveScript.description:
The Sieve script the user manages in webmail and that the mail server runs for the mailbox, as
the mail server reports it. `name` and `script` are `null` when no script is active.

message.description: The parser's message when the script is invalid (English, as the parser writes it).

IdentityProviderCapabilities.description:
What a client needs before it shows or submits the identity provider forms, as configured on this
server. Available whether or not a configuration is stored. Contains no secret and no connection
detail of a stored configuration.

configured.description: Whether a configuration is stored (`GET /identity-provider` answers `404` otherwise).

configuredType.description: Type of the stored configuration, `null` when none is stored.

appReturnUrls.description:
The new web app's sign-in return addresses, one per host name of the server
(`MAILCOW_HOSTNAME` first, then `ADDITIONAL_SERVER_NAMES`). Register them at a Keycloak or
generic OIDC provider before or after the first save.

types.description: The provider types and what each offers.

passwordSignIn.description: Password sign-in of its mailboxes (Keycloak only with the mailpassword flow).

defaults.description: Values a whole save uses for omitted settings (legacy defaults).

limits.description: Field limits of a save, a change and a connection test.

providerTimeoutSeconds.description: Time-out of each call to the provider (7 by default).

pendingLifetimeSeconds.description: Lifetime of a started single sign-on (600 by default).

renewalIntervalSeconds.description: Interval after which a single sign-on session is renewed with the provider (300 by default).

Oauth2ClientCapabilities.description:
What a client needs to manage OAuth2 clients and to inform application developers, as configured
on this server. Contains no secret.

endpoints.description: Paths of the unchanged legacy OAuth2 endpoints on the server's host names.

scope.description: The only scope, also used when an application omits the scope parameter.

grantTypes.description:
Grant types the legacy token endpoint accepts. The legacy information text documents the
authorization code grant with refresh tokens; the endpoint also accepts the password grant for
mailbox users.

accessTokenLifetimeSeconds.description: Lifetime of access tokens (mailcow's `ACCESS_TOKEN_LIFETIME`, 86400 by default).

refreshTokenLifetimeSeconds.description: Lifetime of refresh tokens (mailcow's `REFRESH_TOKEN_LIFETIME`, 2678400 by default).

redirectUrisMaxLength.description: Maximum length of the redirect URIs joined by single spaces (2,000).

bulkLimit.description: Maximum number of clients in one bulk action (100).

Unauthorized.description:
The caller is not authenticated. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/unauthenticated`: no session and no API key, or the session ended (idle
  timeout, sign-out, changed user agent, account deactivated or deleted).
- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-required`: the session's sign-in still awaits a second factor.
- `/api/v2/problems/api-key-invalid`: the key matches no key, or its owner is inactive or deleted.
- `/api/v2/problems/api-key-expired`, `/api/v2/problems/api-key-revoked`.
- `/api/v2/problems/identity-provider-session-ended`: a single sign-on session ended because the
  provider refused or could not renew it, the provider returned another e-mail address, the
  identity provider configuration changed, or the mailbox no longer authenticates against it
  (feature 012). The session is gone; offer single sign-on again.

Forbidden.description:
The caller is authenticated but may not perform this request. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/forbidden`: the caller's role or permission flags do not allow it.
- `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch`: a session request without a valid `X-CSRF-Token`.
- `/api/v2/problems/session-required`: the operation is not available to API keys.
- `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required`: the session is restricted (extension `pendingActions`).
- `/api/v2/problems/insufficient-key-scope`: a read-only key used for a state-changing request.
- `/api/v2/problems/api-key-source-not-allowed`: the key is used from an address outside its
  allowed networks.
- `/api/v2/problems/impersonation-ended` (feature 007, any session request except ending the
  impersonation and signing out): the session's impersonation became invalid and ended; the
  request was not carried out, and the session acts as the impersonator again.
- `/api/v2/problems/not-allowed-while-impersonating` (feature 007): a sign-in credential
  operation or a webmail sign-in during an impersonation.

SignInRejected.description:
The sign-in step failed. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/sign-in-failed`: one generic error for an unknown account, a wrong password,
  an inactive account or domain, a resource mailbox, a malformed username, a mailbox that
  authenticates against an external identity provider, and an unknown, inactive or
  wrong-role passkey. It never reveals which.
- `/api/v2/problems/sign-in-expired`: there is no pending sign-in or challenge in this session,
  or it expired or was already used. Start again.
- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-failed`: the second factor was wrong or no longer exists. The
  pending sign-in is cancelled; start again with the password.
- The API key types of `Unauthorized` when the request carries an invalid `X-API-Key`.

SignInForbidden.description:
The sign-in request is refused. Possible types:
- `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch`: missing or wrong `X-CSRF-Token`. Call
  `GET /csrf-token` first.
- `/api/v2/problems/session-required`: the request carries an API key; sign-in is for browser
  sessions only.
- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-unavailable`: the password is correct, but the account's only
  active second factors are deprecated U2F or HOTP entries. An administrator must reset them.
- `/api/v2/problems/insufficient-key-scope` and `/api/v2/problems/api-key-source-not-allowed`:
  the request carries a read-only API key, or a key used from a disallowed address.

- `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required`: the caller's role may use the operation, but only
  with a permission flag it lacks (extension `requiredFlags`, for example `["quarantine"]`,
  `["quarantineAttachments"]`, `["spamScore"]`, `["spamPolicy"]` or `["ratelimit"]`). Nothing
  changed.
- `/api/v2/problems/attribute-not-permitted`: a mailbox user would change a notification setting
  whose flag they lack (extensions `attributes` and `requiredFlags`). Nothing changed.
- `/api/v2/problems/insufficient-key-scope`: a read-only key used for a state-changing request.
- `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch`, `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required`,
  `/api/v2/problems/api-key-source-not-allowed`: see `Forbidden`.

Role and flags are checked before the object is looked up, so a refusal never reveals whether an
object exists.

  administrator reading the audit log).
- `/api/v2/problems/permission-flag-required`: the change needs a permission flag the caller

  it.
- `/api/v2/problems/current-password-incorrect`: the current password is wrong. Audited; repeated

- `/api/v2/problems/password-managed-externally`: the mailbox's password lives in an external
  identity provider (LDAP, Keycloak, generic OIDC), so its password, recovery address and second
  factors are not managed here.
- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-required-by-policy`: the account must keep a second factor
  (legacy `force_tfa`).
- `/api/v2/problems/groupware-disabled`: the server runs without the groupware.
- `/api/v2/problems/session-required`: the operation is not available to API keys.
- `/api/v2/problems/pending-action-required`: the session is restricted (extension
  `pendingActions`).
- `/api/v2/problems/insufficient-key-scope`, `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch`,
  `/api/v2/problems/api-key-source-not-allowed`: see `Forbidden`.

- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-unavailable`: the account's only second factors are deprecated

- `/api/v2/problems/csrf-token-mismatch`: call `GET /csrf-token` first.
- `/api/v2/problems/session-required`: the request carries an API key; password reset is for
  browser sessions only.
- `/api/v2/problems/insufficient-key-scope`, `/api/v2/problems/api-key-source-not-allowed`: see

- `/api/v2/problems/second-factor-failed`: the second factor was wrong, a TOTP code was already
  used, or the WebAuthn challenge was missing or expired. The token stays valid; the failure counts
  towards the sign-in throttling of the account and client address.
- The API key types of `Unauthorized` when the request carries an invalid `X-API-Key`.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description:
`ETag` from a previous read, or `*`. When it does not match the current representation, the
request fails with `412` and nothing changes.

Order.name: order
Order.description: Sort direction. Each list documents its default.

Search.name: q
Search.description:
Case-insensitive substring search over the list's documented search fields. Leading and trailing
whitespace is ignored; an empty value means no search.

PasskeyId.name: passkeyId
PasskeyId.description: `id` of one of the caller's passkeys. Other accounts' passkeys answer `404`.

ProblemTypeName.name: problemType
ProblemTypeName.description: Last path segment of a documented problem type URI.

SyncJobSort.name: sort
SyncJobSort.description:
Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id` in the same direction.
In ascending order, jobs that never ran (`lastRunAt` empty) come first for `lastRunAt`, and
`lastResult` sorts `unknown`, then `failed`, then `succeeded`.

SyncJobId.name: syncJobId
SyncJobId.description:
`id` of a sync job (mailcow's `imapsync.id`). A job whose target mailbox lies outside the
caller's scope answers `404`, exactly like a job that does not exist.

DomainSort.name: sort
DomainSort.description:
Sort field. Default `name` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by name. `mailboxes`, `aliases`,
`quotaAllocated` and `storageUsed` sort by the usage figures.

DomainName.name: domain
DomainName.description:
Name of a domain, in ASCII or Unicode form and any letter case (it is trimmed, lower-cased and
converted to ASCII with UTS #46). A name that does not exist, that lies outside the caller's
scope, or that belongs to an alias domain answers `404`.

DomainTagSort.name: sort
DomainTagSort.description: Sort field. Default `name` (alphabetical, ignoring letter case) with `order=asc`.

DomainTemplateId.name: templateId
DomainTemplateId.description: ID of a domain template. IDs of mailbox templates, and unknown IDs, answer `404`.

AliasSort.name: sort
AliasSort.description:
Sort field. Default `id` with `order=desc`, which lists the newest aliases first, as the legacy
screen does. Ties are broken by `id`.

AliasId.name: aliasId
AliasId.description:
Identifier of the alias (mailcow's `alias.id`). It never changes, also when the address changes.
Find an alias by address with the `address` filter of `listAliases`.

AliasDomainSort.name: sort
AliasDomainSort.description: Sort field. Default `name` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `name`.

AliasDomainName.name: aliasDomain
AliasDomainName.description:
Name of the alias domain, in ASCII (punycode) or Unicode form and in any letter case. It is
trimmed, lower-cased and converted to ASCII with the UTS #46 rules before the lookup.

ResourceSort.name: sort
ResourceSort.description:
Sort field. Default `address` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `address`. `bookingRule` sorts
by mailcow's stored value; ascending that is unlimited (-1), always free (0), then limited by the
number of concurrent bookings.

ResourceAddress.name: resourceAddress
ResourceAddress.description:
Address of the resource, for example `MeetingRoom1@example.org`, in any letter case and with the
domain in ASCII or Unicode form (percent-encode non-ASCII characters; `@` may stay literal). A
mailbox address answers `404`.

SenderSettingsMailbox.name: mailbox
SenderSettingsMailbox.description:
Full address of the mailbox, in any letter case and with the domain in ASCII or Unicode form
(percent-encode non-ASCII characters; `@` may stay literal). A mailbox outside the caller's
scope, a resource and an address of anything other than a mailbox all answer `404`.

MailboxSenderPermissionCandidateSort.name: sort
MailboxSenderPermissionCandidateSort.description:
Sort field. Default `type` with `order=asc`: "any address" first, then domains, then addresses,
each group ordered by `value`. Ties are broken by `value`.

MailboxSort.name: sort
MailboxSort.description:
Sort field. Default `address` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by address. Mailboxes without a
value for the field (an unlimited quota for `percentUsed`, no login, no recorded password change,
never modified) come after all others in both directions. `lastMailLogin` is the most recent IMAP,
POP3 or SMTP login.

MailboxTagSort.name: sort
MailboxTagSort.description: Sort field. Default `name` with `order=asc`, alphabetical without regard to letter case.

MailboxAddress.name: mailbox
MailboxAddress.description:
Full address of the mailbox, in any letter case and with the domain in ASCII or Unicode form
(percent-encode non-ASCII characters; `@` may stay literal). A mailbox outside the caller's
scope, a resource and an unknown address all answer `404`.

MailboxTemplateSort.name: sort
MailboxTemplateSort.description: Sort field. Default `name` with `order=asc`. Names are compared without regard to letter case; ties are broken by identifier.

DkimKeySort.name: sort
DkimKeySort.description:
Sort field. Default `name` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `name`. Entries without a key sort
after the others for `selector` and `keyLength` in ascending order.

DkimName.name: dkimName
DkimName.description:
Name of a domain, an alias domain or an unused key, percent-encoded. It is accepted in ASCII
(punycode) or Unicode form and in any letter case, and it is trimmed, lower-cased and converted to
ASCII with the UTS #46 rules before the lookup. For administrators, an unused key that legacy stored
under a name that is not in this form is also found by its exact stored name, which is compared
first. A name outside the caller's scope answers `404`, exactly like a name that does not exist.

MtaStsPolicySort.name: sort
MtaStsPolicySort.description: Sort field. Default `domain` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `domain`.

MtaStsPolicyDomain.name: policyDomain
MtaStsPolicyDomain.description:
Domain of the policy, percent-encoded, in ASCII (punycode) or Unicode form and in any letter case.
It is trimmed, lower-cased and converted to ASCII with the UTS #46 rules. Policies belong to
domains: an alias domain's name answers `404`, because an alias domain publishes its target
domain's policy. A domain outside the caller's scope answers `404` too.

DnsDiagnosticsName.name: diagnosticsName
DnsDiagnosticsName.description:
Domain or alias domain to check, percent-encoded, in ASCII (punycode) or Unicode form and in any
letter case. It is trimmed, lower-cased and converted to ASCII with the UTS #46 rules. A name that
is not a domain or alias domain in the caller's scope answers `404`.

IdentityProviderIfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IdentityProviderIfNoneMatch.description:
`*` makes the save create-only: it fails with `412` when a configuration is stored, so that two
administrators setting up the provider at the same time cannot overwrite each other. A listed
version tag fails with `412` when it is the stored configuration's tag. Nothing changes on `412`.

Oauth2ClientSort.name: sort
Oauth2ClientSort.description: Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. `redirectUri` sorts by the stored redirect URIs, so by the first one.

Oauth2ClientId.name: oauth2ClientId
Oauth2ClientId.description: Numeric identifier of the OAuth2 client.

AdminSort.name: sort
AdminSort.description:
Sort field. Default `username` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by username, ascending.
Accounts that were never modified sort first for `modifiedAt` ascending.

AdminUsername.name: username
AdminUsername.description:
Username of the administrator, in any letter case. A domain administrator's username answers
`404`, exactly like a username that does not exist.

DomainAdminSort.name: sort
DomainAdminSort.description:
Sort field. Default `username` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by username, ascending.
`domainCount` is the number of assignments. Accounts that were never modified sort first for
`modifiedAt` ascending.

DomainAdminUsername.name: username
DomainAdminUsername.description:
Username of the domain administrator, in any letter case. An administrator's username answers
`404`, exactly like a username that does not exist.

ContainerSort.name: sort
ContainerSort.description: Sort field. Default `name` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by name.

ContainerName.name: containerName
ContainerName.description: Compose service name of the container, for example `postfix-mailcow`.

LogSort.name: sort
LogSort.description:
Sort field. Logs are sorted by time only, newest first by default (`order=desc`) or oldest first
(`order=asc`). Entries with the same time keep the order in which mailcow stored them.

LogFrom.name: from
LogFrom.description: Only entries at or after this time (inclusive).

LogTo.name: to
LogTo.description: Only entries at or before this time (inclusive).

LogBefore.name: before
LogBefore.description:
Only entries older than the entry with this `id`, in the list's time order. To load older
entries while new ones arrive, pass the `id` of the oldest entry the client holds and keep
`offset` at 0: the next page then has no duplicates, whatever arrived meanwhile. When that entry
was trimmed by mailcow's retention, nothing older is retained and the page is empty. A malformed
cursor is refused (`invalidFormat`, `format: logCursor`).

`before` always selects the entries older than the cursor's entry, whatever `order` says; `order`
then sorts that selection, so with `order=asc` the page starts at the oldest retained entry.
Clients that page backwards keep the default `order=desc`. With `before`, `meta.total` counts the
matching entries older than the cursor (the remaining ones), not the whole log.

LogSeverityFilter.name: severity
LogSeverityFilter.description: Only entries of these severity classes. Repeat the parameter for several.

RspamdHistorySort.name: sort
RspamdHistorySort.description: Sort field. Default `time` with `order=desc`. Ties keep Rspamd's order (newest first).

MailQueueMessageSort.name: sort
MailQueueMessageSort.description: Sort field. Default `arrivalTime` with `order=asc` (oldest first). Ties are broken by queue ID.

Fail2BanActiveBanSort.name: sort
Fail2BanActiveBanSort.description: Sort field. Default `endsAt` with `order=asc` (soonest ending first). `network` sorts by address, then prefix length. Ties are broken by network.

Fail2BanNetwork.name: network
Fail2BanNetwork.description:
The banned network in prefix notation, exactly as listed in `Fail2BanActiveBan.network`, with
the `/` percent-encoded: `203.0.113.0%2F24`, `2001%3Adb8%3A%3A%2F64`.

Fail2BanPermanentBanSort.name: sort
Fail2BanPermanentBanSort.description: Sort field. Default `startedAt` with `order=desc` (newest first). `network` sorts by address, then prefix length. Ties are broken by network.

RelayhostSort.name: sort
RelayhostSort.description: Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id`.

RelayhostChoiceSort.name: sort
RelayhostChoiceSort.description: Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id`.

RelayhostUsageSort.name: sort
RelayhostUsageSort.description:
Sort field. `kind` (default) lists domains before mailboxes, each by name; `name` sorts by name
only. Default `order=asc`.

TransportSort.name: sort
TransportSort.description: Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id`.

BccMapSort.name: sort
BccMapSort.description: Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id`.

BccDestinationChoiceSort.name: sort
BccDestinationChoiceSort.description:
Sort field. `kind` (default) orders by kind (domains, alias domains, mailboxes, aliases,
alias-domain addresses), then by value; `value` sorts by value only. Default `order=asc`.

BccMapId.name: bccMapId
BccMapId.description: Identifier of the BCC map (mailcow's numeric `id`).

RecipientMapSort.name: sort
RecipientMapSort.description: Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id`.

RecipientMapId.name: recipientMapId
RecipientMapId.description: Identifier of the recipient map (mailcow's numeric `id`).

TlsPolicyMapSort.name: sort
TlsPolicyMapSort.description: Sort field. Default `id` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id`.

TlsPolicyMapId.name: tlsPolicyMapId
TlsPolicyMapId.description: Identifier of the TLS policy map (mailcow's numeric `id`).

ForwardingHostSort.name: sort
ForwardingHostSort.description:
Sort field. Default `address` with `order=asc`: IPv4 before IPv6, numerically, then by prefix
length. Ties are broken by address.

ForwardingHostAddress.name: forwardingHostAddress
ForwardingHostAddress.description:
Stored address or prefix of the forwarding host, exactly as listed, percent-encoded: `/` becomes
`%2F` and `:` may be sent as `%3A` (for example `192.0.2.0%2F24` or `2001%3Adb8%3A%3A1`).

QuarantineItemSort.name: sort
QuarantineItemSort.description:
Sort field. Default `arrivedAt` with `order=desc` (newest first). Ties are always broken by `id`,
newest first. Items without a score sort before every scored item in ascending order.

QuarantineValidateOnly.name: validateOnly
QuarantineValidateOnly.description:
`true` checks the request by every rule of the change, including `If-Match` and the notification
template check, without storing or auditing anything (feature 013's pattern). A valid request then
answers `200` with `{"data": {"valid": true}}` and no `ETag`; an invalid one answers exactly as a
real change would.

QuarantineItemId.name: itemId
QuarantineItemId.description:
`id` of a quarantine item (mailcow's `quarantine.id`). An item outside the caller's scope answers
`404`, exactly like an item that does not exist.

QuarantineAttachmentPosition.name: position
QuarantineAttachmentPosition.description:
`position` of an attachment as listed in the item's parsed content (`content.attachments`),
starting at 0. An unknown position answers `404`.

PolicyTargetMailbox.name: mailbox
PolicyTargetMailbox.description:
Username (address) of a mailbox (mailcow's `mailbox.username`), matched after trimming and
lower-casing. Resources (location, thing and group kinds) are not mailboxes here and answer
`404`, as does a mailbox outside the caller's scope. A mailbox user reaches only their own
mailbox.

PolicyTargetDomain.name: domain
PolicyTargetDomain.description:
Name of a domain (mailcow's `domain.domain`). It is matched after trimming, lower-casing and
conversion to its ASCII (IDNA) form. A domain outside the caller's scope answers `404`, and so
does an alias domain (use `/alias-domains/{aliasDomain}`).

SpamPolicyEntrySort.name: sort
SpamPolicyEntrySort.description: Sort field. Default `pattern` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `id`, ascending.

SpamPolicyEntryId.name: entryId
SpamPolicyEntryId.description:
`id` of an allow or block list entry (mailcow's `filterconf.prefid`). The entry must belong to
the owner named in the path: an entry of another owner, such as a domain entry addressed through
one of its mailboxes, answers `404`.

PolicyTargetAliasDomain.name: aliasDomain
PolicyTargetAliasDomain.description:
Name of an alias domain (mailcow's `alias_domain.alias_domain`), matched like a domain name. A
domain administrator reaches the alias domains whose target domain they manage. Others answer
`404`.

RateLimitSort.name: sort
RateLimitSort.description: Sort field. Default `object` with `order=asc`. Ties are broken by `object`, ascending.

RateLimitBucketId.name: bucketId
RateLimitBucketId.description:
Identifier of a rate-limit bucket as it appears in the rate-limited log (feature 011): `RL`
followed by letters, digits and `=`. Matched case-sensitively against the spam filter's bucket
key and the log entries' bucket identifier.

SettingsValidateOnly.name: validateOnly
SettingsValidateOnly.description:
`true` checks the request by every validation rule of the operation without storing, restarting
or auditing anything. A valid request then answers `200` with `{"data": {"valid": true}}`; an
invalid one answers `422` exactly as a real request would. Version tags (`If-Match`) are checked
too.

RspamdSettingsRuleId.name: ruleId
RspamdSettingsRuleId.description: Identifier of an Rspamd settings rule. An unknown identifier answers `404`.

RspamdRegexMapSort.name: sort
RspamdRegexMapSort.description: Sort field. Default `name` with `order=asc`. Without `sort`, the maps keep the operator's configured order.

RspamdRegexMapId.name: mapId
RspamdRegexMapId.description:
File name of an editable global regex map, as listed by `GET /settings/rspamd-regex-maps`. Any
other name answers `404`.

GlobalSieveFilterId.name: filterId
GlobalSieveFilterId.description: `prefilter` (runs before the mailboxes' own filters) or `postfilter` (runs after them).

PresetKind.name: presetKind
PresetKind.description:
`rspamd` (examples of Rspamd settings rules, administrators only) or `sieve` (example Sieve
scripts, administrators and domain administrators).

MassMailJobId.name: jobId
MassMailJobId.description: Identifier of a mass mail job. An unknown identifier answers `404`.

OwnSecondFactorId.name: secondFactorId
OwnSecondFactorId.description: Identifier of one of the signed-in account's second factors (mailcow `tfa.id`).

AppleProfileVariant.name: variant
AppleProfileVariant.description:
`email`: the IMAP account with its SMTP server only (legacy `?only_email`). `emailAndDav`
(default): also a CalDAV and a CardDAV account, refused with `groupware-disabled` when the
groupware is disabled.

AppPasswordSort.name: sort
AppPasswordSort.description: Sort field. Default `name` (ascending unless `order` says otherwise).

AppPasswordId.name: appPasswordId
AppPasswordId.description: Identifier of the app password (mailcow `app_passwd.id`). An app password of another mailbox answers `404`.

TemporaryAliasSort.name: sort
TemporaryAliasSort.description:
Sort field. Default `createdAt`; with the default sort the default order is `desc` (newest
first). Permanent aliases sort after every expiring one for `expiresAt`.

TemporaryAliasAddress.name: temporaryAlias
TemporaryAliasAddress.description:
Address of the temporary alias, in any letter case (percent-encode non-ASCII characters; `@` may
stay literal). An expired temporary alias, or one of another mailbox, answers `404`.

RecentLoginDays.name: days
RecentLoginDays.description: Period in days, counted back from now, as legacy counts it (whole hours). `outOfRange` outside 1 to 31.

RecentLoginSort.name: sort
RecentLoginSort.description: Sort field. Default `lastSeenAt`; with the default sort the default order is `desc` (newest first).

SieveFilterSort.name: sort
SieveFilterSort.description: Sort field. Default `mailbox`, then `description` as the second key.

SieveFilterId.name: sieveFilterId
SieveFilterId.description: Identifier of the Sieve filter (mailcow `sieve_filters.id`). A filter of another mailbox answers `404`.
